For the negative half the lattice-component argument is proved directly by the same finite tail calculation as the module string lemma: if u=sum_n F_i^(n)v_n, set T_n=e-tilde_i^n u; then v_n=T_n-f-tilde_i T_(n+1) lies in the lattice. Induction on the largest position, using the residue partial inverse, shows that a basis residue has exactly one nonzero component and that its top residue is positive. Root height makes the tails finite. This proves the half version without applying an integrable-module-only Statement to U^-. Conjugating this argument through the signed lattice theorem gives the asserted signed right version, without assuming unsigned star. The integer c_i(b) is epsilon_i of the absolute value of star b.

The field right ideal U^- F_i^t is the direct sum of right-string positions n>=t. Its adapted global subset is therefore precisely the positive indices b with c_i(b)>=t: conjugate the already proved left-string adapted global subset through star, whose possible signs do not affect which A-basis vectors span the ideal. The based quotient's field kernel is the sum of these right ideals at t=lambda_i+1. Since all are adapted to ONE global basis, their sum is the span of the union of their basis subsets. Therefore

    pi_lambda(b)!=0 iff c_i(b)<=lambda_i for every i.    (A)

This proves the highest-weight survivor criterion already with signed star. It neither assumes unsigned star nor infers an adapted intersection from an arbitrary linear sum. The surviving residues are bijective with B(lambda) by the existing based quotient/grand loop. Raising cannot turn a survivor into a killed nonzero residue: if e_i b were killed, the ALL-residue lowering identity pi_lambda(f_i(e_i b))=f_i pi_lambda(e_i b)=0 and the negative-half partial inverse f_i e_i b=b would force b killed, a contradiction. Thus every nonzero raising iterate of a survivor survives. Combining this with the surviving-residue raising identity proves equality of the entire raising lengths, epsilon_i(pi_lambda b)=epsilon_i(b), including the zero endpoint. This supplies the precise statistic identification used later in the finite-model construction without circularly using elementary embeddings. Raising on survivors and surviving lowering are exactly these existing projection compatibilities. The shifted statistics are epsilon_i(b) and epsilon_i(b)+<h_i,lambda+wt(b)> because B(lambda) is the actual highest-weight module crystal; raising preservation gives epsilon equality, and its rank-one formula gives phi.

## Canonical elementary embedding by finite highest-weight tensor models

Fix color i and a finite set of lowering words of height at most H. Work in the regularized finite support. Choose lambda_i=0 and lambda_j large for j!=i, large enough that no right ideal for those j meets any relevant root component of height at most H+1. Choose N>H+1. The total label lambda+N Lambda_i is then large at every relevant color, so its projection identifies the canonical B(infinity) vertices and all edges under consideration with the corresponding finite-degree vertices of B(lambda+N Lambda_i). Apply the strict highest-weight tensor embedding into B(lambda) tensor B(N Lambda_i).

Throughout these finite lowering paths the second factor is a pure i-string f_i^m u_(N Lambda_i). Indeed initially it is highest. For j!=i its epsilon_j is0 at every pure i-string position: E_j commutes with F_i and kills the highest vector, so all such vectors are E_j-highest. The first factor's phi_j is positive and larger than any second epsilon_j in the bounded degree, because lambda_j is chosen large. Thus both lowering and raising of any j!=i act on the first factor. Color i preserves the pure i-string form. Its string endpoint N is not reached in this height bound.

Lift the first residue b_1 uniquely to its surviving positive residue b' in B(infinity). Replace the second pure i-position m by b_i(-m) in the elementary crystal. The finite tensor rules become exactly those on B(infinity) tensor B_i: for i, lambda_i=0 means the first phi_i is epsilon_i(b')+<h_i,wt(b')>, and the second epsilon_i is m. For j!=i the elementary statistics are -infinity, so its tensor rule selects the first factor, just as the large-lambda finite model does. The finite tensor epsilon formula reduces to epsilon_j(b') for j!=i because lambda_j is large; for i it reduces to max(epsilon_i(b'),m-<h_i,wt(b')>). Root weights add to wt(b')-m alpha_i. Thus the replacement preserves the generic weight, epsilon and formal phi statistics as well as every considered operator.

This construction is independent of lambda,N WITHOUT assuming a stabilization theorem. Define its candidate value on a lowering word w by computing w(u_infinity tensor b_i(0)) using the actual generic tensor rules. The preceding finite-model argument shows that this computation agrees with the replacement of the finite tensor image for every bounded path. If two words w,w' give the same b in B(infinity), choose one common finite bound and one common pair lambda,N. Their images in B(lambda+N Lambda_i) coincide, hence their strict tensor images coincide, and the unique surviving lifts of their first factors coincide. Therefore the candidate generic tensor values coincide. Conversely if the candidate values coincide, choose the same finite model for the two words; its first-factor projections and second positions coincide, and injectivity of Phi followed by the large-label projection identification gives w u_infinity=w' u_infinity. This proves a well-defined injective Psi_i, independent of all choices.

For lowering use the same finite model on a word and that word with one appended operator. For raising use a model containing the vertex, its raising neighbor if nonzero, and the next boundary; strictness of finite Phi and the already checked branch/statistic formulas give Psi_i(e_j b)=e_j Psi_i(b), including zero. Hence

    Psi_i:B(infinity)->B(infinity) tensor B_i

is strict, sends the vacuum to u_infinity tensor b_i(0), and every elementary coordinate is nonpositive. This is an actual finite-word construction, rather than a citation to Kashiwara Theorem8.2.

## Identifying the elementary coordinate with the right-string index

The remaining coordinate identification can be checked on the coproduct rather than assumed from unsigned star. For a homogeneous P of root beta, the coefficient of one i in the second tensor factor of Delta(P), after extracting its toral K_i, is e_i''(P). On homogeneous root beta this derivative is

    e_i''(P)=q_i^(<h_i,beta>-2) (star e_i' star)(P).

Check this first on a generator. Both sides then satisfy the same twisted deletion rule, with prefix versus suffix twists interchanged; the displayed homogeneous scalar converts one rule into the other. Hence their kernels agree. Coassociativity or repeated deletion shows that every higher pure-second-i coefficient is a nonzero field scalar multiple of the corresponding repeated derivative; it therefore vanishes on P in the right-string kernel. Thus projecting Delta(P) onto the terms with pure i root degree in the second factor leaves exactly P tensor1.

Apply this to the right expansion u=sum_n u_n F_i^(n) above, acting on v_lambda tensor v_(N Lambda_i) with lambda_i=0. Every mixed-color second-factor term has a different second root degree and is removed by the pure-i projection. For u_n in the right kernel only u_n tensor1 survives that projection. In Delta F_i^(n), every term whose first divided power F_i^(a) has a>0 kills v_lambda before u_n acts. The remaining term is K_i^n tensor F_i^(n), and K_i^n v_lambda=v_lambda because lambda_i=0. Therefore the exact pure-second-i projection is

    sum_n pi_lambda(u_n) tensor F_i^(n)v_(N Lambda_i).   (B)

No uncontrolled q shift occurs in this formula with the actual native coproduct. The derivative equality above is only used to identify the kernel; scalar rescalings do not change it.

The coefficient u_c, c=c_i(b), has signed positive crystal residue ±bar b with right index0. Its projection at lambda_i=0 survives by (A); all other coordinates survive because lambda_j is large. Thus its projected residue is nonzero. Every n!=c coefficient has zero crystal residue. Formula (B) consequently has exactly one nonzero pure-i tensor residue, at position c. On the other hand Phi(pi_(lambda+N Lambda_i)b) is a positive pure-i tensor residue by the finite model. It follows that its elementary coordinate m is exactly c_i(b), and that the top right-string coefficient u_c has POSITIVE residue bar b, not negative. Thus

    Psi_i(b)=bar b tensor b_i(-c_i(b)),
    c_i(bar b)=0,  b=(f_i^right)^(c_i(b)) bar b.          (C)

In particular every nonvacuum b has positive extraction at some i: star b is a signed nonvacuum crystal residue, and the canonical lowering-generated crystal has a nonzero raising direction on its absolute value.

## Unsigned star follows rather than being assumed

Induct on root height. The vacuum is fixed by star. For a positive-height b choose i with c_i(b)>0. Formula (C) gives b=(f_i^right)^c bar b with bar b a POSITIVE residue of strictly smaller height. Apply star:

    star b=f_i^c(star bar b).

By induction star bar b is positive, and canonical lowering preserves positive crystal residues. Therefore star b is positive. Since star is an involution, it permutes B(infinity) bijectively without signs. This proves unsigned star for every real symmetrizable datum from the actual signed theorem plus tensor positivity. Then c_i(b)=epsilon_i(star b) is the usual epsilon_i^star, and (C) is the exact canonical elementary extraction formula. The proof does not invoke a symmetric-type geometric basis.

## Identification of the generic and cyclotomic module crystals

the preceding local one-step and jump/embedding lemmas construct the generic module strict elementary embeddings, with extraction coordinate epsilon_i^L and positive extraction on every nonvacuum module. Both its graph and the canonical graph just constructed are generated by lowering words from their vacua and have every lowering operator nonzero. The finite-extraction comparison lemma proved next identifies the two graphs uniquely by lowering words. Strictness also forces their elementary extraction coordinates to agree: the comparison tensor identity holds on the vacuum and on every lowering word, so

    epsilon_i^L(M)=epsilon_i^star(b_M).

The local one-step lemma's first-dot criterion identifies the cyclotomic module vertices with epsilon_i^star(b_M)<=lambda_i. Equation (A) identifies exactly that subset with the surviving canonical vertices, hence with B(lambda). Existing projection compatibility proves the raising and surviving-lowering correspondence, while The local jump lemma's actual normal-length formula gives the canonical epsilon/phi data. This proves the full all-field/general homogeneous-Q simple crystal theorem, using exactly the stated local quantum and algebra suppliers. Projective vertices are labeled by the indecomposable projective COVER P(M) of each simple M. The cover–simple Hom pairing transports this graph: E/F crystal labels on covers mean P(e-tilde M), P(f-tilde M), with zero when the simple label is zero. This does not identify P(M) with an arbitrary # dual of M. Independently defined projective Kashiwara operators still require their exact leading-term convention.

## Finite-extraction comparison proof

There is a smaller recognition contract for this application, whose proof is elementary. Suppose C and D are crystals, each generated from its unique weight-zero vertex by lowering words, every f_i is everywhere nonzero, and each has strict elementary embeddings Psi_i with nonpositive elementary coordinates and a positive coordinate for some i on every nonvacuum vertex. Assume the weight support of a vertex is finite and extraction subtracts a nonnegative multiple of alpha_i from its root weight. Then there is a unique crystal isomorphism C=D carrying the two vacua to each other.

Proof. Fix a finite color set containing the support of a lowering word. Cycle through these colors, applying Psi_i to the current first factor, and leave every elementary tensor factor already extracted in place. Tensoring a strict embedding with identity maps is strict: for each color the tensor max formulas preserve epsilon/phi and weight, hence preserve the branch inequality including equality. Therefore every finite composite is strict and injective. Each extraction lowers the nonnegative height of the first factor by its elementary coordinate c. If an entire cycle makes no extraction from a nonvacuum factor, that factor is unchanged throughout the cycle, yet its support has a color with positive extraction, contradiction. Thus after at most the starting height many cycles (and one harmless final cycle) the first factor is the vacuum. Extraction of absent colors is zero: a nonzero alpha_i extraction would give a residual root weight with negative alpha_i coefficient, forbidden. Consequently this finite procedure works in both crystals using the same finite color cycle.

For a word w of length h, use h+1 cycles. Every prefix has height at most h, so both images of every prefix have vacuum first factor. Strictness computes the image of w by applying that same lowering word to the same tensor of a vacuum and elementary zero vertices. While the underlying vacua belong to different crystals, their weights and epsilon/phi are identical and their raising operators vanish; at each intermediate prefix the first factor is still the vacuum, so a nonzero lowering operation cannot take place in that first factor. All operations occur in the identical elementary factors, and the resulting elementary coordinates are identical. If two words w,w' produce the same vertex in C, use a common finite color set and enough cycles for both lengths; their identical C images give identical coordinate tensors, hence identical D images and, by injectivity, identical D vertices. Interchanging C and D gives the converse. Mapping a lowering word in C to that word in D is therefore a well-defined bijection. It preserves lowering by construction, raising by partial inverses, weights by word content, and epsilon/phi because the common strict finite tensor embeddings preserve these statistics. Uniqueness follows from lowering generation. This proves the lemma.

item.title: Crystal lattice polarizations are perfect at q=0
item.statement: For the highest-module and negative-half Kashiwara lattices, their respective normalized polarizations take values in A0 and their crystal residue bases are orthonormal. On every finite label/root component the Gram determinant is a unit, the A0 pairing is perfect and L^vee=L. Moreover L={x:B(x,x)∈A0} inside its field scalar extension. These are consequences after the grand loop, not prerequisites for it. Only the field-half supplier's inherited AC hypothesis is retained.
item.strategy: Module-valuedness and modulo-q adjunction were proved inside the grand loop before J. After D and C, induct on root height: for residue b choose i with ẽ_i b≠0, so b=f̃_i ẽ_i b. Then B_0(b,b')=B_0(ẽ_i b,ẽ_i b'). If ẽ_i b'=0 this is zero; otherwise lower-height orthonormality and the partial-inverse injectivity show it is delta_(b,b'). The top has norm1; since all a_ii=2 the operator Q_i of JKK7.25 is identity, hence no larger positive integer norms occur. Thus the finite Gram matrix is I modulo q, invertible over A0. Its inverse proves the dual lattice equals the lattice. For U^- use the exact corrected C_nu comparison, with sufficiently large regularized dominant weight: the field pi is a lattice isomorphism and its crystal map is a bijection in the degree, and C_nu≡1. For any P,Q in the half lattice, the module pairing is regular and its error relative to C_nu B_infty(P,Q) can be made q^N-small, proving regularity and the same identity Gram residue. This supplies half valuedness and perfection as conclusions. Finally if B(x,x)∈A0 but x has a pole, choose minimal N>0 with q^N x∈L and nonzero residue; its square is a nonzero positive rational sum of squares in the orthonormal residue basis, whereas q^(2N)B(x,x) has zero residue, contradiction. This is finite-component positivity and applies also to any vector's finite support. JKK7.37/7.39 and Kashiwara91§5.1 supply the source argument; the corrected degree-color comparison is proved in the grand loop rather than imported from the printed erroneous factor.

item.title: Integral residues of the negative half: freeness, the crystal basis and the form characterization
item.statement: For L_Z(infinity)=U_A^-∩L(infinity), its canonical injection L_Z/qL_Z→L/qL has image exactly ⊕_(b∈B∞)Z b. It is a free Z-module with basis B∞ and becomes the full rational crystal space after tensoring with Q. The normalized Kashiwara half form takes values on U_A^- in K_Z=Z[q,q^-1,(1−q^(2n))^-1:n≥1], and on L_Z in A_Z=Z[q,(1−q^(2n))^-1:n≥1]. Thus its residue pairing is Z-valued. Its coefficients in B∞ are the integer pairings with b, and its norm1 elements are B∞∪(−B∞). The operators ẽ_i,f̃_i preserve L_Z and its integral residue subgroup. No A-module structure on L_Z, no equality with the rational residue as a Z-module, and no unsigned norm1 characterization is asserted. The module integral residue basis is established in globalization.
item.strategy: The integral skew-string supplier proves every string coefficient and both half Kashiwara operators preserve U_A^-. The completed crystal theorem proves their L∞ stability. Consequently every lowering word applied to1 lies in L_Z, providing an integral representative of every b∈B∞. For P,Q in U_A^-, the exact divided-word denominator bound from the half form places B(P,Q) in K_Z: quantum factorial denominators are Laurent powers times products (1−q^(2d_i r)) divided by powers (1−q^(2d_i)), so K_Z contains every such value. This is the same normalized Kashiwara form as the q0 polarization; there is no second normalization factor between them. The post-grand-loop polarization lemma puts B(P,Q)∈A0 when P,Q∈L_Z. To prove A0∩K_Z=A_Z, take a common denominator D=∏(1−q^(2n))^e with D(0)=1 and integer Laurent numerator. Regularity at0 says exactly that numerator has no negative powers. Evaluation of A_Z at0 gives integers. Thus, for any x∈L_Z with rational residue Σ a_b b, pairing with the integral word representative of b gives a_b∈Z by orthonormality. Conversely all finite integer combinations of the representatives lie in L_Z. The kernel is qL_Z by the preceding Definition, proving the actual free integral residue quotient. For norm1, Σ a_b²=1 with integers a_b has a single coefficient+1 OR−1, so the signed assertion follows. No global integral basis has been presumed.

item.title: Divided-power integrality of the quasi-$R$ action on based lattices
item.statement:
For the actual Θ∈U^+⊗U^- and the exact four-axiom based modules, integral ACTION is proved in these cases: (a) V(lambda)⊗N for any based N (highest FIRST); (b) M⊗ωV(lambda) for any based M (lowest SECOND), with vectorwise finite action; (c) arbitrary U_A-stable based pairs in FINITE Cartan type; (d) a first factor in C_high with arbitrary based second, or an arbitrary based first with second in C_low, under vectorwise finite action. Here C_high consists of exact based subquotients of weight-admissible direct sums of finite highest tensor constructions; C_low is its lowest/unsigned-Chevalley counterpart. Based subobjects are saturated basis subsets and quotient maps are integral/bar compatible. These classes are closed under their normalized finite tensor construction. In particular all finite highest products and ordered highest-prefix/arbitrary-based-middle/lowest-suffix products have the integral tensor action and construction. Upper-cone/finite-component conditions are imposed on direct sums; in the lowest case use its explicit lower-cone action bound. No arbitrary based-O_int pair is covered in general type.
In these cases Θ preserves the actual integral tensor lattice and has A-valued ACTION coefficients in its tensor bases. Its degree0 component is identity; every positive root component shifts the first label up and second down, so the bar is locally weight-transfer triangular with diagonal1. In finite Cartan type the stronger algebra coefficients Θ_nu∈U_A^+_nu⊗U_A^-_-nu are also proved. That stronger universal coefficient claim is false in general affine type. A normalized triangular bar-correction constructs the genuine tensor global basis; raw tensor products of lower basis vectors need not themselves be bar fixed. The class in(d) means based subquotients of weight-admissible direct sums of finite highest tensors with the constructed tensor basis, not arbitrary integral lattices in semisimple field modules. The affine construction in the proof explicitly disproves unqualified arbitrary-based action integrality while retaining these full general symmetrizable cases.
item.strategy:
Highest-first action. The exact divided coproduct is ΔF_i^(r)=Σ_(t=0)^r q_i^(−t(r−t))F_i^(r−t)K_i^t⊗F_i^(t). This follows from q-commutation of F_i⊗1 and K_i⊗F_i and the finite Gaussian theorem. On a homogeneous m of label mu its t coefficient is q_i^(t(mu(h_i)−r+t)), an A-unit. The t=0 term is F_i^(r)m⊗n with coefficient1. The tensor bar Ψ=Θ(psi⊗psi) fixes v_lambda⊗b for each bar-fixed b of N, because every positive root kills the first top. Induct on the first divided-word height. Solve the displayed Δ expression for F_i^(r)m⊗n; all t>0 inputs have strictly smaller first height. U/bar compatibility of Ψ and bar stability of U_A make their barred outputs integral by induction. Thus Ψ preserves every pure divided-word tensor, hence V_A(lambda)⊗N_A, with termination at the finite word height and separately established Θ action finiteness. Since the factor bar is an A-bijection, Θ itself preserves that lattice. This is the complete Bao–Wang approximate-cyclicity proof in the flipped convention; neither lattice freeness nor a highest decomposition of N is used.
Lowest-second action is the exact dual induction: ΔE_i^(r)=Σ_t q_i^(t(r−t))E_i^(t)⊗K_i^-t E_i^(r−t), whose t=0 term raises only the second factor with coefficient1. Θ fixes b⊗the second lowest vector. Induct on its finite positive divided-word height, with t>0 smaller second height and U_A-stable first factor. The lower support bounds give finite action separately. The same reasoning applies to Verma-generated integral images when needed, not an arbitrary invented integral highest section.
Finite-type universal coefficients. Choose a longest Weyl element w0 and sufficiently large regular dominant weights. In each finite highest module construct its lowest extremal vector by the reduced w0 string of divided powers. Each step is a complete rank-one top-to-bottom string, whose normalized norm factor d_(a,a)=1; weights at the extrema are one-dimensional by the already-proved classical character comparison. Hence the extremal vector is integral, bar fixed, norm1, and is the unique signed global element at that weight by the established q0 norm/globalization criterion. Let ω be the unsigned E↔F,K↔K^-1 Chevalley map. It commutes with the normalized sigma (check generators with the toral q² factors), so the field isomorphism from the corresponding lowest module to the highest module, normalized at that extremal vector, is a form isometry and bar compatible. Its source integral lattice maps into the target because the extremal vector is integral and U_A stable. Every transported global vector is integral/bar fixed with residue norm1; the integral signed norm criterion identifies it with ±a target global basis vector. Equal finite dimensions prove a signed integral lattice identification: the transported basis is the target global basis up to individual signs. This is an A-basis/lattice identification, sufficient for the coefficient test below; it is not asserted to be a strict based morphism (which would require basis images without minus signs). Thus the integral lowest and highest lattices are genuinely identified, not merely their field spaces.
Expand Θ_nu in positive/negative global half bases with field coefficients. Choose the finite highest/lowest test modules large enough that all half basis elements in that degree survive their based projections; after the just-proved signed extremal lattice identification these actions are ±distinct global basis vectors. Apply Θ to the lowest extremal vector of the first highest module and the highest extremal vector of the second lowest module. Highest-first action already proves this output integral. Different degrees have distinct weight PAIRS, and in the fixed degree the output basis vectors are independent parts of an actual A-basis. Therefore every expansion coefficient is in A. This reproduces the actual source24.1.6 finite-type argument, including its w0/integral basis prerequisite. It proves algebra integrality in finite type only and hence integral action on arbitrary based pairs there.
General highest tensor construction and closure. Form right-associated products of highest modules: highest-first action proves integral bar at every step, while the field cocycle gives all parenthesizations the same bar without assuming integral action for intermediate arbitrary pairs. The partial order is the first-weight-up/second-weight-down transfer order (and its iterated prefix-weight version). Positive components give strictly transferred pairs, only Θ_0 gives diagonal1. Every relevant upward interval has finite root bounds; for highest/O_int factors each total-weight block is finite as well. In a finite interval solve for a bar-fixed lift g_t=e_t+Σ_(s>t)a_ts e_s with a_ts∈qZ[q], starting at its top. After subtracting already constructed larger lifts, involutivity makes the remaining coefficient f satisfy f+bar f=0. Its unique positive-q part a with a−bar a=f supplies the next correction. Finite induction gives existence/uniqueness and a unitriangular A-matrix with a finite-interval inverse. The corrected family is an A-basis, an A0-basis with the raw tensor crystal residues, and bar-fixed; its A∞-span is the ACTUAL tensor bar chart. Thus its integral balanced intersection is its Z-span. The completed crystal tensor rule supplies the lattice operators/residue basis; bar does not literally preserve A0. This is the full semilinear system proof of Lusztig24.2.1 and the Bao–Wang2.7/2.9 extension, reproduced locally.
For two such highest tensor objects P,Q, the cocycle identifies their grouped tensor bar with the integral normalized bar on the concatenated highest factors. The factor bars are A-bijections, so Θ on P⊗Q is integral. Based subobjects are spanned by subsets of their actual constructed bases and hence saturated: (P_A⊗Q_A)∩(P′⊗Q′)=P′_A⊗Q′_A. Θ preserves their field submodules by its U-monomial terms; integral action follows from that equality. Based quotient maps are U-linear, send basis to basis-or0, have a basis-subset kernel, and commute with bars because both bars fix those bases. Their integral tensor maps are surjective onto free complementary quotient lattices; Θ commutes with the maps termwise, so integral action descends. No field summand is converted into an integral section. Direct sums are handled componentwise with their stated finite weight/upper-cone bounds. These arguments establish exactly the admissible closure class stated above.
Affine algebra and ACTION boundaries. For A1^(1), a01=a10=−2, the degree-delta Kashiwara Gram in F0F1,F1F0 is [[1,q²],[q²,1]]. The correct D coevaluation has factor (q−q^-1)²/(1−q⁴)=q^-2(1−q²)/(1+q²), so it is not a universally integral algebra tensor. For the stronger arbitrary-pair failure, take dominant lambda=Lambda0, mu=lambda−delta and p=[2]. The global g=F1F0v_lambda satisfies E0g=0,E1g=pF0v; F0^(r)g=0 for r≥2 by the length-three divided Serre relation applied to the first highest vector, and F1g=pF1^(2)F0v,F1^(r)g=0 for r≥2 by its rank-one length2 string. The proved integral based-quotient presentation therefore gives a U_A-map V_A(mu)/p→V_A(lambda)/p, sending the highest vector to g modp. For each global h_b its image has bar-fixed coefficients in A/(p)=Z[i], whose bar-fixed ring is Z. Let T_b be its unique integer-coordinate lift in the lambda global basis. Define c_b=h_b+T_b/p and M_A with free basis B_lambda∪{c_b} inside Vlambda⊕Vmu. U_A-stability follows because U T_b−T(Uh_b) is divisible by p. All basis vectors are homogeneous/bar fixed; because 1/p=q/(1+q²)∈qA0, its EXACT chart/residue data equal the standard direct-sum based module, proving all four based axioms, not just field integrability. For N=Vmu and its highest h_mu, Θ(c_top⊗h_mu)=c_top⊗h_mu−(1−q²)/(1+q²)v_lambda⊗g_mu. The simple-root terms vanish; E0E1g=pv,E1E0g=0,F0F1h_mu=0,F1F0h_mu=g_mu, and every higher first raising degree vanishes. The displayed coefficient is not in A and is on a distinct tensor basis vector. Thus the original unrestricted arbitrary based-O_int ACTION assertion is false. The theorem's corrected ordered/constructed hypotheses are mathematically necessary, not a finite-type convenience restriction. For the stronger closure statement, first concatenate a pure highest product P with an arbitrary based N. Right-associated highest-first action makes the whole normalized bar integral. The field cocycle identifies it with the grouped bar Ψ_(P,N); since both factor bars are A-bijections, Θ preserves P_A⊗N_A. Repeat the exact basis-subset intersection and based-quotient image argument on the FIRST factor only, giving C_high⊗N without assuming N belongs to that class. The dual lowest-second argument gives M⊗C_low. Normalized tensor products of based morphisms remain based: they commute with bars and module crystal operators; their image of a tensor global element is integral/bar fixed with the corresponding raw tensor residue or0. The proved triangular balanced uniqueness forces the corresponding target global element or0, and the free bases make the kernel exactly the killed basis subset. Therefore subobjects/quotients of pure highest tensor parents remain based subquotients after further tensoring, proving closure of C_high; likewise C_low. For an ordered highest-prefix/based-middle/lowest-suffix product, each binary split has either a pure highest-class left block or a pure lowest-class right block, so the appropriate action case applies. At a given basis tuple, every prefix transfer is bounded either by that prefix's highest upper cone or by the complementary lowest suffix's lower cone. Thus all correction intervals are finite even when an entire mixed total-weight space is infinite dimensional. The finite triangular construction and field cocycle then prove all bracketings and based quotient inheritance exactly as stated.

item.title: Integrality of the string decomposition and the divided-power string ideals
item.statement:
For the negative-half decomposition u=Σ_l F_i^(l)u_l, ker e_i'∋u_l, all u_l are in U_A^- if u∈U_A^-. The integral projector is P_i=Σ_l(−1)^l q_i^(−l(l−1)/2) F_i^(l)(e_i')^l and u_l=q_i^(l(l−1)/2)P_i(e_i')^l u. All derivation powers here are ORDINARY, not divided by [l]_i!.
Define I_(i,n)^A=U_A^-∩F_i^n U_q^-=⊕_(l≥n)F_i^(l)(ker e_i'∩U_A^-)=Σ_(l≥n)F_i^(l)U_A^- and J_(i,n)^A=pi_lambda(I_(i,n)^A)=Σ_(l≥n)F_i^(l)V_A(lambda). The latter is an A-submodule inside the field string-image subspace F_i^n V(lambda), not a U_q-submodule or U_A-stable lattice in general. Its equality with V_A∩F_i^n V is proved after the adapted global basis construction, not presumed before it.
The integral residue of I_(i,n)^A∩L∞ is the free Z-span of B∞∩f̃_i^n B∞, and the corresponding rational residue of F_i^nU^-∩L∞ is its Q-span. Integral balancedness of the zero/infinity triple is proved by the subsequent string-ideal induction. On every U_A-stable integrable module lattice M_A, if a label mu has <h_i,mu>=−n≤−1, then each u∈(M_A)_mu satisfies the finite identity u=Σ_(k≥n)(−1)^(k−n)[k−1 choose k−n]_i F_i^(k)E_i^(k)u. Thus (M_A)_mu=Σ_(k≥n)F_i^(k)(M_A)_(mu+k alpha_i). This is the exact boundary-generation supplier used in the string-ideal induction.
item.strategy:
The first part is exactly the proved ordinary-power integral skew-string supplier; no divided-derivation integrality is used (in rank one, (e_i')²/[2]_i applied to F_i^(2) gives1/(1+q_i²), not an A scalar). Unique field string positions show membership in F_i^nU^- is equivalent to all u_l=0 for l<n. Integral coefficient extraction therefore proves the direct sum with ker e_i'; the larger spaces F_i^(l)U_A^- overlap and are only a sum. Applying pi gives the stated module IMAGE sum, without asserting saturation/intersection or generator stability. For the integral residue, every b in the indicated subset has an integral representative f̃_i^n applied to an integral word representative. String component extraction preserves L∞, so the rational field image has exactly the Q-basis of those positions. The Z-valued residue pairing from the integral residue supplier forces coefficients of any integral member to be integers. This proves the Z subgroup and kernel as above, not a premature global lift.
For the boundary identity fix z=q_i, mu(h_i)=−n and an admissible string u=F_i^(m)v, Ev=0. Its top weight is2m−n, so m≥n. Rank-one divided-power formulas give F^(k)E^(k)u=[m−n+k choose k]_z[m choose k]_z u, and vanish for k>m. It suffices to prove Σ_(k=n)^m(−1)^(k−n)[k−1 choose k−n]_z[m−n+k choose k]_z[m choose k]_z=1. Here is a complete finite proof. Put Q=z², (Q;Q)_s=∏_(j=1)^s(1−Q^j), and H(t)=∏_(j=1)^(n−1)(1−Q^(-j)t)∏_(j=1)^(m−n)(1−Q^j t), of degree m−1. For every polynomial of degree≤m−1, the finite q-binomial theorem (proved by the Gaussian Pascal recurrence) yields Σ_(k=0)^m(−1)^k Q^(k(k−1)/2−k(m−1)) Gaussian_Q(m,k) H(Q^k)=0: check each monomial t^s, where the sum is ∏_(j=0)^(m−1)(1−Q^(j+s−m+1)), with a zero factor j=m−1−s. For 1≤k<n, H(Q^k)=0. For k≥n, H(Q^k)/[(Q;Q)_(n−1)(Q;Q)_(m−n)]=Gaussian_Q(k−1,n−1)Gaussian_Q(m−n+k,k). For k=0 this ratio is(−1)^(n−1)Q^(−n(n−1)/2). Multiply the zero-sum identity by(−1)^n Q^(n(n−1)/2) divided by those two factorials. Its k=0 term is−1; the remaining terms are exactly the required symmetric-binomial sum, using [a choose b]_z=z^(−b(a−b))Gaussian_Q(a,b). Their exponent is k(k−1)/2−k(m−1)+n(n−1)/2. Hence the remaining sum is1. This proves the boundary identity on every string, therefore on every vector, with finite support by integrability. All coefficients are in A, and E^(k) preserves the actual U_A module lattice, yielding the claimed generation. This reproduces Kashiwara91 Lemma6.1.4 and Proposition6.1.3 with a local proof of the finite Gaussian identity instead of importing Andrews' identity.

item.title: The string-ideal triples are balanced: the induction step (Kashiwara 7.4.1 / JKK 10.4)
item.statement: Fix a root degree alpha of height r. Assume integral balanced/global lifts in every degree of height<r for both the negative half and all dominant highest modules, including based-quotient compatibility there and the negative-half string-ideal membership of each lower lift G∞(b) whenever b∈f̃_i^nB∞. Then for every i,n≥1 the image string-ideal J_(i,n)^A in each highest module, with its rational zero/infinity chart intersections, is integrally balanced in degree lambda−alpha. Its balanced Z-intersection maps isomorphically to the Z-span of Bλ∩f̃_i^n Bλ in that degree. Similarly the half ideal I_(i,n)^A is integrally balanced in degree−alpha, with residue Z-span B∞∩f̃_i^n B∞. Their Laurent extensions are free A-modules with these adapted global lifts. Freeness, chart intersection and the eventual module saturation J_(i,n)^A=V_A∩F_i^n V are conclusions, not hypotheses.
item.strategy:
Use the exact printed Kashiwara91 Proposition7.4.1, descending on n in the fixed degree, where n beyond the degree is zero. Assume J_(i,n+1)^A balanced. Put mu=lambda−alpha. If n+mu(h_i)<0, the boundary generation identity of the preceding supplier gives J_(i,−mu(h_i))^A_mu=V_A_mu, hence J_(i,n)^A_mu is the same full component as the already handled larger-n ideal. The field string-position sets agree because every admissible position at mu is at least−mu(h_i). Thus reduce to n+mu(h_i)≥0.
By definition J_n=F_i^(n)V_A[mu+n alpha_i]+J_(n+1). The lower-degree based quotient expresses the source V_A component using lower G∞(b) with surviving pi_lambda(b). If ẽ_i b≠0, lower-height negative-half string membership puts G∞(b) in I_(i,1)^A, so F_i^(n)G∞(b) lies in I_(i,n+1)^A by multiplying divided powers (integer Gaussians). It contributes only to J_(n+1). The remaining finite Z-module F is generated by phi_b=F_i^(n)G∞(b)v_lambda for ẽ_i b=0 and surviving image; their lower degree global lifts are bar fixed. To see phi_b∈L_mu+J_(n+1), extract P_iG∞(b): G∞(b)−P_iG∞(b) lies in F_iU^- with integral string coefficients, so its F_i^(n) multiple is in the image J_(n+1). The vector F_i^(n)P_iG∞(b) lies in L∞ and has residue f̃_i^n b, since lower-height string extraction and ẽ_i b=0 make all positive components of G∞(b) q-divisible. Project it to Llambda using the completed grand loop. Bar-fixedness of phi_b and bar stability of J_(n+1) give the analogous infinity condition.
The condition n+mu(h_i)≥0 ensures the module string at the surviving top class has length at least n; thus f̃_i^n pi(b) is nonzero and at exactly positionn. These classes biject onto (Bλ∩f̃_i^nBλ)\(f̃_i^(n+1)Bλ), using the completed crystal partial inverses and based quotient in lower degree. By descending balancedness, QJ_(n+1) has residue basis the higher positions, so phi(F) maps injectively modulo that rational subspace at0. The infinity injection is its bar image. Apply the correctly stated integral chart-extension lemma to M=J_n, N=J_(n+1), F with these explicit lifts. It proves balancedness, the exact integral residue sequence and the Z-basis consisting of the new n positions plus all higher positions. This also proves finite A-freeness as a conclusion.
For the half, choose all dominant coordinates large in the explicit auxiliary regular datum. In the fixed degree the Serre ideal is absent, so pi is a field isomorphism, and by definition carries U_A^- onto V_A, and I_n onto J_n. Grand-loop projection carries the rational zero chart isomorphically; commuting bar carries the infinity chart. Transport the already proved integral module triple and its signed-free residue basis back. No global half basis or module-saturation equality was assumed. This uses the primitive-coroot auxiliary weights exactly where the printed source requires large lambda.

item.title: Tensor products of integrable weight modules and of their crystal lattices
item.statement:
Let $M_1,M_2$ be chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight modules ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]), and let $M_1\otimes M_2$ carry the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module structure of [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]] given by the coproduct $\Delta E_i=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$, $\Delta F_i=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$, $\Delta K_h=K_h\otimes K_h$ of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Then:

(a) **Grading.** $M_1\otimes M_2$ is a chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight module for $(M_1\otimes M_2)_\mu=\bigoplus_{\mu_1+\mu_2=\mu}(M_1)_{\mu_1}\otimes(M_2)_{\mu_2}$, a direct sum by [[thm-tensor-products-commute-with-arbitrary-direct-sums]].

(b) **Integrability.** If $M_1,M_2$ are integrable then so is $M_1\otimes M_2$: $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every pure tensor, hence on the whole module.

(c) **Finite weights and bounded support.** If in addition every label-weight space of $M_1,M_2$ is finite dimensional and each weight set is contained in a finite union of cones $\lambda-Q_+$, then the same holds for $M_1\otimes M_2$.

(d) **Tensored lattices.** If $(L_1,B_1),(L_2,B_2)$ are crystal bases of $M_1,M_2$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]), then $L_1\otimes_{A_0}L_2$ is a free $A_0$-submodule of $M_1\otimes M_2$ generating it over $\mathbb Q(q)$, satisfies $(L_1\otimes L_2)_\mu=\bigoplus_{\mu_1+\mu_2=\mu}(L_1)_{\mu_1}\otimes(L_2)_{\mu_2}$, and $B_1\otimes B_2$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $(L_1\otimes L_2)/q(L_1\otimes L_2)$ compatible with these weight decompositions.

No choice principle is used.
item.strategy:
(a) $\Delta K_h$ acts on $(M_1)_{\mu_1}\otimes(M_2)_{\mu_2}$ by $q^{\langle\mu_1,h\rangle}q^{\langle\mu_2,h\rangle}=q^{\langle\mu_1+\mu_2,h\rangle}$, and $\Delta E_i$, $\Delta F_i$ shift the bidegree by $\alpha_i$ and $-\alpha_i$; the direct sum over bidegrees is the published compatibility of tensor products with direct sums.

(b) Put $x:=F_i\otimes1$ and $y:=K_i\otimes F_i$; then $yx=q_i^{-2}xy$, so [[lem-q-binomial-expansion-for-q-commuting-elements]] gives $\Delta(F_i)^n=(x+y)^n=\sum_{j=0}^n\gamma_{n,j}F_i^{\,n-j}K_i^{\,j}\otimes F_i^{\,j}$ with $\gamma_{n,j}\in\mathbb Q(q)$ (only finiteness of the sum matters). On $u\otimes v$ choose $A$ with $F_i^Au=F_i^Av=0$; every term with $n>2A$ has $n-j>A$ or $j>A$ and vanishes, so $F_i$ is locally nilpotent on $u\otimes v$. The same argument with $\Delta E_i=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$, using $(1\otimes E_i)(E_i\otimes K_i^{-1})=q_i^{2}(E_i\otimes K_i^{-1})(1\otimes E_i)$, gives local nilpotence of $E_i$; local nilpotence on all pure tensors gives it on every vector.

(c) For fixed $\mu$ the space $(M_1\otimes M_2)_\mu$ is the sum over pairs $(\mu_1,\mu_2)$ with $\mu_1+\mu_2=\mu$ and both label spaces nonzero. Writing $\mu_j=\lambda_j-\nu_j$ with $\nu_j\in Q_+$ inside the finitely many cones containing the weight sets, the relation $\nu_1+\nu_2=\lambda_1+\lambda_2-\mu$ has only finitely many solutions, so the sum is finite and each term is finite dimensional. The weight set of $M_1\otimes M_2$ is contained in the sum of the finitely many cones.

(d) $L_1\otimes L_2$ is free, and $\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}(L_1\otimes L_2)\cong M_1\otimes M_2$ by the generation hypotheses; the weight decomposition is the tensor product of the direct sum decompositions of $L_1$ and $L_2$. Since $q(L_1\otimes L_2)=qL_1\otimes L_2+L_1\otimes qL_2$, right exactness of the tensor product gives $(L_1\otimes L_2)/q(L_1\otimes L_2)\cong(L_1/qL_1)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}(L_2/qL_2)$, so $B_1\otimes B_2$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis, weight-graded. Only the easy lattice conditions are established here; stability under the crystal operators is the tensor product theorem on this page.

item.title: The vector representation is a perfect crystal of level one and carries a lower global basis
item.statement: The derived level0 vector module has a level1 perfect crystal B={b_1,…,b_e}. Its weights are the finite Weyl orbit of lambda°=Lambda1−Lambda0 in P_cl, with one-dimensional weight spaces and the usual finite highest-weight cone; B⊗B is connected. Every epsilon/phi has level1, B_min=B, and epsilon,phi biject onto the level1 dominant P_cl weights. The basis G(b_j)=v_j, with ordinary semilinear coefficient bar, is an integral/bar-compatible lower basis: all rank-one strings have TWO vertices (highest weight1), their E/F coefficients are1, and divided powers of order≥2 vanish. On V_aff take G(z^a b_j)=z^a v_j with the same properties and the full P-weight; A=Z[q±] and A0 charts are kept separate. The finite V is a U-prime module with P_cl weights, not a level1 full P-graded highest module.
item.strategy: The finite Weyl reflections permute the vector weights Lambda_j−Lambda_(j−1); take the finite subdiagram I\{0} and lambda° for the highest cone. For B⊗B in our convention, any off-diagonal(a,b) can be raised in its FIRST factor by e_(a−1) until a=b: while a≠b, both comparison entries are0, so the non-strict e tie picks the first factor and that arrow exists. Diagonal(j,j) connects to(j+1,j+1) by two f_j moves. This proves connectedness, and the OP channel is its flip. The displayed epsilon/phi are the fundamental-class bijections, proving the level1 perfect conditions; the weights themselves have level0 and are not in W Lambda0. Direct generator matrices prove integral stability, both bar relations and the lower A0 crystal data. All relevant T_(i,c,t) on these integral weights have Gaussian eigenvalues. There is no invocation of highest-module global basis existence for an unbounded level0 affinization.

item.title: Category-O translation intertwines residue induction and restriction
item.statement: There are natural isomorphisms f_i^H π≅π f_i^O and e_i^H π≅π e_i^O, compatible with residue projectors, units/counits and ordinary restricted/*-dualities. Category O uses the genuine typed coset realization for admissible nonintegral origins, not an unqualified integer block. This statement preserves the actual residue/standard filtrations; an unspecified graded parity or Koszul lift is not asserted by these ungraded suppliers.

item.title: Existence of the crystal basis $(\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty))$ of the negative half
item.statement:
Let $\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq U_q^-$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the Kashiwara lattice and set of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with the Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]](iii).

(i) $(\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty))$ is a crystal basis of $U_q^-$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is a free $A_0$-submodule with $U_q^-\cong\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}\mathcal L(\infty)$, stable under $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$; and $\mathcal B(\infty)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ satisfying $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$, $\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)$, and $\tilde f_ib=b'\iff b=\tilde e_ib'$ for all $b,b'\in\mathcal B(\infty)$.

(ii) The root-graded components are free: $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ is a free $A_0$-module of rank $\#\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}=\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^-[-\nu]$.

(iii) For every $\lambda\in P^+$ the projection $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$ maps $\mathcal B(\infty)$ onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$, and the compatibility statements of [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]] hold: $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0\}\cong\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ and $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ whenever $\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0$.

(iv) The root-graded crystal has finite epsilon_i on each element, formal phi_i=epsilon_i+<h_i,wt>, and actual lowering length ell_i^-=infinity. Every f̃_i iterate is nonzero because ẽ_i f̃_i=id holds on its lattice and residue. Thus it is the infinite lowering crystal of the unit, with the negative-half convention of the crystal-graph Definition.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and enters only through the grand loop: the partial-inverse axiom in (i) uses clause J(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof consumes the AC-dependent form comparison of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]]. The freeness and rank statements are choice-free.
item.strategy:
All content is read off from the grand loop, exactly as in Kashiwara's Theorem 4 and JKK Theorem 7.1(b).

(i) $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is by definition the $A_0$-span of the monomials $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$; each weight piece is a finitely generated $A_0$-module ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]](c)) inside the finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q(q)$-space $U_q^-[-\alpha]$, hence torsion-free and free over the principal ideal domain $A_0$ ([[cor-finitely-generated-torsion-free-modules-over-a-pid-are-free]]); this gives the freeness in (i) and the decomposition in (ii), and $\mathcal L(\infty)\otimes_{A_0}\mathbb Q(q)=U_q^-$ by the argument of Step 7 of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]] (for $\lambda\gg0$ the map $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-[-\alpha]\to V(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ is an isomorphism and $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$). Stability of $\mathcal L(\infty)$ under $\tilde f_i$ is by construction (a $\tilde f$-monomial is a monomial), and stability under $\tilde e_i$ is clause H(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]](i). The basis statement and $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$ are clauses K(r) and I(r); $\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)$ because a $\tilde f_i$-image of a monomial is a monomial and because $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\operatorname{id}$ prevents the class from vanishing modulo $q$; and the partial-inverse axiom follows from clause J(r) together with $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\operatorname{id}$: if $\tilde f_ib=b'$ then $b=\tilde e_ib'$ by [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]](iii), and conversely if $b=\tilde e_ib'$ with $b'=\tilde f_ib''$ then $b=b''$ by J(r), so $b'=\tilde f_ib$. The rank formula in (ii) is K(r) together with the spanning of $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ over $A_0$ and the equality $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\otimes_{A_0}\mathbb Q(q)=U_q^-[-\alpha]$.

(iii) is the content of [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]], which is proved from the same induction; the surjectivity of $\pi_\lambda$ onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ is its clause (c).

(iv) $\tilde f_i$ is injective on $U_q^-$ by [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]](iii), so $\varphi_i(b)=\infty$ for every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)$, while $\varepsilon_i(b)<\infty$ by the definition of the crystal basis; the remaining properties of [[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]] are parts of the crystal-basis axioms. The axiom of choice is inherited through clause J(r) of the grand loop, which the partial-inverse axiom uses via [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]] (JKK Proposition 7.29); it is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. Apart from that inheritance, all lattices involved are finitely generated over the principal ideal domain $A_0$ and no choice is used. Interpret formal phi_i by the corrected negative-half convention; it is not the number of remaining lowering arrows. The ẽ_i f̃_i identity proves nonvanishing directly modulo q, not merely by field injectivity.

item.title: The degenerate Ariki categorification theorem
item.statement: Assume the bounded-below charge hypothesis: $I$ is a non-empty set of consecutive integers bounded below and $\Lambda\in P^+$ has level $l$ and charge $m_1\ge\cdots\ge m_l$. Then the two identifications of the preceding theorems hold simultaneously for the degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower $H^\Lambda$: $[\mathrm{Proj}(H^\Lambda)]\cong V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ with $[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ and $[\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)]\cong V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ with $[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$, $[S(B)]\mapsto S_B$, and they are mutually dual under the Cartan and Shapovalov pairings. Moreover: (i) for every $B\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ one has $[S(B)]=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)[D(A)]$, where $d_{A,B}(s)\in\mathbb Z[s]$ is defined by $M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)L_A$ (equivalently $P_A=\sum_B d_{A,B}(s)M_B$); (ii) the endomorphisms of both Grothendieck groups induced by $e_i,f_i$ $(i\in I)$ are the Chevalley operators $e_i,f_i$ of $\dot U_{\mathbb Z}(\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+})$; (iii) for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $i\in I$ the module $e_iD(A)$ (resp. $f_iD(A)$) is nonzero if and only if $\tilde e_i(A)\neq\varnothing$ (resp. $\tilde f_i(A)\neq\varnothing$), in which case it is a self-dual indecomposable module with irreducible socle and head isomorphic to $D(\tilde e_i(A))$ (resp. $D(\tilde f_i(A))$); (iv) in the source's normalization the projective classes correspond to the quasi-canonical family $P_A$, which at parameter one equals the canonical family on $V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z}$ ($P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}$ at $s=1$), while the simple classes correspond to the dual-canonical family $D_A=\pi L_A$, the label bijections being the rectification $A\mapsto A^\uparrow$ and its inverse $\downarrow$ between $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda_\alpha$ and $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda_\alpha$. For any admitted consecutive I, including Z and half-infinite sets, the same blockwise statements hold. For a fixed alpha and finite list of residue operations choose lower/upper cuts whose LETTER alphabet contains every charge and whose ROOT interval contains the support of alpha and the required shifted supports. Added bottom tails are common ground and added top entries absent; the actual16 double-cut compatibility and actual17 contractible-central-corner restriction identify these SAME Hecke blocks, intrinsic Spechts, projective/simple labels and residue maps. These compatible finite pieces give the original arbitrary-I statement. At level0 only alpha=0 and the ground survive.
item.strategy: Assume AC. Combine the corrected G0/K0 theorems, preserving the natural lattice inclusion and projected simple pairing. Exact pi sends every standard composition series to its Specht series, so the true source inverse-chart d_(A,B)(1) gives decomposition multiplicities on Std rows. Actual17 tensor/residue intertwining gives both Chevalley actions. For head/socle transfer, actual16's simple translation of a Std label has Std head and socle. The corner right adjoint G has injective unit on a Std-socle target and torsion cokernel; a Std-head source has no maps to that cokernel. Hence Hom(M,N)=Hom(pi M,pi N) in this exact situation. It proves the specified simple head; ordinary duality proves the same socle and self-duality, giving indecomposability and the nonzero/crystal criterion. This does not require pi* exactness or all-projective image preservation. At parameter1 the actual16 weight power disappears and P_A=T_(A up), while D_A=pi_Fock L_A retains the correct dual lattice. For arbitrary I choose cuts containing EVERY charge and support; if needed use an auxiliary stable alphabet, then contract its forced-ground rows and absent top letters. Fixed content forces precisely those additions, so the actual16 basis equations and actual17 block/projector maps agree; intrinsic Spechts depend only on the same multipartitions/charges. The standard lattice and pairing are finite weightwise duals of this compatible G0 map. Thus the identifications glue over the actual common-tail/double-cut embeddings. Focused proof §§2,4 records the exact hypotheses; no source17 mathematics is reopened.

item.title: The based quotient: projection of the lower global basis to a highest weight module
item.statement: The projection pi_lambda:U_A^-→V_A(lambda) is a based quotient over Z[q,q^-1]: G∞(b) maps to0 if its crystal image is0 and to Gλ(pi(b)) otherwise. Thus its kernel is the A-span of exactly the killed global basis elements, and the surviving global basis elements map bijectively onto the integral highest-module basis. The module weight components are finite free over A, and the compatible zero/infinity chart and residue projections have the already proved crystal compatibility. This holds for every symmetrizable datum with the explicit label/auxiliary-realization convention. More precisely its integral kernel is Σ_iΣ_(s>lambda(h_i)) U_A^-F_i^(s). Thus the integral highest-module presentation uses ALL divided right powers beyond each highest limit, not just an ordinary power with a nonunit factorial.
item.strategy: Apply the integral balanced theorem’s actual string-ideal argument for killed images and its uniqueness argument for surviving images. The free A-decompositions then make the kernel precisely the span of killed basis vectors and give the quotient basis, with no appeal to symmetric canonical-basis agreement. Chart projection and modulo-q compatibility come from the completed grand loop and commuting bar. This is Kashiwara91 Lemma7.5.2 and the final proof of Theorem7(ii), printed p.516, not an unproved quotient fallback. For this integral presentation, reversal preserves integral/chart lattices and carries each global lift to a signed global lift: its image is bar fixed, its integral residue has norm1, hence is ±a crystal residue, and balanced uniqueness supplies the signed lift. It therefore carries the already saturated left ideal I_(i,n)^A to the saturated right ideal R_(i,n)^A=U_A^-∩U^-F_i^n=Σ_(s≥n)U_A^-F_i^(s), each adapted to subsets of one signed global basis. The field Serre kernel is Σ_iU^-F_i^(lambda(h_i)+1). A sum of subspaces spanned by subsets of one basis is the span of their union; intersecting its field span with the full free A-global lattice gives exactly the A-span of that union. This proves the stated integral sum of all divided right ideals, without presuming that arbitrary integral intersections commute with sums.

item.title: The column monomial basis of the higher-level Fock module
item.statement: For a finite interval, normally ordered wedges $v_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge v_{i_d}$, $i_1>\cdots>i_d$, form the integral basis of the fundamental wedge, with antisymmetrizer coefficients $(-s)^{\ell(w)}$. The antisymmetrizer embedding is primitive over $\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]$; this does not assert lower-q0 basedness of that embedding into raw tensor powers. The column monomials form the tensor basis of $F(\Lambda)$, with their stated weights. Upper cuts include all entries of a given monomial; lower-cut embeddings append the common bottom $k-1$ entry to each column. Their compatible direct limit gives the full bounded or semi-infinite Fock module. All generators act by finitely many box moves and SHIFT weight spaces; fixed-weight spaces are finite-dimensional. A merely lower-bounded infinite interval need not give finite-dimensional fundamental factors; all finite-Cartan statements are applied on finite cuts.
item.strategy: Sorting the quantum exterior quotient by adjacent interchange relations gives unique ordered words: braid overlaps have the same scalar product, and repeated letters vanish. Hence the integral quotient is free, not a generic-field dimension inference. The corresponding antisymmetrizer vectors have disjoint permutation supports and ordered coefficient1, so their span is primitive/saturated. Direct E,F action replaces a valid entry once and gives0 on a repeated entry; it identifies the wedge with the fundamental highest module and its own divided-power lattice/bar/crystal. Tensoring these bases gives column monomial independence. Adding a common lower tail gives injective maps with the stated monomial action; every semi-infinite tableau belongs to some lower/upper finite cut. Fixed weight determines a finite multiset change from the common ground tail, so only finitely many tableaux occur. Direct generator formulas move finitely many boxes and are compatible once the cut contains the residue and input/output supports.

item.title: Highest weight components in a tensor product crystal
item.statement:
**Assume the axiom of choice** ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited through [[thm-crystal-bases-of-integrable-modules-decompose-into-highest-weight-crystals]]. Let $M_1,M_2$ be integrable chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight modules with finite-dimensional label-weight spaces and weight sets contained in finite unions of cones, let $(L_1,B_1),(L_2,B_2)$ be crystal bases of $M_1,M_2$, and let $B_1\otimes B_2$ be the crystal of $M_1\otimes M_2$ ([[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]], [[lem-tensor-products-of-integrable-weight-modules-are-integrable]]).

(a) **Highest vertices.** For $b=b_1\otimes b_2\in B_1\otimes B_2$ the following are equivalent: (i) $b$ is a highest weight element, i.e. $\tilde e_ib=0$ for every $i\in I$; (ii) $\varepsilon_i(b_1)=0$ and $\varepsilon_i(b_2)\le\langle h_i,wt(b_1)\rangle$ for every $i\in I$; (iii) $\varepsilon_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=0$ for every $i\in I$. In this case $wt(b)=wt(b_1)+wt(b_2)$ is dominant.

(b) **Generated components.** For every highest vertex $b\in B_1\otimes B_2$ of weight $\lambda$, the lowering-generated subcrystal $F(b)$ is a connected component of $B_1\otimes B_2$, is isomorphic as a crystal to the canonical $B(\lambda)=\mathcal B(\lambda)$ of [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-exists]], and $\lambda\in P^+$.

(c) **Decomposition.** $B_1\otimes B_2$ is the disjoint union of the subcrystals $F(b)$ over the highest weight elements $b\in B_1\otimes B_2$, each of which is a highest weight crystal in the sense of [[def-highest-weight-element-and-connected-highest-weight-crystal]]; the multiplicity of $B(\lambda)$ as a component equals the multiplicity of $V(\lambda)$ in the tensor product module $M_1\otimes M_2$.

No choice principle beyond the inherited one is used.
item.strategy:
(a) By [[lem-crystal-tensor-product-weight-epsilon-and-phi-formulas]](b), $\varepsilon_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\max(\varepsilon_i(b_1),\varepsilon_i(b_2)-\langle h_i,wt(b_1)\rangle)$, so $\tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=0$ for all $i$ if and only if this maximum is $0$ for all $i$, i.e. $\varepsilon_i(b_1)=0$ and $\varepsilon_i(b_2)\le\langle h_i,wt(b_1)\rangle$; this is the equivalence of (i),(ii) and, by definition, of (iii). Dominance: $\langle h_i,wt(b)\rangle=\varphi_i(b)\ge0$ because $\varepsilon_i(b)=0$ and $\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,wt(b)\rangle$ is finite and nonnegative for a crystal of an integrable module ([[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]]).

(b) Apply [[thm-crystal-bases-of-integrable-modules-decompose-into-highest-weight-crystals]] to $M_1\otimes M_2$, which satisfies the category hypotheses by [[lem-tensor-products-of-integrable-weight-modules-are-integrable]](a)-(c), with the crystal basis $(L_1\otimes L_2,B_1\otimes B_2)$ of [[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]]. The theorem decomposes the crystal into components $\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$ whose highest vertices are exactly the highest weight elements (clause (iii)). The component of $b$ therefore is a highest weight crystal of weight $\lambda=wt(b)$; by [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-exists]](ii) its vertex set is $F(b)$, and its identification with $\mathcal B(\lambda)$ is the transported isomorphism of the uniqueness theorem.

(c) The disjoint-union statement is the component decomposition of the same theorem together with the uniqueness of the highest vertex in each component; the multiplicity statement is clause (ii) there applied to $M_1\otimes M_2$, whose highest weight multiplicities are those of the tensor product module. The axiom of choice is used only through the uniqueness theorem, where it is already declared; no new nonconstructive step occurs.

item.title: Indecomposable tilting objects exist and are classified in parabolic category O
item.statement: Assume AC. Every label A in a genuine tableau parabolic block has a unique indecomposable tilting $T(A)$ whose standard flag begins with $M(A)$ once at the bottom and all remaining labels $B<A$. Equivalently it has that maximal-label normalized standard flag and $\operatorname{Ext}^1(M(B),T(A))=0$ for all B. Every tilting is a finite direct sum of these and their classes form a unitriangular Grothendieck basis. Restricted duality fixes $T(A)$. For a finite lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing A the corresponding partial tilting is the SAME ambient $T(A)$, since all support is $\le A$; compatible ideal systems therefore stabilize in each finite block, with the stated flag-preserving inclusions. No uniqueness is claimed from a bottom-standard occurrence alone without indecomposability/maximal support. In the original inline prinjectivity claim, P(A) is projective-injective (equivalently self-dual) exactly when A is standard; in that case P(A)=T(A^up) with the proved rectification label.
item.strategy: Apply the independently proved parabolic semiregular CONTRAVARIANT standard-flag equivalence to opposite projective Pbar(A). Extensions from target standards to its image invert to split extensions of the opposite projective, so Ext1(Δ,−)=0 and the preceding genuine finite-highest-weight criterion makes it tilting. Opposite BGG/reversed order gives labelA once with onlyB<A, and maximal trace arranges Δ_A at the bottom. For two candidates, extend the common bottom inclusion both ways using Ext1 against standard flags; composites restrict to its identity, hence are nonnilpotent. Finite-dimensional local End/Fitting forces isomorphisms. For any tilting summand choose a maximal flag label, extend maps to/from its T(A), split the resulting idempotent and induct on length. Duality preserves its normalized support so fixes it by uniqueness. This also proves partial-ideal and Grothendieck basis assertions. No Irving prinjectivity criterion or Borel-only theorem is imported. The inline prinjectivity proof is also local. The full source-positive projection kernel spanned by L_offStd is U-stable, and the actual mixed multiplicity map identifies these with simple classes. Since residue functors have nonnegative composition coefficients, iterating them on an offStd simple never gives a Std composition factor. Every generalized standard M(B) embeds into an iterated e-word of an irreducible standard M(C): add successively huge offsets to the later columns so all later entries lie above earlier ones, making C the unique minimum in its fixed-multiset tableau order, hence its standard is simple. Lower the later-column entries back, columns left-to-right and entries bottom-to-top, with the explicit residue word. A later column remains above the active residues; a wrong move can only occur in an earlier column and strictly increases an earlier prefix weight, so the intended B is the unique maximal final standard section and occurs once. Exact flags and the canonical maximal trace embed M(B) at the bottom. Use a temporary larger finite alphabet for this finite word, returning to the original character. If L(A) embeds M(B), adjunction gives the Std L(C) as a quotient of an f-word on L(A), impossible offStd by kernel stability/positivity. Conversely each Std label is reached from the unique ground simple projective by the crystal f-word. The proved simple-head clause makes P(A) a summand of that translated projective-injective, hence injective. A projective-injective indecomposable is self-dual: DP(A)=P(B), the simple classes are duality-fixed, and the Cartan matrix is D D^transpose with unitriangular D, hence invertible; [P(A)]=[P(B)] forces A=B. SelfdualP(A) has its head in its socle and its standard flag embeds that simple into a standard section. Finally P_Std=s^a T_Aup in the proved pure highest normalization gives equality of classes at1; since P(A) is an indecomposable tilting, its unique maximal standard label identifies it as T(A^up). No Irving or futureSchur theorem is imported.

item.title: Tensor bars on finite products of based integrable modules
item.statement:
For ANY finite sequence of based integrable modules in finite-weight-space O_int, the field tensor bar Ψ=Θ(composite factor bars) is well defined, semilinear, U/bar compatible, involutive and independent of all parenthesizations. All root-height sums are vectorwise finite. This field assertion is preserved for arbitrary based pairs; it does not imply integral action.
Its integral/based assertion holds for the actual admissible cases proved by the integral-action supplier: highest-first or first C_high with arbitrary based second; arbitrary based first with lowest/C_low second under finite action; all finite highest products and exact based subquotients/direct sums of their tensor constructions; ordered highest-prefix/based-middle/lowest-suffix products with explicit local support bounds; and arbitrary based pairs/products in finite Cartan type (including the finite-degree polynomial type-A modules). For any other pair the same conclusion is conditional on an independently PROVED integral Θ action, not field semisimplicity or lattice freeness.
In these cases Ψ preserves the divided-power integral tensor lattice. Its action on raw tensor lower basis vectors is locally weight-transfer triangular with diagonal1; the actual tensor global vectors are its uniquely corrected bar-fixed lifts congruent to those raw tensor vectors moduloq, with corrections in qZ[q]. They form a genuine A-basis and give the integral balanced tensor triple. The q0 tensor lattice and crystal basis are supplied separately by the completed crystal tensor rule. Its infinity chart is Ψ(L0_tensor), not an asserted bar containment in L0; semilinearity sends q toq^-1. The raw tensor lower vectors are generally not bar fixed. The exact based integral/bar-compatible subquotient maps preserve the corrected global bases by balanced uniqueness. No assertion covers arbitrary two-sided-unbounded evaluation, semi-infinite limits, a universal-R braiding, or general arbitrary-based integral action (the affine boundary in the supplier disproves the latter).
item.strategy:
Field construction first. Θ's explicit positive-first weight action is finite on upper-cone pairs and their finite products; on the ordered lowest cases use the supplied lower bounds before evaluating. Define the binary semilinear bar as Θ(psi_M⊗psi_N). Its scalar involution is q↦q^-1. Applying it twice gives ΘbarΘ=1, hence Ψ²=id. The exact ΔuΘ=ΘbarΔu gives Ψ(u x)=psi(u)Ψ(x). For three factors the two maps are ((Δ⊗id)Θ)Θ12 times factor bars and ((id⊗Δ)Θ)Θ23 times factor bars; the established field cocycle makes them equal. Binary associativity generates all finite rebracketings. This uses no integral action assumption and retains the valid rational theorem for arbitrary O_int inputs.
Integral cases are the complete action proof of the preceding supplier, not inferred from freeness or sourcefinite-type statements outside their range. With those hypotheses, Ψ preserves the A-tensor lattice and Ψ²=1 makes it an A-bijection. Each positive root term raises the first factor's label and lowers the second; only degree0 fixes a label pair, so it is triangular with diagonal1 in the explicit weight-transfer order. The supplier's finite semilinear correction algorithm then gives unique Ψ-fixed tensor global vectors with qZ[q] corrections. Local finite intervals ensure all corrections and inverse transition sums terminate. For upper-cone inputs each fixed total-weight block is finite; for ordered lowest suffixes use bounded transfer intervals instead of falsely claiming finite-dimensional mixed total-weight spaces.
The corrected vectors form an A-basis and an A0-basis of the ORIGINAL tensor crystal lattice; their residue classes are precisely the raw tensor crystal basis. Because they are Ψ-fixed, their A∞-span is the actual bar chart Ψ(L0_tensor). Intersecting the Laurent/zero/infinity coefficient rings in this basis gives Z-span and proves integral balancedness. Thus q0 crystal stability is a consequence of the independent crystal tensor supplier, whereas the bar chart is an infinity chart; no bar-preserves-A0 assertion is made. The integral tensor lattice is U_A-stable by the explicit Gaussian divided coproducts for E/F and diagonal toral Gaussian actions on the chosen label basis. Homogeneous corrected weights, U/bar compatibility and the residue tensor crystal verify every based condition. Exact based subobjects/quotients have saturated basis-subset kernels, commute with bar and residue operators; their images of these global lifts are integral/bar fixed with one residue or0, so balanced uniqueness proves basis-or0 compatibility. This proves the claimed inheritance without arbitrary integral sections.

item.title: Simple and projective crystals of the cyclotomic quotient are $B(\Lambda)$
item.statement: For the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient over any field with the general real symmetrizable datum and graded KLR parameters, let $\mathcal B_\Lambda$ be the normalized $D_\psi$-self-dual simple classes. Set $\mathrm{wt}(S)=\Lambda-\beta$, $\varepsilon_i(S)=\max\{r:(E_i^{\rm basic})^rS\ne0\}$ and $\varphi_i(S)=\varepsilon_i(S)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(S)\rangle$. For $\varepsilon_i>0$, define $\widetilde e_iS$ by the unique simple isomorphism type in the socle of one-step right restriction, with its unique self-dual normalization; define $\widetilde f_iS$ by the simple head of right induction when nonzero, otherwise zero. The one-step socle/head is one shifted copy, not a quantum-factorial multiplicity. These data form a crystal canonically isomorphic to $B(\Lambda)$, with vacuum sent to $u_\Lambda$. The normalized indecomposable projectives carry the same crystal by their normalized simple heads and covers. The projective graph here is explicitly transported from these labels, rather than obtained by applying linear Kashiwara operators to an unspecified projective basis. The highest-weight quotient has simple survivors exactly when $\varepsilon_i^{\rm LEFT}(S)\le\lambda_i$ for every $i$.
item.strategy:
1. Inflate a cyclotomic simple to the generic algebra. The one-step supplier proves the actual unique head/socle and rank-one multiplicities through the nil-Hecke matrix/corner description; its first-dot index identifies the FIRST-strand ideal criterion with $\varepsilon_i^{\rm LEFT}\le\lambda_i$. This argument uses finite-dimensional nilpotent-dot simples and works over the original field, including positive characteristic.
2. The two-color supplier proves the full general-$Q$ jump formula and strict elementary embeddings from actual shuffle filtrations, divided restriction multiplicities and explicit rank-two operators. The linear Serre relation is applied in $G_0$, not to a nonlinear simple operator. It establishes the generic crystal extraction hypotheses in every real symmetrizable type; no ADE-only or finite-rank-two-orbit argument replaces them.
3. Apply the canonical elementary-extraction/highest-weight-survivor supplier. Its positive highest-weight tensor models and unsigned star identification give the generic $B(\infty)$ labeling by RIGHT operators and identify the left-survivor subset with the canonical $B(\Lambda)$ under $\pi_\Lambda$. It proves connectedness from the vacuum, strictness and the truncation of induction at the string endpoint. If an auxiliary primitive-coroot datum is needed for sufficiently large containing weights, it has the same $A,D,Q$ and does not change the KLR algebras. Thus the displayed weight, epsilon and phi are precisely the highest-weight crystal functions.
4. The quotient-cover lemma identifies normalized covers with their simple heads bijectively, with diagonal tensor pairing. Transfer the simple arrows through this bijection. This proves the projective crystal statement and its normalized labeling without using the later lower/upper global-basis conclusions. Choice is inherited only through the declared abstract crystal/balanced-lift suppliers in the extraction step.

item.title: Standard tableau monomials form a basis of the highest weight Fock submodule
item.statement: The highest vector $M_{A_\Lambda}$ generates the multiplicity-one constituent $V(\Lambda)\subset F(\Lambda)$ and there is its normalized module projection $\pi$. The vectors $S_A=\pi M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a basis, and $D_A=\pi L_A$ on that set form the SOURCE dual-canonical basis. What vanishes is $\pi L_A$ for $A$ not standard; $\pi M_A$ need not vanish there. The integral kernel is the saturated direct summand with basis $L_A$ off $\mathrm{Std}$, and $\pi(F_\mathcal A)$ has the actual basis $D_A$ (also $S_A$ on $\mathrm{Std}$), the source upper/costandard lattice. For every $B$, $\pi M_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}}d_{A,B}(s)D_A$, giving explicit straightening of nonstandard projected monomials. All bases/maps commute with upper cuts and common-tail embeddings; this proves the full direct-limit assertion. The relation of source $D_A$ to the library form-dual upper family is the weight rescaling below, not an unqualified identification.
item.strategy: Use a based HIGHEST inclusion, not an internal antisymembedding. The map j:VΛ→F sends the pure ground highest monomial, maps the divided-power lattice into F_A, commutes intrinsic lower divided-string operators and sends their zero chart into the actual finite8 tensor chart. Every crystal edge remains nonzero by partial inverses. It commutes ordinary bar by equality on the highest generator, hence maps the infinity chart too; balanced uniqueness gives jG_low=T on the original lower ground component Rev. For the reverse-factor product the same proof gives tildeT on Std. The column signature rule cancels−+ and selects rightmost+/leftmost−; neighbor row inequalities prove Std closed. At a highest tableau the rightmost column is consecutive ground; inductively overlapping rows force ground in earlier columns, and a gap above the overlap has an unmatched−. Raising terminates by bounded entry sum, so Std is exactly that component. Reverse column order with the prescribed top slides gives Rev; row/reverse insertion is a crystal isomorphism because the two elementary Knuth moves preserve cancelling signs and follow the changed entry along its bump path. This proves both actual label sets. Define π by C0(v,πy)=C(j_reverse v,y), where C0 is the normalized nondegenerate EF-swap form on the highest constituents. The typed contravariance of C gives U-linearity and highest normalization identifies the canonical projection. C(tildeT_A,L_B)=δ then proves vanishing offStd and gives D_Std as the C0-dual basis. Restricting the unitriangular d matrix to Std makes S_Std a basis and gives the explicit straightening inverse. The integral kernel/images follow from this actual basis, not from an A-unit Gram determinant. Finite double-cut compatibility and unique highest maps give the full limit proof. No quantum flag algebra, PeterWeyl or category-O dimension argument is imported.
