item.title: Normally ordered q-wedges form a basis for every finite wedge length
item.statement: For every N, decreasing-index wedges are a field basis and an A=Z[q±] basis of W_A. Straightening terminates using a well-founded pair profile: correction terms strictly decrease dominance of the sorted index multiset, while a leading adjacent swap decreases inversion count. Indices stay inside their original finite bounds; there is no bound by the initial inversion count alone. Define W0=⊕_(normal tuples) A0 u_I, and W_inf its actual bar chart once the normalized bar is constructed; these are not W_A moduloq. W0 with residues of the ordered wedges is a crystal basis of the integrable affine wedge module. The unordered image of the full A0 tensor lattice need not equal W0, and negative q powers in straightening are not falsely called q0-triangular.
item.strategy: Spanning: each relation preserves total index sum and keeps indices in the original finite interval. There are finitely many possible multisets/permutations; every secondary pair is more balanced, lowering the sorted dominance profile, and leading swaps reduce inversions. A repeated entry gives0. Thus all branches terminate. Independence: apply the finite antisymmetrizer to any finite family of decreasing tensors; its Laurent coefficients specialize atq1 to independent ordinary antisymmetrizations, so a nonzero finite minor remains nonzero in Q(q). This proves field independence. Integral Laurent straightening then proves W_A is free with precisely that basis, not by nonPID torsionfreeness. For the crystal claim, fix i and the occupied set of a normal integer tuple. The pairs(i+ke,i+ke+1) are disjoint even at e=2. Empty/doubly occupied pairs are frozen; a singly occupied pair is a two-vertex string. Shifting an index by1 either stays ordered or collides and vanishes, so every finite orbit is a product of these free bits. In decreasing-index order the projected coproduct coefficients are exactly the standard tensor of highest-weight1 strings; frozen double pairs contribute net K weight0. Existing finite rank-one tensor rule proves A0 string stability, partial inverses and the residue basis on every such block. This supplies the correct lower chart without importing a source-chart identification through the OP flip.

item.title: Parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials give the dual-canonical transition matrix
item.statement:
For $I$ bounded below use the actual finite classical tableau-block dictionary (including repeated entries). Fix the right place action $(a w)_i=a_{w(i)}$. Let $w_A$ be shortest with $a(A)w_A$ weakly increasing, and let $K$ be the Young stabilizer of that sorted multiset. Then $w_A$ is shortest RIGHT modulo $K$, $d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ shortest LEFT, and
$$p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,w_B}(s^{-2}).$$
This is the ANTISPHERICAL/sign family for the ENTRY stabilizer, in the left convention after inversion, with Hecke variable $v=s$; the library QUANTUM parameter is instead $t=s^{-1}$. It has support $A\le B$ and diagonal1; $d$ is its inverse coefficient matrix through $p(-s)$. The COLUMN Levi subgroup $J$ is generally different from $K$. Assuming AC, the genuine parabolic block composition matrix is
$$[M(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)=\sum_{C\sim_{\rm col}B}(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1).$$
This uses singular ordinary SPHERICAL coefficients for the entry stabilizer inside finite Levi cancellation, so covers mixed singular-ambient/parabolic-Levi blocks. It does not identify a singular category with genuine parabolic O or identify the two polynomial families by an opposite convention.
item.strategy: Check the tensor Hecke generators directly on tuple monomials, with reciprocal sourceB1 parameter; sorting identifies trivial induction for K and the opposite triangular chart is sign induction. Project ordinary KL vectors to the sign quotient. Simultaneous inversion gives p_{w_Az,w_B}=p_{z^-1d(A),d(B)}, so the15 alternating-sum/triangular uniqueness theorem gives the displayed FULL polynomial identity, not a sample or q=1 family test. The source-positive-s wedge antisymembedding has ordered leading coefficient1, positive-degree within-column corrections and compatible ordinary bar (highest-factor intertwining and quasi-R naturality). Expanding a source L_A gives the ambient tensor L_{a(A)} by positive-chart uniqueness; this embedding is not asserted library-lower based. At1,15 singular ordinary multiplicities give [M(a):L(c)]=P_{w_a w0,w_cw0}(1)=P_{d(a)w0,d(c)w0}(1), by inversion plus longest conjugation. Finite Levi Weyl characters/PBW give ch M(B)=sum_C (−1)^ell(B,C)ch ordinaryM(C). Comparing with the same signed exterior monomial expansion in the tensor L basis proves d_AB(1) equals the displayed mixed parabolic matrix, using character injectivity. Thus regular and singular ambient cases are both closed locally without Koszul or double-coset category equivalence.

item.title: Finitely generated free integral weight lattices and deformation of the classical weight character
item.statement: For every dominant label weight lambda, let V_A=U_Av_lambda=U_A^-v_lambda inside the simple integrable L(lambda). Over A=Z[q,q^-1], each label-weight component of V_A is finite FREE of rank dim_Q(q)L(lambda)_mu, not merely torsionfree. It spans the field module. For every characteristic-zero q=1 specialization k, the fibre has the same weight dimensions and is the classical simple integrable highest module of the explicitly regularized realization, transported to the original label lattice. Thus its character is the Weyl-Kac character (the finite Weyl character in finite type). The integral Serre quotient equals L(lambda) in every symmetrizable type, as already proved by the early local comparison.
item.strategy: The simultaneous global construction and its based-quotient theorem give a Z[q±]-basis of U_A^-v_lambda: each negative global basis element maps to the corresponding highest-module global element if its crystal image survives, and to0 otherwise (Kashiwara91 Theorem7(ii), Section7.5.2). Thus each finite weight lattice is actually free over A, with rank its field dimension. The early local-q1 deformation/universality theorem already proves the simple quantum module, field character and equality with the integrable Serre quotient using DVR-free lattices; it is not dependent on this global result. Base change of the newly proved integral weight basis preserves dimensions. Algebraic positive specialization and finite-support regularization identify the classical fibre and its character, and the classical Weyl-Kac theorem gives the explicit formula. Perfect-pairing/regularity/fundamental-weight hypotheses used by the sources are established by the actual auxiliary-datum lemma. This proves the stronger original global Z-lattice assertion without assuming it as a balanced-triple premise.

item.title: Schur functor images of standard, simple, projective and tilting objects
item.statement: For admissible origins, π(N(A)) is the intrinsic affine-induced Specht module S(A): its jth column contributes the Specht shape read from its nonnegative ground differences and evaluation at a_j=c_j+q_j−n, and the factors are induced along the affine Young subalgebra. π(K(A))=D(A) is simple for A∈Std and zero otherwise; Std labels give all distinct simples of the relevant Hecke image. For A∈Std, π(P(A)) is its projective cover Y(A) and π*π(P(A))=P(A). All ambient offStd projectives still have their genuine images, without a false projective-preservation assertion. Tilting images have the actual opposite-parabolic standard/Specht flag coefficients, and π is fully faithful on tiltings. For B∈Std, [S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):K(B)]=d_(B,A)(1), using the actual typed singular/parabolic coefficient conventions; B offStd is not a simple Hecke label. item.title: Self-dual indecomposable cyclotomic KLR projectives give the lower global basis
item.statement: For a symmetric Cartan datum normalized by $d_i=1$, over any characteristic-zero field, and the SAME finite loopless quiver with arbitrary edge multiplicities and $Q_{ij}=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$ as the generic global theorem, use the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand quotient and RIGHT append. Then, normalizing each indecomposable finitely generated graded projective $R(\beta)$-module to be self-dual for the contravariant graded projective duality $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$ ($P\cong P^\#$ after the unique normalizing shift), the map $b\mapsto[P_b]$ is a bijection between the lower global basis $B(\infty)$ of the negative half ([[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]]) and the shift-orbit basis of $K_0(R)$ by self-dual indecomposable projectives; under the isomorphism $\gamma$ of [[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]] one has $\gamma(G(b))=[P_b]$ for the lower global lift $G(b)$, and the identification is compatible with the based quotient of [[thm-global-basis-projection-from-the-negative-half-to-a-highest-weight-module]]. No extension to arbitrary KLR parameters or to non-symmetric Cartan data is asserted here; any such extension requires its own parameter-change invariance theorem.

Use the proved local quiver-flag semisimplicity corollary and signed Ext-realization theorem in the full finite loopless quiver scope, with arbitrary arrow multiplicities, normalized symmetric d_i=1 and any coefficient field k of characteristic zero. Put L_nu=R(pi_nu)!k[d_nu] and L=sum_nu L_nu. The semisimplicity corollary gives L as a finite direct sum of shifts of simple actual G-equivariant perverse objects. Its proof uses the explicit smooth projective finite-Borel compactification and one finite Stiefel model with r_N>=2f+dmax-dmin; the degree-zero End ring comparison uniquely lifts the finite orthogonal projectors, and bounded equivariant idempotent completeness plus normalized exact conservative perverse pullback reflects simple summands. item.statement: The Fock module has the ordinary compatible bar $\psi$ fixing each ordered fundamental wedge and built by the finite-product quasi-R construction. Weight transfer of a positive-first quasi-R term lowers the source tableau order; the divided-power action makes its coefficients integral. Terms with a new upper endpoint>r kill the prefix, since no such entry is present and positive operators cannot create one. At a new lower endpoint k−1 every prefix wedge already contains that entry; positive operators cannot remove its smallest entry, so all new-boundary terms kill the image. Old-root terms preserve the tail. The same reasoning applies to positive-root products by looking at their first boundary generator. Thus all local operators/bars agree on the double cuts. Involution, parenthesization independence and integrality descend from actual finite8, and every vector calculation stabilizes before taking the limit. item.statement: For admissible c the genuine Whittaker functor is exact on O_c^d, and γ:Hom_g(T,−)→Hom_W(V_c^tensor d,V(−)) is a natural isomorphism. T is a self-dual prinjective detecting object containing all Std-labelled projective-injective covers, not a generator of the entire O summand. V(T) is a projective generator of W_d-mod and V preserves projectivity on add(T). It need not send every O projective to a W_d-projective. Its composite with the Morita equivalence is the Serre quotient killing exactly offStd simples.
item.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Construct Z_A from finite column symmetric powers, embed it into V^tensor d by symmetrization and PBW induce. Split the last column and append its ground label: maximal physical-prefix inequalities force every possible larger polynomial label to retain that same ground column. Positive-radical invariants of a simple are its top Levi simple, proved using the nondegenerate contravariant form. Adjunction gives a single head; exact top centre sections and Levi BGG give the projective-cover character, so the lifted cover is an isomorphism. Induct over columns, then tensor the remaining finite symmetric powers. Specht-to-permutation dominance gives every projective cover once among these Z_A summands. The quotient T/Z_A has a standard flag, hence Std socle by actual16; its injective hull is in add(T). Thus every projective has a two-term add(T) copresentation. For the corner right adjoint G=Hom_B(eA,−), the unit on T is injective, splits by injectivity, and its torsion complementary summand vanishes by adjunction. Left exact G applied to a copresentation gives unit isomorphisms on every projective, proving full faithfulness. Modules with Std head and targets with Std socle give the same Hom argument, proving tilting faithfulness. Morita and the counit factorization give γ. The rank-one dominant Verma maps to a nonprojective simple over C[x]/x², while add(T) maps to projectives. The complete argument is Whittaker-quotient §§4–6, not the false full-generator inference.

item.title: Type-A parabolic category-O Ringel duality via the opposite parabolic
item.statement: Assume AC and the actual type-A tableau parabolic data. Let $\bar p$ have reversed Levi block order, conjugate to the opposite parabolic, with reverse-column labels. Use the parabolic outside-nilradical semi-regular bimodule and exact COVARIANT $F=D\Psi$ constructed by the local label helper. Then $F:\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\simeq\mathcal F(\nabla)$, $F(\bar M(A))=\nabla(A)$ and $F(\bar P(A))=T(A)$; the explicit highest-weight shifts cancel to the original column reading, so labels A and matching central-character blocks are preserved. Therefore the full-block Ringel dual is the opposite-parabolic block, and $(T(A):M(B))=[\bar M(B):\bar L(A)]$. For a proper original lower ideal $\Gamma$, its Ringel dual is the matching opposite HIGHEST-WEIGHT SERRE QUOTIENT by the complementary labels (an upper ideal in the opposite order), not the same Serre down-set subcategory. The filtered equivalence and projective/tilting corner construction give this compatible finite-ideal transport. No unchanged underived full-longest Borel twisting or equivalence on arbitrary category-O objects is asserted.
item.strategy: The earlier helper proves the actual bimodule actions, restricted free/cofree/finite-flag equivalence, variance and reverse-column shift. The tilting theorem proves ΨPbar(A)=T(A); self-duality then gives FPbar(A)=T(A). Comparing its costandard flag with opposite projective BGG and using tilting self-duality gives the displayed reciprocity. Since both filtered equivalences are fully faithful, End of the opposite projective generator is End of the characteristic tilting generator, with the stated opposite convention; finite projective presentations identify their module categories. For a target lower ideal, every T(A),A∈Γ has support≤A so remains in that Serre truncation unchanged. Its end algebra equals that of the corresponding sum of opposite full projectives. Hom from that sum is exact, kills precisely the complementary simples, is dense by projective presentations and realizes the Serre quotient as the corner eΓ Abar eΓ. Thus finite ideals pair with the actual opposite quotient; this retains proper-ideal richness without a false same-downset restriction. The block identification was proved by the explicit shifted-coordinate multiset, not an assumed source refinement.

item.title: Upper and lower global bases are dual and crystal compatible
item.statement:
For every finite root/label component of M=U^- or V(lambda), the restricted integral dual M_A^vee has the actual A-basis {G^up(b)} dual to {G(b)}, and B:(M_A^vee)_mu×(M_A)_mu→A is perfect. Globally these bases form direct sums; this means restricted graded perfectness, not identification with the full product Hom_A(M_A,A).
The dual charts are L0^vee=⊕A0G^up(b) and L∞^vee=⊕A∞G^up(b), and their balanced Z-intersection is ⊕ZG^up(b). Thus the dual triple is integrally balanced. At0, L0^vee=L0 and G^up(b) has residue b; at infinity its residue is the dual of the lower infinity-chart class in the dual infinity chart. The upper bar psi^vee fixes each G^up(b). The upper operators satisfy EXACT mixed adjunction B(f̃^low u,v)=B(u,ẽ^up v), B(ẽ^low u,v)=B(u,f̃^up v). Their reductions at0 equal the lower crystal operators and give the same crystal set B.
For a divided module string F_i^(n)v of top rank-one weight a, put d_(a,n)=q_i^(n(a−n))[a choose n]_i. Then ẽ_i^up at position n≥1 multiplies the preceding divided position by d_(a,n)/d_(a,n−1)=q_i^(a−2n+1)[a−n+1]_i/[n]_i, and f̃_i^up at position n<a multiplies the next by its reciprocal d_(a,n)/d_(a,n+1). For a half string with e_i′v=0, put d_n=q_i^(−n(n−1)/2)/[n]_i!=1/[n]_(q_i²)!; the corresponding ratios are d_n/d_(n−1)=1/[n]_(q_i²) and d_n/d_(n+1)=[n+1]_(q_i²). All admissible ratios are units≡1 in A0. Consequently unweighted lower adjunction holds modulo q, but generally not exactly over Q(q). No equality of upper and lower integral bases, even in symmetric type, is implied.
item.strategy:
Fix a finite component and its already-proved lower A-basis g_b=G(b). The field Gram matrix C=(B(g_b,g_c)) is invertible over Q(q), not asserted invertible over A. Define g_b^up using C^-1. For any x in the component, its coordinates in this dual field basis are exactly B(g_b,x). Hence x is in M_A^vee iff those coordinates are in A. This proves its genuine free A-basis and the perfect pairing with M_A, by the evaluation matrices delta; no A-unit determinant or lower self-duality is required. This is a finite proof in each degree, extended only by restricted direct sums.
The lower chart lattices have bases g_b over A0 and A∞ by integral globalization. The same coefficient criterion proves their dual chart bases g_b^up over the corresponding rings. Their triple intersection is Z-span because A∩A0∩A∞=Z. The exact integral dual globalization follows, with Q extension at each rational residue. Existing post-grand-loop Gram perfection identifies L0^vee=L0, and B(g_b,g_c)≡delta at0 implies g_b^up≡b there. At infinity, pairing with the lower infinity basis defines the actual dual residue; it does not assert congruence modulo q^-1 in the LOWER infinity lattice. Since psi g_b=g_b, the definition B(psi u,psi^vee v)=overline B(u,v) gives psi^vee g_b^up=g_b^up and transports the two dual charts.
For exact operators, extract finite divided strings. Different positions with different highest components are orthogonal: repeated E_i or e_i′ adjunction leaves a highest vector paired with a positive F_i power, hence0; at equal position the pairing is d_(a,n) or d_n times the top-component form. Therefore the adjoint of the normalized lower shift has precisely the displayed norm ratio, proving the exact MIXED adjunction. The module ratio equals (1−q_i^(2(a−n+1)))/(1−q_i^(2n)) after factoring powers, a unit with constant1 for 1≤n≤a. The half ratios are the displayed ordinary q_i² quantum integers and reciprocals, also units≡1. Thus the upper operators preserve L0, reduce to the same crystal actions and satisfy the same partial-inverse edge property. This is Kashiwara91§2.4’s distinction between lower and upper operators, combined with its§5.1 A0-perfection and the constructed global bases. No star-invariance argument is substituted for form-duality, no rank-one check is promoted to a general proof, and no full infinite-rank algebraic dual is invoked.

item.title: K_0 categorification alone does not identify the global basis
item.statement:
**Statement refuted:** once the isomorphism $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(\Lambda)$ of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]] is known, the classes of the word projectives $R^\Lambda(\beta)e(\nu)$ are automatically lower global basis vectors; in particular the K_0-level categorification alone identifies the global basis.
**Counterexample (rank two, $\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$).** Let $I=\{i\}$, $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2$, and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$. In weight $2\alpha_i$ the word projective is $R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)=NH_2/(x_1^2)$, which is not indecomposable: by the rank-one case of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]] it is a direct sum of $[2]_{q_i}!=(q+q^{-1})$ copies of the self-dual divided-power projective $P_{i,2}$, so its class is
$$[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=(q+q^{-1})\,[P_{i,2}].$$
Under $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(2\Lambda_1)$ the class $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]$ is the ordinary product $F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}$, while the lower global basis vector in weight $2\alpha_i$ is the divided power $F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}=F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}/[2]_{q_i}$; the two differ by the scalar $q+q^{-1}\notin\{\pm q^n\}$, so no K_0-level statement that only names the module $R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)$ and its class can decide between them. The lower global basis is picked out only by the additional structure: the self-dual shift normalization of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]], bar invariance, and the positivity of the divided-power coefficients, none of which is part of the bare $K_0\cong V_A(\Lambda)$ statement. The example also shows the true positive claim: the lower global class in weight $2\alpha_i$ is the class of the *indecomposable* projective $P_{i,2}$, not of the word projective.
item.strategy: Compute the two classes in the rank-one quotient and compare. (i) $NH_2$ has the PBW basis $\{x_1^ax_2^b,x_1^ax_2^b\tau\}$ and $NH_2\cong P_{i,2}^{\oplus[2]_{q_i}!}$ with $[2]_{q_i}!=(q+q^{-1})$ given by the polynomial-column decomposition (KL I Section 2.2 and Section 3.1, quoted in [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]); the cyclotomic quotient $R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)=NH_2/(x_1^2)$ is a finite-dimensional graded quotient in which the same projective cover decomposition persists with the shift centering $P_{i,2}$ (the projective decomposition is the rank-two case of the divided-power construction, with the cyclotomic quotient acting on the finitely many PBW classes), hence the displayed class identity. (ii) In $U^-_A(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ one has $F_i^2=[2]_{q_i}F_i^{(2)}$ by the definition of the divided power, so under the K_0 isomorphism the word class $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]$ corresponds to $[2]_{q_i}F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}$; the lower global basis vector is $F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}$ by [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] specialized to the rank-one module. (iii) The scalar $[2]_{q_i}=q+q^{-1}$ is not of the form $\pm q^n$; a rescaling of a basis vector by a non-unit is not a basis change over $A$, so the word class cannot be the global basis element in that weight, and no purely $K_0$-theoretic identification can produce the divided power without dividing by $[2]_{q_i}$. This refutes the stated claim and simultaneously records where the missing input lives: the self-dual normalization and positivity of the extension-of-scalars theorem. No AC is used.

item.title: Specializing the grading variable to one forgets graded decomposition information
item.statement:
Let $q$ be the grading variable and work in the rank-two $e=2$ block of [[ex-projective-versus-simple-grothendieck-classes-in-a-small-block]], where $[P]=(1+q^2)[D]$ and the graded Specht classes are $[S(1,1)]=[D]$, $[S(2)]=q[D]$. Then:

1. the Laurent polynomials $1+q^2$ and $2$ are distinct in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ but equal at $q=1$; correspondingly the graded classes $[P]=(1+q^2)[D]$ and $2[D]$ are distinct in $G_0^{\rm gr}$, while the forgetful map $\zeta$ of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]] sends both to $2[D]$;
2. the graded classes $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and $[S(2)]=q[D]$ are distinct in $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1})$, while the forgetful map $\zeta$ of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]] sends both to $[D]$; correspondingly the graded transition polynomials $d_{(1,1),(1,1)}(q)=1$ and $d_{(1,1),(2)}(q)=q$ are distinct in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ but equal at $q=1$. Thus the nonzero off-diagonal graded coefficient $q$ of the standard vector $S_{(2)}$ becomes invisible at $q=1$, where both standard vectors have the same ungraded decomposition data.

So no specialization $q\mapsto1$ determines the graded decomposition multiplicities, the graded Cartan entries or the shift classes; the graded information lives precisely in the $q$-degrees. This is a genuine failure of injectivity of the forgetful map, not a failure of well-definedness. No choice is used.
item.strategy: All statements are read off from the explicit rank-two computation of [[ex-projective-versus-simple-grothendieck-classes-in-a-small-block]] and the defining expansion $S_\mu=\sum_\lambda d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)D_\lambda$ of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]] (there $G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}$ gives $d_{(1,1),(1,1)}=1$, $d_{(1,1),(2)}=q$, hence $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and $[S(2)]=q[D]$ are distinct in $G_0^{\rm gr}$ but equal after $q\mapsto1$). The counterexample is a direct finite computation; no choice.

item.title: The degenerate cyclotomic Hecke tower and its residue functors
item.statement: Fix a nonempty consecutive I⊂Z, I^+=I∪(I+1), dominant finite-level Λ=sum_j Λ_mj with m_1≥…≥m_l in the admitted letter alphabet, and Q^+=sum_(i∈I)Z_≥0 alpha_i. Write H_d(m) for the full degenerate cyclotomic algebra. Its polynomial joint spectral projectors e(sequence) select generalized weight summands of arbitrary dimension. For alpha∈Q^+, ht(alpha)=d, put e_alpha=sum_(sequence∈I^d, content=alpha)e(sequence) and H_alpha^Λ=e_alpha H_d(m). Each nonzero content algebra is a SINGLE finite-dimensional block. The degree-d supported tower algebra is f_(I,d)H_d(m), f_(I,d)=sum_(sequence∈I^d)e(sequence); it can be a proper central cut of H_d(m). The locally unital tower is sum_alpha H_alpha^Λ. At level0 take H_0=C and H_d=0 for d>0. Its finite-module G0 has simple basis D(A), A∈Std_alpha, and its split projective K0 has cover basis Y(A), paired perfectly by dim Hom. Project the ambient tower map iota:H_d(m)→H_(d+1)(m) to the content alpha+alpha_i; its identity image is u_(alpha,i)=sum_(last residue=i)e(sequence). Residue restriction is u(−) and induction is H_(alpha+alpha_i)u tensor_(H_alpha)−. They are exact, biadjoint, commute with generator-fixing ordinary duality and shift the content by ±alpha_i. For positive level the ambient maps are the usual inclusions; the level0 convention is treated separately.
item.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Finite CRT spectral decomposition supplies e(sequence); symmetric Hermite/CRT polynomial projectors separate the finitely many multiset orbits and commute with the affine generators by the divided-difference relation, proving centrality of content sums. Do not infer primitivity from orbit sums alone. Realize the same charges stably with q_j=m_j+1−k≥d and common admissible origin c=m_1; n=q_1 gives c+q_j−n=m_j. The actual17 stable Hecke component equals End_O(T_alpha)^op. The actual16 fixed-content parabolic category is one linkage block. Choose a FULL projective generator Q containing T_alpha, set A=End_O(Q)^op and H=eAe. By actual17 ALL-projective full faithfulness, End_O(Q)=End_H(pi Q). Central h∈H acts naturally on pi Q; full faithfulness lifts it to Z(A), and restriction to pi T=H recovers h. A central lift vanishing on T vanishes on Hom(T,Q), hence on Q by faithfulness. Thus Z(A)=Z(H), so H has no nontrivial central idempotent and is one block. The actual17 contraction/corner proof shows every I-supported content survives the stable auxiliary enlargement: new bottom occupancy is maximal in all columns, top occupancy0, so all labels are contractible. This proves the supported statement without equating it with the whole degree. Exact residue maps/functors and duality are the actual17 supplier, restricted by these central cuts. Simple/projective bases and Hom duality use the declared finite-algebra Grothendieck suppliers. The focused proof §1 expands this complete missing centre argument; I={0},m=(0),d=2 has supported component0 although full H_2=C[S_2]. The commutative polynomial algebra satisfies the actual CRT supplier hypotheses: distinct spectral characters differ by a nonzero complex coordinate, so their maximal ideals and sufficiently high powers are pairwise comaximal; a finite uniform nilpotence bound gives the required projectors on the regular module.

item.title: The Drinfeld pairing between the positive and negative quantum halves
item.statement: Let B_K be the normalized Kashiwara half form and let ι:U^+→U^- send E_i↦F_i (equivalently use the library's signed Chevalley involution with the compensating degree sign). For x of positive degree nu and y of negative degree−nu define D(x,y)=d_nu^-1 B_K(ιx,y), d_nu=∏_i(q_i−q_i^-1)^nu_i, and set different-degree pairings0. Then D(E_i,F_j)=delta_ij/(q_i−q_i^-1), and D(E_i^(n),F_i^(n))=q_i^(−n(n−1)/2)/([n]_i!(q_i−q_i^-1)^n). The pairing with generator value1 is B_K transport, not this quasi-R/Drinfeld normalization. The completed normalized tensor uses the D-dual basis. On the simple-root Borel extensions its toral normalization is D(K_nu,K_mu)=q^((nu,mu)), with mixed toral/root generator pairings0 and counit normalization; the Hopf adjunction identities use Δ on the negative Borel and Δ^op on the positive Borel. item.statement:

u}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ for $\lambda,

u)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}a_{\lambda,
u}(q)[D(\lambda)]\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad a_{\lambda,
u}(q)=[J(
u):D(\lambda)]_q .$$ Then the matrix $(a_{\lambda,
u})$ is the graded adjustment matrix; its entries are bar-invariant, have nonnegative integer coefficients, satisfy $a_{
u,
u}(q)=1$ and vanish unless $\lambda\unlhd
u$ (dominance); equivalently $a_{\lambda,
u}$ is the coefficient of $[D(\lambda)]$ in $(\Psi_{m can}^{m Hecke})^{-1}(D_

item.strategy: Expand the actual finite-dimensional J(nu) in the shift-orbit basis of normalized positive-characteristic simples; this uniquely defines the Laurent coefficients and makes their coefficients nonnegative integers. The local CP comparison proves J(nu)=D(nu)+terms with smaller labels, giving diagonal1 and dominance support. J(nu) has this same character, and D_psi J(nu) has the inverted character, hence the same one. The actual extremal-word character detection implies equality of their G0 classes. item.title: The integral parabolic category-O blocks for higher-level Schur-Weyl duality
item.statement: Assume AC and $I$ bounded below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite (the upper end of $I$ may remain unbounded). Let classical $g=gl_n(\mathbb C)$ and the standard parabolic have Levi $gl_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus gl_{n_l}$. For the column reading $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ of $A$, set $\lambda_A=\sum_j(a_j+j-1)\varepsilon_j$ and let $L(A)$ be its simple highest module. Strict columns make this Levi-dominant, so the simple and the induced generalized standard $M(A)$ belong to genuine $O^p$. Use the published HALF-SUM convention $\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$. Then $\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+(n-1)/2$, so their $gl_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$; this labels the central character, together with the displayed scalar $gl_n$ centre. The Fock weight $\sum\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ belongs to the DIFFERENT $gl_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that multiset, not a literal gl_n highest weight. The corresponding finite parabolic central blocks $O^\Lambda_\alpha$ have labels $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$, projectives $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with BGG and restricted duality from15. Their simple/standard bases and numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central characters. The direct sum over these characters is $O^\Lambda$. Opposite blocks use reversed Levi order and reverse-column reading, with the corresponding reversed label order.
item.strategy: Finite Levi highest-weight classification applies to the derived Levi and the displayed scalar centre. PBW and the15 local-finiteness proof give the actual generalized standards; the same highest weights identify their heads and all admissible simples. The actual published Harish-Chandra supplier uses the half-sum rho, with HC_rho(z)(mu)=pr(z)(mu−rho) and central scalars evaluated at lambda+rho. For gl_n, rho_j=(n+1−2j)/2 has sum0, and lambda_j=a_j+j−1 gives lambda_j+rho_j=a_j+(n−1)/2. Thus the semisimple shifted Weyl orbit together with the trace-centre value is precisely determined by the sorted entry multiset. No undeclared full-staircase shift is used. The finite admitted parabolic labels in that integral orbit give the15 highest-weight category and character/Grothendieck bases; the preceding local linkage lemma proves SINGLE-block connectedness by actual two-column canonical coefficient1/indecomposable tilting edges and a complete fixed-margin switch argument, including saturated/common rows. This is the specific type-A result, not a generic consequence of a central-character decomposition. Reverse-column reading swaps Levi blocks and reverses prefix order, as computed in the semiregular label helper. No identification with projectively parabolic-presentable properly stratified objects is made.

item.title: The semi-infinite q-wedge Fock space and its q-adic topology
item.statement: For charge M form the algebraic direct limit of the finite wedge spaces by appending u_(M−N),u_(M−N−1),… to a prefix of length N. Equivalently quotient the eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Normal semi-infinite words have i_k=Lambda_k−k+1+M with Lambda a partition, and the vacuum is u_M∧u_(M−1)∧…. Let F_A=⊕_Lambda A|Lambda;M>, F0=⊕ A0|Lambda;M>, F_Z0=⊕ Z[q]|Lambda;M>. The full-field separated q-adic topology is induced by q^n F0, NEVER q^nF_A=F_A. A finite A0 label component completes to a Q[[q]] lattice, and its full-field component completes to Q((q)) tensor_Q(q)F_mu. Separately the finite Z[q] chart completes to a Z[[q]] lattice; that integral completion is not identified with Q((q)) or asserted to be a Q-vector topology. Fix j(M)∈{1,…,e}, M=j−ae. The vacuum P-weight Omega_M is normalized by Omega0=Lambda0 and Omega_M−Omega_(M−1)=wt(u_M). Explicitly if M=te+r,0≤r<e, Omega_M=Lambda_r−[e t(t−1)/2+t r]delta. A partition's weight is Omega_M−Σ_cells alpha_(content+M), and its size is a separate grading. The Cartan d eigenvalue is Omega_M(d) minus the number of residue0 cells, not partition size. No false Omega_M=Omega_(M−e)+delta periodicity is asserted.
item.strategy: Append the exact ground tail. If a finite word becomes nonnormal across the cutoff, integral straightening stays inside its index interval. A tail filled with every integer in that interval eventually forces any offending term to0; ordered words stabilize to the displayed beta-number partition words. Their independence follows from sufficiently large finite normal-basis independence. Thus the algebraic quotient/direct limit has this basis and Laurent/integral/local charts. In the A0 chart every nonzero finite coordinate has finite valuation, so the topology is separated; the A0 lattice completion is Q[[q]] and localization gives the full-field Laurent-series completion Q((q)); the separate Z[q] chart completion is Z[[q]]. The vacuum weights follow by adding one affine vector u_M; summing its loop power a(M)=(j−M)/e gives the explicit quadratic delta shift. This discharges charge rather than silently changing the full d-action. In charge0 Omega0=Lambda0 and residues remain c−r.

item.title: Stable range and block idempotent corner for higher-level Schur-Weyl duality
item.statement: Stable range means at least d Jordan strings have maximum length l, equivalently q_l≥d. For every c this makes the raw H_d(a) action injective. For admissible c outside this range, its image is a central block sum f H_d(a) f; f is the sum of the central blocks supporting contractible simple labels after enlarging all columns to a stable pyramid and deleting the added ground rows. Generalized-eigenvalue sequence idempotents e(i) are not individually central; f is a sum of entire central blocks. Nonadmissible c still has its genuine image algebra and full tensor double centralizer, but the same central-corner/Morita conclusion is not inferred without admissibility.
item.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. The longest-string vector proves stable injectivity on associated graded and hence the filtered algebra. To prove the central-corner clause, enlarge n and every q_j by r, preserving every root a_j; the added bottom entries are c_j+1−(n+k). Let e select degree0 on those rows. Ground minima plus fixed central content force all simple labels in a supporting block to be contractible, and highest-weight PBW shows e kills all other simple blocks. On a supported block, e of the enlarged tensor module is the original tensor module. The original graded first-centralizer argument identifies its W image with the e corner. Under the already-proved stable Morita equivalence this eM is a right progenerator exactly for the supporting central blocks, so its right annihilator is their complement and the image is fHf. Row support and cyclicity are proved by the expanded two-row/induction argument in Specht-corner §§3–4; do not assume e is itself central.

item.title: The level-one vector representation, its affinization and the energy function
item.statement: Use j=1,…,e as representatives (j=e represents0). The derived affine vector module V=⊕ Q(q)v_j has K_i v_j=q^(delta_(j≡i)−delta_(j≡i+1))v_j, E_i v_j=delta_(j≡i+1)v_(j−1), F_i v_j=delta_(j≡i)v_(j+1), indices cyclic. Its P_cl weight is Lambda_j−Lambda_(j−1), level0; its finite crystal has f_i b_i=b_(i+1), e_i b_(i+1)=b_i, epsilon(b_j)=Lambda_(j−1)^cl and phi(b_j)=Lambda_j^cl, level1. The full affinization has u_(j−ae)=z^a v_j of P-weight Lambda_j−Lambda_(j−1)+a delta and K_d eigen q^a. Equivalently E_i(z^a v_j)=delta_(j≡i+1) z^(a+delta_(i,0))v_(j−1), F_i(z^a v_j)=delta_(j≡i) z^(a−delta_(i,0))v_(j+1). Thus E_i u_m=delta_(m≡i+1)u_(m−1), F_i u_m=delta_(m≡i)u_(m+1). Ordinary order is u_m>u_n iff m>n. The energy is explicitly in the OPPOSITE tensor-crystal channel of KMPY bar-Delta-plus (opposite our fixed Delta): H_op(z^a b_j⊗z^b b_k)=chi(j>k)+b−a, and l(z^a b_j)=ae−j. It has the two loop-shift axioms, is constant on that channel's components, is0 on extremal diagonals and H_op>0 iff m1>m2. For a fixed charge M the ground sequence is b°_s=u_(M−s), s≥0: epsilon(b°_s)=phi(b°_(s+1)) and H_op(b°_s,b°_(s+1))=1. It is determined after the initial phase/loop vector (hence charge) is fixed, not independently of an overall loop shift. All statements include e=2.

item.title: Matching the canonical and lower global normalizations in rank one and $A_2$
item.statement:
In rank one the lower global/canonical vectors are exactly F_i^(n), bar fixed and congruent to their normalized crystal classes. Their Kashiwara norms are1/[n]_(q_i²)!, while the transported Lusztig norms are1/∏_(r=1)^n(1−q_i^(2r)); the full color factor is(1−q_i²)^−n. Ordinary F_i^n differs by the nonunit symmetric factorial, and Drinfeld generator normalization includes(q_i−q_i^-1)^−1. This explicitly matches, rather than conflates, the four conventions.
In type A2 degree alpha1+alpha2, the two lower global/canonical vectors are EXACTLY F1F2,F2F1, with no triangular correction. Their Kashiwara Gram matrix is[[1,q],[q,1]], already identity moduloq, and their transported Lusztig Gram is(1−q²)^−2 times this matrix. The Kashiwara upper dual vectors are(1−q²)^−1(F1F2−qF2F1) and(1−q²)^−1(F2F1−qF1F2); they are not the lower vectors. Lusztig form-duals are further multiplied by(1−q²)^2. In degree2alpha1 the lower vector isF1^(2), with the rank-one norm. These computations exhibit the actual convention dictionary and make no false Gram-unimodularity or unspecified correction claim.
item.strategy: Rank one is the unique divided string of1; the corrected balanced theorem gives exactly the divided lower lift, and the already-derived degree-color recursion gives both norms and the Drinfeld scalar. In degree alpha1+alpha2 there is no Serre relation, and e_1′F2=e_2′F1=0. Thus f̃1f̃2·1=F1F2 and f̃2f̃1·1=F2F1, integral/bar fixed with distinct crystal residues. Balanced uniqueness gives them as the exact lifts. Adjunction computes the two diagonals1 and the cross term q (e_1′(F2F1)=qF2), proving the displayed Gram matrix and determinant1−q². Its field inverse gives the two genuine Kashiwara upper duals, not an A-unit inverse. The form dictionary multiplies Gram by(1−q²)^−2 and therefore multiplies dual vectors by its reciprocal. The q0 residues of lower and upper agree, while their A lattices generally differ. The lower degree2alpha1 norm is the exact rank-one1/(1+q²). All displayed finite calculations are complete and consistent with the full canonical comparison supplier.

item.title: The charge-zero level-one crystal through rank four at e = 3
item.statement: At $e=3$, charge $\Lambda_0$, in the symmetric-group convention, the empty component through rank four has exactly the following vertices, one row per rank: rank $0$: $\varnothing$; rank $1$: $(1)$; rank $2$: $(2)$ and $(1,1)$; rank $3$: $(2,1)$ and $(1,1,1)$; rank $4$: $(3,1)$, $(2,2)$, $(2,1,1)$ and $(1,1,1,1)$. These are exactly the $3$-restricted partitions of each size ($1,1,2,2,4$ of them). The cogood-addition arrows staying within ranks0–4 are: $\varnothing\xrightarrow{\tilde f_0}(1)$; $(1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_1}(2)$, $(1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(1,1)$; $(2)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(2,1)$; $(1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_1}(1,1,1)$; $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_0}(2,2)$, $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(3,1)$; $(1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_0}(1,1,1,1)$, $(1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_1}(2,1,1)$; All other additions from ranks0–3 vanish; additions from rank4 leaving the displayed window are omitted, not declared zero. The good-deletion arrows into the listed ranks are: $(1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_0}\varnothing$; $(2)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_1}(1)$, $(1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_2}(1)$; $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_2}(2)$, $(1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_1}(1,1)$; $(2,2)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_0}(2,1)$, $(3,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_2}(2,1)$, $(2,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_1}(1,1,1)$, $(1,1,1,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde e_0}(1,1,1)$. In particular $(2,1)$ has no arrow of residue $1$ in either direction, and $(2,1)\xrightarrow{\tilde f_2}(3,1)$ is the arrow whose conjugate is the QG-6 Fock arrow $\tilde f_1$ from $(2,1)$ to $(2,1,1)$.
item.strategy: Finite verification by the reduced $i$-signature, hand-checkable at every vertex. Compute for each listed partition and each $i\in\{0,1,2\}$ the residues $c-r$, list the addable and removable $i$-nodes from top to bottom, cancel $-$ above $+$ pairs and read the topmost surviving $-$ and the bottommost surviving $+$. For example at $(1,1)$ and $i=1$ the two addable nodes $(1,2)$ and $(3,1)$ both survive, giving $\tilde f_1(1,1)=(1,1,1)$; at $(2,1)$ and $i=1$ the removable node $(1,2)$ lies above the addable node $(3,1)$ and the pair cancels, so $\varepsilon_1=\varphi_1=0$ and both arrows vanish; at $(2,1)$ and $i=2$ the addable node $(1,3)$ lies above the removable node $(2,1)$, the word $+-$ does not cancel, and $\tilde f_2(2,1)=(3,1)$, $\tilde e_2(2,1)=(2)$. Residue labels are $c-r$ as fixed in the convention item. The list of $3$-restricted partitions is the direct check of $\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<3$; the count $1,1,2,2,4$ matches the multiplicity of $V(\Lambda_0)$ (Leclerc, *Fock space representations of U_q(sl_n^)*, sec. 3.14, printed pp. 25-26, where the $n$-regular labels give the basic representation; the restricted reading is the transpose/sign dictionary of the convention item). No module theory is used beyond the vertex list of [[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]. The rank4 outgoing boundary is deliberately omitted; completeness/zero claims concern only ranks0–3. This derived finite signature calculation is not a claimed printed native source example.

item.title: Lower and upper global bases in a small highest weight module
item.statement: For rank-one V(m omega), use w_n=F^(n)v_m, 0≤n≤m, the lower global basis and lower integral lattice M_A=⊕A w_n. Its normalized polarization has B(w_n,w_s)=delta_ns d_(m,n), with d_(m,n)=q^(n(m−n))[m choose n]_q. Thus its upper form-dual global basis is w_n^up=d_(m,n)^−1w_n and M_A^vee=⊕A d_(m,n)^−1 w_n. These two explicit A-lattices are the object being compared; a numeric finite index is not presumed. For m=1, d=1 at both positions and the bases coincide. For m=2, d_(2,0)=d_(2,2)=1 and d_(2,1)=1+q², so M_A^vee=A w_0⊕A(1+q²)^−1w_1⊕A w_2, properly containing M_A. Its middle quotient is isomorphic to A/(1+q²). Both lattices extend to the same A0 crystal lattice and both basis residues are the same three crystal elements. The upper operators are the weighted adjoints from the duality theorem; their q0 reductions give the same finite string, while exact lower adjunction differs by the displayed norm ratios. The upper basis is fixed by the ADJOINT bar, generally not the ordinary lower bar.
item.strategy: Use the exact rank-one contravariant recurrence from the Cartan-projection/module-form supplier: E F^(n)v=[m−n+1]F^(n−1)v and sigma(F)=q^-1 K E give d_(m,n)=q^(m−2n+1)[m−n+1]/[n] times d_(m,n−1), with d_(m,0)=1. Iterating yields the stated Gaussian norm; distinct labels are orthogonal. Invert these field diagonal entries to obtain the genuine dual basis. For m=2 the middle norm is q[2]=1+q²; it is not a unit of A, so (1+q²)^−1w_1 is outside the lower lattice. The quotient of its coefficient module by A is isomorphic to A/(1+q²), exhibiting the actual pair of lattices rather than a misleading 'index of E'. At0 this norm is an A0-unit≡1; both basis residues agree. The finite-string ratio formulas then give the exact upper/lower adjoint operators and their modulo-q agreement. Ordinary bar fixes w_1 but sends its upper scalar denominator to(1+q^-2), so only the adjoint bar fixes w_1^up, exactly as the duality theorem states. All calculations are finite and choice-free apart from inherited general supplier assumptions.

item.title: The projective-simple Cartan pairing in a small cyclotomic block
item.statement: For rank one $d_i=1$, $\lambda=2$, let $B_r=R^\Lambda(r\alpha_i)$. The normalized simples are $S_0=k$, $S_1=k$ with $x=0$, and $S_2=C\{-1\}$ of graded dimension $q^{-1}+q$, where $C=k[x_1,x_2]/(x_1+x_2,x_1x_2)$. Their normalized projective covers are $P_0=k$, $P_1=k[x]/x^2$, $P_2=S_2$. Then $T(P_r,S_s)=\delta_{rs}$, with distinct roots paired by zero. Under the integral projective identification $P_0,P_1,P_2$ map to $v,Fv,F^{(2)}v$, respectively, while $[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[P_2]$ maps to $F^2v$. In $G_0$ the correct regular classes are $[B_1]=(1+q^2)[S_1]$ and $[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[S_2]$. The canonical restricted-dual map sends $S_r$ to the form-dual of the corresponding divided lower vector; it does not identify $B_1$ with $S_1$.
item.strategy: The preceding rank-one example supplies $B_1$ and the centered polynomial column for $B_2$. The first regular module has two composition factors $S_1,S_1\{2\}$, giving $1+q^2$. The second block is the endomorphism matrix algebra of the graded column $S_2$, so its regular left module is the column tensored with its graded vector dual: the latter has dimension $q+q^{-1}$, yielding the stated shifted-column decomposition in both groups. The normalized cover-to-head Hom space is $k$ in degree zero and there are no other simple types in a block; quotient-cover evaluation identifies its tensor pairing with this value. The divided-power idempotent identifies $P_2$ with the actual second divided induction, hence $[B_2]=[2]_q[P_2]$ and $F^2=[2]_qF^{(2)}$. This is a cover/simple pairing, not a Cartan matrix claimed to be all ones or a trace that removes a denominator. The integral and dual-module theorems give the stated two identifications.

item.title: Projective and simple Grothendieck classes in a small non-semisimple block
item.statement: Take $F=\mathbb C$, $\xi=-1$ (so $e=2$), level one $\Lambda_0$ and $d=2$. Then $H^\Lambda_2=H_{\mathbb C,-1}(S_2)$ with $T_1^2=-2T_1-1$, i.e. $(T_1+1)^2=0$; the algebra is $\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$ with $t=T_1+1$, a local algebra whose unique simple is $D=\mathbb C$ with $t$ acting as $0$, and whose regular module is the unique indecomposable projective $P=H^\Lambda_2$. Both partitions of $2$ have content $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ in the charge-$0$ convention, so $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ is the only nonzero block and $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}=\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$; its transported grading has $\deg t=2$ (the KLR block is the rank-two $e=2$ block $F[t]/(t^2)$ with $\deg y_2=2$). The graded Specht modules are the one-dimensional modules $S(2)=\mathbb C$ and $S(1,1)=\mathbb C$, both with trivial underlying action of $t$, and the graded composition series of $P$ is $0\subset tP\subset P$ with $tP\cong D\{2\}$, so $$[P]=(1+q^2)[D]\quad\text{in }G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}),\qquad [P]\notin\{[D],q^{\pm1}[D],\dots\}.$$ The restricted label is $(1,1)$ (since $(1,1)$ is $2$-restricted and $(2)$ is not), the edge degrees of the two shapes are $\deg(S(1,1))=0$ and $\deg(S(2))=1$, so the graded Specht classes are $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and $[S(2)]=q[D]$, and the level-one Fock data give $G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}$ and $G^*(1,1)=(M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)})/(1+q^2)$; hence under the transported identifications of [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] $$[P]\longmapsto G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}=(1+q^2)G^*(1,1),\qquad [D]\longmapsto G^*(1,1).$$ The graded Cartan pairing of [[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]] has $h([P],[D])=1$ and $h([P],[P])=1+q^2$, while the graded composition multiplicity is $[P:D]_q=1+q^2$ (ungraded value $2$). Thus the projective class $[P]$ is not a simple class, and the two bases are dual to each other under $h$ without being equal as classes. All computations are finite and explicit; choice is inherited only through the transported identifications cited.
item.strategy: Compute in the algebra: $T_1^2=(\xi-1)T_1+\xi=-2T_1-1$ gives $(T_1+1)^2=0$; the algebra $\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$ is local with radical $(t)$ and unique simple $D=\mathbb C$, and the regular module is the unique indecomposable projective because a local algebra has a unique simple and its regular module is projective; the graded composition series follows from $tP\cong D\{2\}$ (multiplication by $t$ shifts degree by $2$) and $P\cong D\oplus tP$ as graded vector spaces. The block statement uses the residue-content computation: nodes of $(2)$ have residues $0,1$ and nodes of $(1,1)$ have residues $0,-1\equiv1$, so both lie in the block of content $\alpha_0+\alpha_1=\alpha_1+\alpha_0$; the transported grading is [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]. The Fock identities are the explicit $e=2$ computation of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]] (its recorded $e=2$ example), the graded Specht degrees are read from the degree recursion of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]] (the unique tableau of $(2)$ has degree $d_A(2)=1$: the addable $1$-node $(2,1)$ lies strictly below the removable node $(1,2)$, and there is no removable $1$-node below it), and the projective/simple identifications are [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]]. The pairing values are read from $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,D)=\mathbb C$ and $\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,P)=1+q^2$ (endomorphisms are the identity and multiplication by $t$, of degree $2$). No choice.

item.title: The balanced-triple linear algebra over $\mathbb P^1$
item.statement:
For finite-dimensional V over Q(q), let M⊂V be an A=Z[q,q^-1]-submodule spanning V and L0,L∞ full free A0,A∞ lattices. Write E=M∩L0∩L∞. (1) If E→(M∩L0)/(M∩qL0) is a Z-isomorphism, then M∩L0≅Z[q]⊗_Z E, M∩L∞≅Z[q^-1]⊗_Z E and M≅A⊗_Z E; the infinity residue map is also an isomorphism. Rational chart extension gives A0⊗_Z E≅L0 and A∞⊗_Z E≅L∞. If E has a finite Z-basis, these are actual free bases. No containment M⊂L0∩L∞ or freeness of M/E is assumed.
(2) If a Z-module F maps into M∩L0∩L∞, generates M over A, and maps injectively into both rational residues L0/qL0 and L∞/q^-1L∞, then F≅E≅(M∩L0)/(M∩qL0).
(3) More generally let N⊂M be an A-submodule with integral balanced intersection E_N=N∩L0∩L∞. If a Z-module F maps to M∩(L0+N)∩(L∞+N), generates M modulo N over A, and maps injectively into (L0+Q N)/(qL0+Q N) and (L∞+Q N)/(q^-1L∞+Q N), then M is balanced. The sequence 0→(N∩L0)/(N∩qL0)→(M∩L0)/(M∩qL0)→(L0+Q N)/(qL0+Q N) is exact, and the last image is the image of F. If F and E_N are finite free Z-modules, so is E_M, and M is free over A. These are Kashiwara91 Lemmas7.1.1–7.1.2, in integral notation; their rational base extension gives the usual Q[q±] criterion.
item.strategy:
(1) E injects into the rational residue by the hypothesis, hence is Z-torsionfree. Residue surjectivity gives M∩L0⊂Σ_(k=0)^n q^k E+M∩q^(n+1)L0 for every n, by repeatedly subtracting a lift and dividing by q (which preserves M). For x also in q^nL∞, the subtracted terms k≤n lie there; the remainder is in q^n(M∩qL0∩L∞)=0 by residue injectivity on E. Thus M∩L0∩q^nL∞=⊕_(k=0)^n q^kE. Every element of M∩L0 has a finite infinity-pole bound, so the union over n gives Z[q]E. Distinct powers are independent: in a finite relation normalize the lowest exponent and reduce modulo q, then successively remove it. Also M=Z[q±](M∩L0) by finite zero-pole bounds. The analogous infinity-pole argument gives Z[q^-1]E and the mirror residue isomorphism. Since M spans V, Q(q)E spans V; rational residue injection shows a Q-basis of QE is independent and full. Expanding in that basis, zero/infinity valuation gives the full chart extension identities. Freeness over A is claimed only if E is actually finite free over Z.
(2) Laurent expansions in phi(F) have unique finite coefficients: reduce the lowest exponent at0 using the first injection. If an expansion lies in L0 it has no negative exponent; if it lies in L∞ it has no positive exponent, by the second injection. Therefore the intersection is exactly phi(F), with the claimed residue map and factorization. This is finite Laurent linear algebra, not passage to an unjustified formal limit.
(3) Work first on each finitely generated submodule F′ of F; its rational residue injection implies Z-torsionfreeness and hence finite Z-freeness. The balanced factorization of N gives N=(N∩L0)+(N∩L∞). If x∈M∩(L0+N)∩(L∞+N), subtract an element of N to put it in L0. Its remaining discrepancy from L∞ lies in N; split that discrepancy into its zero and infinity chart parts, then subtract its zero chart part to obtain an element of M∩L0∩L∞. Thus the lifts of a finite Z-basis of F′ can be changed by N so that they lie in the simultaneous intersection. Their direct sum with E_N injects into each rational residue: in the quotient modulo QN the F′ component is forced0 by the assumed injection, and then E_N injectivity forces the remaining component0. They generate AF′+N over A. Apply (2) to obtain balancedness and the exact residue sequence there. Taking the union over finite F′ proves the general assertion, without claiming an infinite torsionfree Z-module is free. When F and E_N are finite free, the direct sum description gives E_M finite free. This reproduces the printed diagrams and avoids the native unsupported chart containment, wrong q^nL0/q^nL∞ recursion and coherent-sheaf freeness shortcut.

item.title: Cyclotomic projective covers and dualities descend through the quotient
item.statement: Let $A=R(\beta)$ and $B=A/J$ be the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient. For an indecomposable finite graded projective generic cover $P(S)$, $B\otimes_A P(S)$ is its same-head indecomposable $B$-cover if $JS=0$, and is zero otherwise. Every graded simple/indecomposable projective $B$-orbit arises this way, and distinct surviving heads do not merge. Finite projective Hom duality commutes with this basechange, and finite vector duality commutes with inflation. Thus generic normalized $\#$-self-dual covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual simples supply unique normalized $B$-covers/simples. For these labels $h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)$ and $T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_B S)$ are both $\delta_{P,S}$; $T$ is bilinear and $h$ first-bar sesquilinear. Extension induces a surjection on projective $K_0$. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal premise is used.
item.strategy:
Tensor a shifted-free retract to prove finite projectivity. Every degree-zero endomorphism of $B\otimes P$ lifts through $P\to B\otimes P$ by generic projectivity; endomorphisms preserve $JP$, so this is a surjective endomorphism-ring homomorphism. Its domain is local for indecomposable $P$, hence a nonzero quotient is indecomposable. If $JS=0$, the old cover factors through $P/JP$ and remains essential: pull back a submodule and use the old superfluous kernel. If $JS\ne0$ and $P/JP\ne0$, finite dimension supplies a simple quotient, which must be the old unique head $S$, contradicting its being annihilated by $J$. Every $B$-simple inflates to a generic simple; its descended cover therefore exhausts the projective basis, proving surjectivity and no merging.
For finite $P$, evaluation on a shifted-free module and restriction to retracts gives $\operatorname{HOM}_B(B\otimes P,B)=\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,A)\otimes_A B$. Applying $\psi$ gives $(B\otimes P)^\#=B\otimes P^\#$. Inflation does not change $D_\psi S$. Use only the choice-free finite-module normalization clauses of the generic positive-divided-string supplier. They yield the unique self-dual representatives; no conditional quantum-global clause is used.
Finally $h(P,S)=T(P^\#,S)$ by finite-projective evaluation and $D(P^\psi\otimes S)=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,D_\psi S)$ by evaluation of a tensor functional. A normalized cover has $h(P,S)=q^a$ because absolute $\operatorname{End}(S)=k$. Both dualities fix the normalized labels, so $q^a=q^{-a}$ and $a=0$. Other simple heads have zero Hom. Shift-orbit bases now make both normalized pairings perfect. This proof distinguishes projective Hom duality from vector duality and never uses a symmetric trace.

item.title: Homogeneous dual-basis sums: basis independence and weightwise finiteness
item.statement: For a field basis u_a of U^+_nu and its D-dual basis v_a of U^-_-nu, the tensor Θ_nu=Σ_a u_a⊗v_a is independent of the chosen basis and Θ_0=1. It has finite-dimensional components and defines a vectorwise finite action under the exact root-height finiteness hypotheses of the completion Definition. Its degree-nu action shifts the label pair (mu,eta) to(mu+nu,eta−nu), preserving total weight. On finite-weight O_int pairs each fixed total-weight space has a uniform finite tail bound. No integral algebra coefficients are asserted; the positive-height components have no same-weight-pair diagonal term.

item.title: The quasi-$R$ intertwiner determines its inverse and the coproduct factorizations
item.statement:
In the same positive-first/negative-second completion, Θ^-1=barΘ=(psi⊗psi)(Θ). For every nu the exact threefold identities are
(Δ⊗id)Θ_nu=Σ_(gamma+eta=nu)(Θ_gamma)_23(1⊗K_-eta⊗1)(Θ_eta)_13,
(id⊗Δ)Θ_nu=Σ_(gamma+eta=nu)(Θ_gamma)_12(1⊗K_eta⊗1)(Θ_eta)_13.
The two normalized tensor-bar compositions satisfy the field cocycle identity ((Δ⊗id)Θ)Θ_12=((id⊗Δ)Θ)Θ_23, coefficientwise in the transported source completion and on every vector for which the iterated actions are finite. The inverse does not switch positive/negative tensor order. Removing Θ_0=1 permits scalar multiples of the same linear intertwiner equation, so normalization is essential. No integrality or uncontrolled infinite evaluation is asserted. The bar-coproduct counterpart needed for the cocycle is (id⊗barΔ)Θ_nu=Σ_(gamma+eta=nu)(Θ_gamma)_13(1⊗K_-gamma⊗1)(Θ_eta)_12.
item.strategy:
The bar of the intertwining equation gives barΔu·barΘ=barΘ·Δu. The product ΘbarΘ has zero component1 and commutes with ΔU. Equivalently the inverse, recursively defined in the positive root-height convolution algebra from Θ_0=1, has bar of itself satisfying the same normalized intertwiner equations as Θ. The established uniqueness therefore identifies the inverse with barΘ, exactly Lusztig4.1.3. No inverse in an opposite tensor completion is invented.
For the coproduct identities, follow the complete printed4.2.2 computation: expand the twisted half coproduct r(b)=Σ f(b,b1,b2)b1⊗b2 and its bar version, expand each coevaluation, and pair against arbitrary homogeneous basis tensors. Multiplication/coproduct adjunction of the half form identifies the paired coefficients with those of b1b2; the bar-twisted coproduct coefficient relation from§1.2.11 reverses their order with the precise root q-power. Toral commutation converts that power to K_±eta in the MIDDLE factor. Under v=q^-1, K_L↦K_K^-1 and threefold tensor reversal, the source4.2.2(a,b) give exactly the displayed orders/indices; at degree alpha_i they read ΔE_i⊗F_i and E_i⊗ΔF_i, fixing the indices. This pairing against a finite tensor basis is a complete degreewise proof.
The full source4.2.3 applies Δ to ΘbarΘ=1 and uses the paired coproduct expansions to obtain (id⊗barΔ)Θ_nu=Σ_(b+c=nu)Θ_b13 K_-b^(2) Θ_c12, with K^(2) in the middle tensor position, after the exact convention map. Now the LEFT cocycle expression ((Δ⊗id)Θ)Θ12 expands by the already-proved Δ identity as Σ_(a,b,c)Θ_a23 K_-b^(2) Θ_b13 Θ_c12. The RIGHT expression ((id⊗Δ)Θ)Θ23 equals Θ23((id⊗barΔ)Θ), by intertwining applied in positions23 to every negative-half coefficient. The counterpart identity expands it as Σ_(a,b,c)Θ_a23 Θ_b13 K_-b^(2) Θ_c12. These expressions are identical because a middle-position K commutes with Θ_b13. For fixed outer root degrees, b+c and a+b are fixed, so the possible a,b,c form a finite set; the coefficient calculation involves no uncontrolled infinite rearrangement. This is the complete transported4.2.4 argument and proves field parenthesization independently of integral action. In the highest-module setting the same identity can be checked without formal manipulation: both composite bars are U-compatible, agree on v_lambda⊗m⊗n (the first highest kills all positive root terms), and induction on the first negative divided-word height using ΔF^(r)'s coefficient1 term forces agreement everywhere. Finiteness is verified before evaluating any completed identity. Finally, the linear intertwining equations are homogeneous, so scaling Θ scales its zero component and gives precisely the claimed unnormalized family.

item.title: Reduction of characteristic-zero simple modules modulo p
item.strategy: Apply [[lem-rational-garnir-annihilator-lines-present-the-specified-specht-generator]] to the specified LEFT Murphy cell module and its initial homogeneous cyclic generator. Its finite integral row-permutation crossing matrices define a rational simultaneous Garnir-annihilator line; the strict crossing filtration proves standard spanning, and the actual homogeneous standard basis proves generator-preserving scalar-extension equality. It factors through the finite integer cyclotomic algebra by faithful rational scalar extension. Then [[lem-integer-cyclic-presentation-descends-the-simple-head-generator-line]] identifies the radical by the regular trace pairing, proves rational radical base change, and descends the specified simple head and initial-generator image. Absolute Schur makes every quotient map to the fixed normalized head differ only by a scalar. Thus the special vector lies in a scalar multiple of this proved rational form. No arbitrary-vector rational descent, KMR brick identity, or ordinary DJ comparison is used in this lattice step. The integer algebra orbit is finitely generated and torsion-free by the integral algebra theorem, spans the rational head by cyclicity, and is homogeneous; hence it is a full lattice of rank equal to the K-dimension. Word idempotents give graded direct summands, whose ranks survive tensoring with F, proving equality of graded word characters. Any other full homogeneous stable lattice has those same word-component ranks; the actual extremal-word character lemma proves G0 injectivity, so its reduction has the same G0 class. No assertion that all arbitrary K-lattices are literally commensurable without a rational/scalar identification is needed. Finally the restricted Specht classes are an A-basis of the UPPER dual lattice, have field-independent characters, and map under the corrected canonical identification to the same pi(M_mu). Character injectivity therefore shows that modules of equal characters over the two fields have equal images under Psi_can. Apply this to J(lambda) and the normalized characteristic-zero simple and invoke the characteristic-zero upper-basis theorem, proving part(3). No new choice beyond the declared sources.

item.title: Semi-infinite wedges are indexed by partitions and the action gives the node formulas
item.statement:
Normal charge-M wedges are indexed bijectively by partitions Lambda through i_k=Lambda_k−k+1+M; at M=0 the vacuum is the empty partition. Define the linear endomorphisms by stable finite-prefix action. In charge0,
F_i|lambda>=Σ_(addable gamma resi) q^(A_i^r−R_i^r)|lambda+gamma>,
E_i|mu>=Σ_(removable gamma resi) q^−(A_i^l−R_i^l)|mu−gamma>,
where both counts for E use the SMALLER partition mu−gamma and exclude gamma. All sums are finite. K_i acts by q^(addable_i−removable_i), and K_d by q^−m0(lambda); size|lambda| is separate. ChargeM replaces residues by content+M and d byOmega_M(d)−m0. This item constructs the operators/formulas before proving their full quantum relations, avoiding the native backwards proof cycle.
item.strategy: For N>length(lambda), all tail indices are consecutive. The finite F coproduct shifts a selected entry i_k to i_k+1; if it collides with the previous entry it is0, otherwise it is exactly addition of a corner cell of residue i_k. Frozen doubly occupied i-pairs have total K weight0; singly occupied pairs are the addable/removable corners, so the prefix K exponent is exactly the signed count at larger content. For E, finite prefix action shifts i_k to i_k−1; its suffix K^-1 counts smaller content. A finite cutoff has one artificial boundary pair; renormalize E by q^−delta_(i≡M−N) and discard its duplicate-tail term. Appending one more vacuum entry changes precisely this boundary scalar, so the operator is cutoff-independent. Equivalently use the full wedge/tail coproduct with the highest tail K scalar. This gives the SMALLER-diagram left count and correct minus sign. Each ordinary endomorphism has a finite stable sum; its weight shift and d-action are read from the explicit affine labels. Leclerc§3.8–3.10 complete formulas(35)–(39) are actually read; no quantum-relation theorem is used as a prerequisite for this construction.

item.title: The Drinfeld pairing is nondegenerate in each root degree and matches the shuffle pairing
item.statement: The normalized D pairing is homogeneous, descends to the actual Serre halves and is nondegenerate/perfect over Q(q) in every finite root degree. Its rank-one values are those of the preceding Definition, with the factor(q_i−q_i^-1)^−n. Thus D(xx′,y)=ΣD(x,y_(1))D(x′,y_(2)) and D(x,yy′)=ΣD(x_(1),y)D(x_(2),y′), with Δy on the negative Borel and Δ^opx on the positive Borel, including their toral factors. item.title: The local affine-Hecke socle argument for residue translations
item.statement: Assume AC and the preceding positive biadjoint residue $sl_2$/local degenerate affine-Hecke action. At a coincident eigenvalue the completed affine-Hecke algebra on r steps is $Mat_{r!}$ over the completed symmetric polynomial centre. The first-i image in its central fibre is $Mat_{i!}(Z_{i,r})$, where $Z_{i,r}=\mathbb C[c_1,\ldots,c_i]/(h_{r-i+1},\ldots,h_r)$ is a finite local complete-intersection Frobenius ring of dimension $\binom ri$ and one-dimensional socle. Divided residue functors and the complementary-idempotent restriction have the corresponding simple head/socle. Consequently $e_iL(A)$ and $f_iL(A)$ are either0 or self-dual indecomposables with simple isomorphic head and socle labelled $\tilde e_iA$ and $\tilde f_iA$, respectively. Vanishing is exactly absence of that crystal edge. This retains the complete residue-translation crystal claim, not only its K0 action.
item.strategy: Use polynomial representation T_j=s_j−partial_j, partial_j=(1−s_j)/(x_j−x_{j+1}); PBW follows by ordered spanning and leading permutation independence after localization. At the coincident completion, partial_j=(x_j−x_{j+1}+1)^−1(1−T_j), with LEFT inverse. Polynomial multiplication and longest divided difference give the relative perfect trace; reduction is the actual coinvariant Frobenius pairing, and complete-local Nakayama gives every matrix unit. The trivial/sign symmetric-group idempotents have fibre rank1: divided-difference terms lower degree and the diagonal character is the regular coinvariant character; idempotent splitting and Nakayama lift rank1. Partial elimination of remaining elementary coefficients gives the displayed h-relations. Their only common zero is0, since vanishing of i consecutive h's and their recurrence makes the reciprocal elementary series polynomial, hence constant. Nullstellensatz makes the quotient finite; polynomial Cohen–Macaulayness and the actual system-of-parameters theorem give regularity, globally by homogeneous localization. Koszul Hilbert series yields dimension binomial(r,i); the variable and h Koszul resolutions compute a unique socle in degree i(r−i). Thus no Grassmannian/Poincare theorem is imported. The ordered partial ring is free of rank i! over this centre and has dimension r!/(r−i)!, by successive monic distinguished-root equations. PBW group cosets and this basis prove the restriction freeness; the complementary idempotent removes (r−i)! multiplicity and leaves the indecomposable projective over Mat_{i!}(Z), with simple head/socle. These are the full algebraic steps of CR3.2–3.3/3.6. In the positive simple-class basis the sl2 string-height filtration is stable; biadjunction prevents a socle/head summand of E^jS from having lower maximal string height than S. At an extremal simple FS=0, E^(r)S is a single opposite-extremal simple by finite sl2 string theory/positivity. The Hecke action on E^rS has multiplicity module K_r; complementary restriction forces the socle/head of E^(j)S simple, since no maximal-height summand is killed by E^(r−j). Dimension comparison gives binomial(r,j) leading multiplicity and smaller-height other factors. For a general S take an extremal quotient of F^(h_minus)S and use adjunction to embed S in its divided translate; the opposite extremal translate is a sum of one simple, and the adjoint Hom into its simple socle bounds its multiplicity by1. This proves CR5.20 without importing it as a black box. Source Fock L is the balanced SOURCE upper-chart family. Kashiwara93§5.1 proves kernels of powers spanned by the global vectors with bounded epsilon (apply the maximal string power and balanced injectivity); §5.2 finite sl2 highest-string filtration is balanced by isolating a maximal constituent and annihilator test, whose remainder lies in the zero triple intersection. Thus in each associated string fG=[phi]G(tilde f) and eG=[epsilon]G(tilde e), and all other constituents have smaller corresponding height. The actual upper/lower string definitions in§3, the two source-positive coefficient charts and the typed reverse pairing verify these hypotheses; this is not the library8 adjoint-bar family by fiat. The full source5.3.1 proof uses the upper divided-string expansion and kernel-spanning induction to lift that leading term. At1, comparing with the preceding categorical unique maximal-height factors gives precisely the stated tableau labels. Commuting restricted duality makes head and socle equal and gives self-duality; one simple socle forces indecomposability.

item.title: Parabolic semi-regular duality and the reverse-column label map
item.statement: For a lower-bounded Fock tableau shape, set n_j=m_j+1−inf(I), n=sum n_j and lambda_A,j=a_j+j−1 from its finite column reading. These data define the genuine finite integral parabolic CENTRAL SUMMANDS by the structural category of15; no connectedness is assumed. Assume AC. For the reversed-block standard parabolic $\bar p\subset gl_n$, grade simple Levi roots by0 and outside roots by1, so $g_0=\bar l$, $g_{<0}=\bar u^-$ and $\gamma=2\rho_g-2\rho_{\bar l}$ is a Levi character. There is the explicit semi-regular $U(g)$-bimodule $S_{\bar u,\gamma}=U(\bar u^-)^\#\otimes U(\bar p)$, with the two PBW module identifications. Tensor/Hom give inverse exact equivalences on finite-rank graded free/cofree $U(\bar u^-)$ objects. Restricted contragredient dual and $c(X)=-w_0X^tw_0$ give an exact CONTRAVARIANT equivalence $\Psi$ from finite generalized-standard flags for $\bar p$ to those for $p$. The Levi highest-weight map is $\lambda_{\bar A}\mapsto-w_{\bar J}\lambda_{\bar A}-2\rho_{\bar u}$, then $-w_0$; in reverse/original column readings it gives $a_i+i-1$, so $\Psi(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\Delta(A)$. BGG restricted duality $D$ gives the COVARIANT equivalence $F=D\Psi$ from opposite standard flags to target costandard flags, with $F(\bar\Delta(A))=\nabla(A)$. It preserves the corresponding central blocks and reverses the label order. item.title: Type-A tableau central summands are single linkage blocks
item.statement: Assume AC. For the Fock shape $n_1\ge\cdots\ge n_l$ (the original nonincreasing-charge hypothesis) and any admitted integral entry multiset, the genuine $gl_n$ parabolic central summand labelled by its strict-column tableaux is a SINGLE linkage block. The same holds for its reverse-column/reversed-Levi counterpart. This includes repeated-entry singular ambient characters. The proof uses actual indecomposable generalized standards and locally constructed tiltings: adjacent-column positive exclusive-pair canonical coefficients specialize to1, so those labels lie in a common actual linkage block; these edges connect the whole fixed-margin binary tableau fiber. No future higher-Schur/cyclotomic-centre theorem is imported.
item.strategy: Do not presume connectedness. Work in the actual15 finite highest-weight central summand, possibly a product, and use the earlier parabolic standard-flag equivalence Psi. Put X(B)=Psi(Pbar(B)). Its standard flag has labelB once at the bottom and onlyA<B otherwise, by opposite BGG/order reversal. Projectivity makes Ext1(Delta,X)=0, so the independently proved generic criterion makes X tilting. Both X andDX have the same maximal normalized flag; extending the bottom inclusion both ways and finite local-End/Fitting proves selfduality. Thus (X(B):M(A))=[barM(A):barL(B)]. To identify these coefficients with SOURCE T at1, use the direct tensor/wedge matrix bridge: sortingw is shortestRIGHT in the ENTRY stabilizer and d=w^-1 shortestLEFT. Pure tensor Hecke generator action and the reverse-position complementary-chart pairing (sourceB1§4, with reciprocal parameter) identify tensor d(1) with spherical P_{d(C)w0,d(A)w0}(1), exactly15singular ordinary multiplicities. Finite Levi Weyl cancellation gives the signed column-permutation expansion of genuine generalized standards. Source-positive wedge embedding sends its L to tensorL by ordinary-bar and triangular uniqueness, hence the same signed matrix is the actual parabolic d. Apply this also in reverse columns. The typed C(tildeL,T)=delta gives (X(B):M(A)) equal to the coefficient of M(A) in source T_B at1. All this concerns central SUMMANDS, so invokes neither connectedDefinition nor later16Ringel/tilting theorem. Now independently construct the two-column canonical coefficient: CWZ0409016§4.3–4.4 defines disjoint positive pairs (left exclusive b>right exclusive a), chosen by increasing b−a distance and discarding previously used endpoints. With q=t=s^-1 its normal wedge action/coproduct equals this library/source dictionary. The source3case Procedure4.11 reduces to a typical tuple with no positive pairs; its monomial is ordinary-bar fixed since every positive-first quasi-R correction would need an exclusive b>a pair. In the reduction steps the explicit wedge Chevalley formulas give either K_f alone or K_f+qK_swapped. Each Chevalley generator is bar fixed. The recursion terminates lexicographically in the number of matched pairs and the sum of their distances: losing a pair lowers the first measure, and retaining the pairs moves only the selected endpoint inward. The source Lem4.14 induction therefore gives a bar-fixed qZ[q]-triangular vector; uniqueness identifies the canonical vector. Its3cases prove U_f=sum_{Sigma subset greedy positivepairs}q^{#Sigma}K_{fSigma}. Distinct subsets change distinct exclusive entries, so each single-pair coefficient is EXACTLYq. This is a complete two-factor proof, not a super-duality conjecture. For adjacent columns in a larger tensor, endpoints agreeing outside those columns have identical outer prefix weights. Every tableau in their Bruhat interval has those same outer prefix weights. Parenthesize with the pair as one factor: a positive transfer across an outer boundary would strictly change a prefix weight and cannot be cancelled by further positive transfers. Thus the interval bar matrix, and by triangular correction its canonical coefficient, equals the two-column matrix. At1 a greedy-pair edge gives (X(B):M(A))=1; indecomposable X(B) has both simple heads as composition factors, so A,B lie in the SAME actual original block. Opposite BGG gives [barM(A):barL(B)]=1, and barM(A) also has headbarL(A), so the same edge connects the opposite blocks. To connect all labels, identify a tableau with the0/1 incidence matrix of which entry values occur in each column; row margins are entry multiplicities and column margins are n_j. Two such matrices differ by alternating cycles in their bipartite symmetric difference. A long cycle splits by a chord: if the chord is0 flip the smaller4cycle first, otherwise flip the complementary shorter cycle first; induction flips the entire cycle while restoring the chord. Hence arbitrary valid2x2 switches connect the fiber. Reduce a switch between nonadjacent columnsS,U through the next intermediate columnT. IfT has onlya or onlyb, two switches with shorter column distance suffice. IfT contains botha,b, choose c inS\T: it exists because |S|>=|T| andT\S containsb. Perform c↔b betweenS,T, a↔b betweenT,U, thena↔c betweenS,T, restoringT and making the desired S/U switch. IfT contains neither, choosec inT\U (exists |T|>=|U| andU\T containsb), and use c↔b betweenT,U, a↔b betweenS,T, thena↔c betweenT,U. Induct distance; all switches remain binary and preserve margins. Sorted ORIGINAL heights justify precisely these cardinal comparisons. Finally any adjacent-column switch lies in a fixed two-column union/intersection fiber. Repeatedly swapping a greedy positive pair strictly lowers its inversion order until the unique configuration with all left-exclusive values below right-exclusive values; hence all such fibers connect through the already-proved coefficient1 edges. Combining the paths proves original and opposite linkage connectedness. This supplies the full promised singleblock result without merely asserting a shuffle graph or importing future17/18 centre-surjectivity.
