item.title: The module Grothendieck group is the dual integral highest weight module
item.statement:
For the same standard homogeneous general-field/general-Cartan parameters as the integral projective theorem, the tensor pairing $T(P,M)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes M)$ is weightwise perfect and $A$-bilinear, with normalized cover/simple dual bases. Its associated map
$$\Psi_{\rm can}:G_0(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow V_A(\Lambda)^\vee=\bigoplus_\beta\operatorname{Hom}_A(V_A(\Lambda)_{\Lambda-\beta},A),\qquad \Psi_{\rm can}(M)(\phi(P))=T(P,M)$$
is an isomorphism to the RESTRICTED weight dual, identified inside $V(\Lambda)$ using the highest-weight contravariant form. It intertwines the CANONICAL module action having the same normalization as projective $K_0$, and sends normalized simple classes to the form-dual projective basis. The KK module action is also sound, but its intertwiner is $\Psi_{\rm KK}|_\beta=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}\Psi_{\rm can}|_\beta$. Thus an unrescaled KK identification is not asserted to send simples to the upper global basis. The Hom pairing is instead first-bar-sesquilinear, $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$; this does not alter the bilinear tensor-dual identification.
item.strategy:
1. Finite blocks have finitely many absolutely simple graded shift orbits and normalized projective covers, by the quotient-cover lemma. Exactness of projective tensor pairing and the unscaled diagonal values give perfectness over $A$ on each weight. Consequently $G_0$ is free with these simple classes, and the functional map is an isomorphism to the weightwise dual of $K_0$. Take the DIRECT SUM over weights, not the full unrestricted product dual.
2. Transport $K_0$ by $\phi$. Its tensor form is the actual highest-weight contravariant form with $\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$. From tensor adjunction, $T(P,F_i^{\rm basic}M)=T(E_i^{\rm basic}P,M)=T(\sigma(F_i)P,M)$; the analogous normalized $E_i$ identity is $T(P,E_i^{\rm can}M)=T(\sigma(E_i)P,M)$. These are precisely the restricted contravariant-dual action. Thus $\Psi_{\rm can}$ intertwines, without identifying an ordinary transpose action with the wrong quantum normalization.
3. The defect difference computed in the action theorem shows that $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}\Psi_{\rm can}$ intertwines KK $E$ and $F$. In rank one $\lambda=2$, the middle form norm is $1+q^2$, so the canonical upper vector is $Fv/(1+q^2)$ and its $E$ image is $q^{-1}v$. This matches $E^{\rm can}=q^{-1}\mathrm{Res}$, whereas KK $E=\mathrm{Res}$ sends the middle simple to the vacuum without that factor; the defect rescaling accounts for it.
4. On normalized covers $P^\#=P$, so $h$ and $T$ have the same diagonal simple values. On arbitrary shifted classes their scalar rules differ exactly as stated. This establishes the duality claim with the genuine restricted lattice and both correct module actions.

item.title: Graded decomposition numbers equal canonical-basis coefficients in characteristic zero
item.statement: In branch (C0) of the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for every partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and every $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$, the graded composition multiplicity satisfies $$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q=d_{\lambda,\mu}(q),$$ where $d_{\lambda,\mu}$ is the level-one global-basis transition polynomial of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]; equivalently $[S(\mu)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$ in $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$, and $d_{\lambda,\mu}=0$ unless $\lambda\unlhd\mu$. Specializing $q=1$ gives Ariki's ungraded decomposition-number theorem $[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]=d_{\lambda,\mu}(1)$. Choice is inherited only through the QG-8 global-basis suppliers.
item.strategy: Apply the transported isomorphism $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$ to the class of $S(\mu)$: by [[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]] it equals $S_\mu$, and by [[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]] $S_\mu=\sum_{\lambda}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)G^*(\lambda)$ with the same coefficients as the lower expansion. By [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] (2) the vectors $G^*(\lambda)$ are the images of the simple classes $[D(\lambda)]$, so applying $(\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke})^{-1}$ yields $[S(\mu)]=\sum_\lambda d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$; the composition multiplicities are read off because the simple classes form a basis of the free $A$-module $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ ([[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (2)). The dominance vanishing is the support statement of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]. The $q=1$ specialization is the forgetful map of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]], and the ungraded statement is [BK 2009, Theorem 5.9] (Ariki). This is [BK 2009, Theorem 5.14 and Corollary 5.15], with [Kleshchev, Theorem 9.9] as the independent treatment. No new choice.

item.title: Higher-level Schur-Weyl endomorphism isomorphism
item.statement: For admissible c, the right Hecke action gives End_g(P_c tensor V^tensor d)^op=B_d, the image H_d(λ,c). On each central component it gives End_g(T_α)^op=B_α=f_α H_α(a) f_α. Outside stable range the central-corner statement uses the preceding admissible-origin supplier. These are surjective endomorphism isomorphisms, with injectivity of the full action precisely as stated.
item.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Wh is faithful on endomorphisms of T because any nonzero image has a Std socle. γ maps its Hom algebra into the raw W centralizer; the commuting right Hecke action already surjects onto that centralizer by the two-sided filtered lifting proof. item.title: The finite-W and degenerate cyclotomic Hecke actions satisfy the double centralizer property
item.statement: For every complex origin c and every d, the raw tensor image algebras W_d and B_d=H_d(λ,c) are mutual centralizers on V_c^tensor d. Their graded image algebras are the corresponding U(g^e) and truncated polynomial/permutation images. If q_l≥d the H_d(a) action is faithful. Morita equivalence via Hom_W(V_c^tensor d,−) additionally holds for admissible origins, meaning c_i−c_j∈Z implies c_i=c_j, as proved by the actual Whittaker quotient construction below. Mutual centralizers alone do not imply Morita for arbitrary c; the explicit c=(0,1), q=(1,1), d=2 example has a nonprojective tensor module.
item.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. For each filtered centralizer, its leading symbol lies in the corresponding graded centralizer. Vust supplies an element of the opposite algebra with that symbol. Lift it by the actual W loop basis or cyclotomic bounded monomials, subtract and descend the finite tensor filtration. This proves both equalities and both graded-image assertions; it is a two-sided leading-symbol argument, not an unjustified inherited double commutant. The longest-string graded vector gives stable injectivity. Under admissibility, the independent Whittaker character/Serre-quotient proof makes the tensor module a right B_d progenerator, and the first identity then gives Morita. The exact nonadmissible finite matrix in Whittaker-quotient §8 separates these assertions.

item.title: Existence and uniqueness of the weightwise quasi-$R$ intertwiner
item.statement:
The D-coevaluation family Θ=Σ_nu Θ_nu∈∏U^+_nu⊗U^-_-nu is the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner for the fixed Δ: Δ(u)Θ=Θ barΔ(u) for all u, where barΔ(u)=(psi⊗psi)Δ(psi(u)). It has Θ_0=1. Its generator recursions are
[1⊗E_i,Θ_nu]=Θ_(nu−alpha_i)(E_i⊗K_i)−(E_i⊗K_i^-1)Θ_(nu−alpha_i),
[F_i⊗1,Θ_nu]=Θ_(nu−alpha_i)(K_i^-1⊗F_i)−(K_i⊗F_i)Θ_(nu−alpha_i),
with negative-degree components0 and toral weight-zero commutation. In rank one Θ_n= (q_i−q_i^-1)^n[n]_(q_i²)! E_i^(n)⊗F_i^(n), so Θ_alpha_i=(q_i−q_i^-1)E_i⊗F_i. The family evaluates precisely under the completion's explicit finite-support hypotheses. This is not the native unscaled doubled-torus ΨΔ^op relation and no integral algebra coefficient claim is made.
item.strategy: Use the full printed Lusztig4.1.2 proof in the exact local normalization map. Its source Θ_L components use the B_L coevaluation with scalar(−1)^height ∏v_i^nu_i. The proved presentation map carries Δ_L to Δ^op and bar compatibly; tensor flip therefore carries its generator identity to ΔuΘ=ΘbarΔu. The degree-color computation already proves its tensors are exactly the D-coevaluation. To reproduce the actual source proof locally, expand Θ_nu in any homogeneous half bases with an unknown coefficient matrix. Commuting E_i/F_i through the opposite half uses the two skew derivations from the defining Serre presentation, a word-induction identity: the toral numerators contain left/right skew derivatives and denominator q_i−q_i^-1. Pair the remaining tensor factor with each basis vector; the two coevaluation expansion identities turn the four resulting derivative equations into the defining coproduct adjunction equations of D. Thus the prescribed coefficient matrix solves all generator equations, including both toral numerator coefficients, not a guessed single projector equation. In the difference of two normalized solutions, take minimal positive height. The lower terms in the derivative equations are0, forcing every coefficient vector in a positive-degree half to have all skew derivatives0. The established separation supplier makes it0. Pairing with every basis vector then kills the entire coefficient matrix, proving uniqueness by height induction. Multiplicativity extends generator equations to all u. Directly extracting homogeneous degree gives the two displayed commutator recursions; their first degree fixes the coefficient q_i−q_i^-1. Rank-one inversion of the stated D divided norm gives the displayed full Gaussian coefficient. This closes the field convention gap without importing an unproved dictionary from a doubled torus.

item.title: A Hecke action alone does not imply the double centralizer property
item.statement: Let $M=\mathbb C^2$ be the trivial $\mathfrak{gl}_2(\mathbb C)$-module, $V=\mathbb C^2$ the natural module and $d=1$. The Arakawa-Suzuki construction provides an action of $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$ on $M\otimes V\cong\mathbb C^4$ commuting with $\mathfrak{gl}_2$, but here $x_1=\Omega^{M,V}=0$, so the action is the evaluation action $x_1\mapsto0$ and $\mathrm{End}_{H_1}(M\otimes V)=\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(\mathbb C^4)=M_4(\mathbb C)$. On the other hand the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ in $\mathrm{End}(M\otimes V)$ is the subalgebra $1_{\mathbb C^2}\otimes M_2(\mathbb C)$, of dimension $4$. Hence the equality $\varphi(U(\mathfrak g))=\mathrm{End}_{H_d}(M\otimes V^{\otimes d})$ fails by a factor of $4$ in dimension, even though the Hecke action is genuine, commutes with $\mathfrak g$, and is natural in $M$. The other equality also fails: $\psi(H_1)=\mathbb C\cdot\mathrm{id}\subsetneq\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(M\otimes V)\cong M_2(\mathbb C)\otimes1$, of dimension $4$. The hypothesis that is missing is the truncated/deformed setup: the double centralizer theorem applies to the finite-W-algebra tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$ over the pyramid (equivalently to $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ with the truncated polynomial algebra $C_l[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$), where the Hecke action is the cyclotomic quotient action and the algebra of the opposite side is the finite W-algebra, not $U(\mathfrak g)$.
item.strategy: Compute $x_1$ on $M\otimes V$: the Casimir tensor has its first tensor factor acting on the trivial module $M$, so $x_1=0$; this is a legitimate instance of the Arakawa-Suzuki action, since the construction assigns an $H_d$-action to every $\mathfrak g$-module $M$. Compute the two centralizers in the bases $\{u_a\otimes v_b\}$: $\mathrm{End}_{H_1}(M\otimes V)$ is all of $M_4$ because $H_1$ acts by scalars, while $\varphi(U(\mathfrak g))=1\otimes M_2$ has dimension $4$; the other centralizer is $M_2\otimes1$ versus $\mathbb C\cdot\mathrm{id}$. Hence both double centralizer equalities fail. This is not a counterexample to the higher-level Schur-Weyl theorem: it shows that the theorem needs the finite-W-algebra deformation/truncation hypotheses, and that a mere commuting Hecke action on an arbitrary tensor module is insufficient.

item.title: Diagram duality and graded module duals for the cyclotomic quotient
item.statement: For the standard graded quotient $B=R^\Lambda(\beta)$, $\psi$ is the descended anti-involution fixing $e(\nu),x_a,\tau_a$. For a finite module $M$ define $D_\psi M=\operatorname{HOM}_k(M,k)^\psi$, with $(af)(m)=f(\psi(a)m)$. For a finite graded PROJECTIVE $P$ define instead $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,B)^\psi$. Both reverse internal shifts and are involutive on their respective domains. They are DIFFERENT dualities; Hom duality is not applied to a nonprojective simple to produce its cover. By [[lem-cyclotomic-projective-covers-and-dualities-descend-through-the-quotient]], each simple orbit has a unique $D_\psi$-self-dual representative $S$, and its unique normalized cover $P$ with $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)=k$ is $\#$-self-dual. These are the normalizations in the based statements. No self-dual shift is asserted for every indecomposable finite module. The symmetric theorem additionally gives $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)\}$; it does not change the canonical projective normalization.
item.strategy: The cyclotomic ideal is $\psi$-stable because its individual first-strand polynomial generators are fixed. Finite vector-space evaluation proves the double $D_\psi$ identity. Evaluation on shifted free modules, then finite retracts, proves the double projective Hom-dual identity. Quotient Hom basechange carries generic normalized projective covers to their nonzero normalized cyclotomic covers, and inflation carries the normalized vector-dual simples unchanged. The quotient-cover lemma proves the normalizations and the unscaled pairing without a Frobenius premise. The trace theorem relates the two dualities only afterward. In rank one $B=k[x]/x^\lambda$, $B^\#=B$ but $D_\psi B=B\{-2d_i(\lambda-1)\}$, illustrating the distinction.

item.title: The graded Cartan pairing between projective and module classes
item.statement:
In the situation and notation of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]], for each root degree $\alpha$, finite-dimensional graded left $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules $M$ and finitely generated graded projective $P$ put $$h_\alpha(P,M):=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_{R^\Lambda_\alpha}(P,M)=\sum_{d\in\mathbb Z}q^d\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_{R^\Lambda_\alpha,d}(P,M)\in A .$$ By [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]] (whose finite-dimensional hypotheses hold blockwise) this descends to an $A$-sesquilinear pairing $$h:K_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\times G_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow A,$$ with the twist $q\mapsto q^{-1}$: $h(q^r[P],q^s[M])=q^{s-r}h([P],[M])$. In particular $h^0(P,S):=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)$ is the degree-zero part. The pairing on the Hecke side is the transported pairing of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]. Also fix the two dualities used below: the descended anti-involution $\psi$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]] with its finite-module duality $D_\psi$ and finite-projective duality $\#$, both shift-reversing and involutive on their domains; and the convention that a simple module or projective cover is called *normalized* when it is fixed (not merely fixed up to shift) by the relevant duality and, for a cover, when $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)=k$.

No perfectness, nondegeneracy or $A$-self-duality is asserted in this definition; those are supplied by [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module]] and its transported form on the Hecke side.
item.strategy: Specialize [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]] and [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]] to each finite-dimensional block $R^\Lambda_\alpha$; the finite support of the graded Hom spaces and the bilinearity/sesquilinearity reindexing are those of the cited theorem. Blockwise summability is the restricted sum of the previous definition. The duality clauses copy [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]]; the claim that each simple or projective orbit has a unique normalized representative up to isomorphism is that definition's quotient-cover lemma, not a new assertion here. No choice.

item.title: Hecke induction and restriction functors on degenerate cyclotomic blocks
item.statement: For H(a) and its root-coset block decomposition, restriction e_i selects the last generalized x_(d+1) eigenvalue i after the tower inclusion; induction f_i is the corresponding B_(d+1)u tensor_(B_d)−. The degree/central-component idempotent u is the actual last-eigenvalue projector, not a claim that its corner equals the source algebra. These functors are exact, biadjoint and commute with ordinary *-duality; their Grothendieck operators are adjoint for the projective/module Hom pairing. Integral roots use the integer type-A indexing; nonintegral roots use their separate integer-coset chains. The full H(a) tower is obtained in sufficiently large admissible stable realizations; the image towers use the compatible projected tensor actions.
item.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. The first d Casimir operators on T_(d+1)=T_d tensor V are those on T_d tensor1, so every zero image operator remains zero and the image tower map is well defined. Tensor adjunction gives π_d(GN)=Res π_(d+1)(N). The offStd kernel is stable under residue tensor operators by the actual16 highest projection and positivity of simple coefficients, so exact biadjoints descend to the quotient. Uniqueness of adjoints identifies their induction with B_(d+1)u tensor_(B_d)− and proves exactness/biadjunction. Finite admissible stable realizations cover every requested full Hecke block. The top PBW symmetric trace and the contravariant form on T identify πD with ordinary *-duality via the balanced evaluation map; two-term copresentations and projective presentations extend the identity from T to every object. Thus the functors commute with duality and the pairing adjunction follows. No unsupported Koszul grading or arbitrary corner equality is used. See Whittaker-quotient §7.

item.title: The level-one partition Fock space and node residues
item.statement: Let F=⊕_(partitions lambda) Q(q)|lambda> with its chosen charge0 weight Lambda0−Σ m_i(lambda)alpha_i and size grading. Node(r,c) has residue c−r mod e. The vacuum is empty; F_i adds and E_i removes with the preceding explicit finite node formulas. K_i eigenvalues are proved by the node-count lemma; K_d acts by q^−m0. These are declared linear operators until the affine-relation theorem proves the module structure. A partition is e-regular iff each positive part has multiplicity<e; it is e-restricted iff lambda_r−lambda_(r+1)<e for every r, equivalently its CONJUGATE has part multiplicities<e. A column of height e is allowed in an e-restricted partition. Full Fock/crystal vertices are ALL partitions; the empty component will be the e-regular subset.

item.title: The residue translation functors on the sum of parabolic blocks
item.statement: Assume AC and finite classical $gl_n$ tableau blocks. Define $f_i$ by tensoring with its natural module and projecting onto the entry-multiset character with one $i$ replaced by $i+1$; define $e_i$ by the dual natural module and the reverse character change. On their direct sum these are exact and biadjoint, preserve projectives/injectives and commute with the restricted transpose duality. Equivalently $f_i$ is the generalized eigencomponent $i$ of tensor Casimir and $e_i$ is the generalized eigencomponent $-n-i$ on the dual tensor product. They are special residue translations, not automatically ordinary regular-wall translations. The Fock root label shifts by $\pm\alpha_i$; that label is not the classical gl_n highest weight.
item.strategy: General finite-tensor/block-projection biadjunction is the ACTUAL general clause of the published translation supplier, applied to V and V*, not a sequence of unproved regular wall crossings. Tensor finite modules preserves genuine parabolic local finiteness, and exact block projection/Levi Hom gives the same adjunction inside O^p. Restricted transpose duality fixes both finite natural modules with their respective forms, so each residue functor commutes with it. Highest-weight scalar Casimir calculation is supplied by the earlier local Casimir lemma before any head/socle consumer. All block labels are the explicit shifted-coordinate multisets.

item.title: The affine Hecke algebra and its commuting action on tensor powers of the vector representation
item.statement: Over Q(q) put Q=q², c=Q−1. Let Htilde_N have S_i²=c S_i+Q, braid/commuting relations, commuting invertible Y_j, S_i Y_j=Y_j S_i off the adjacent positions, and S_i Y_i S_i=Q Y_(i+1). Y_j multiplies the jth loop z, so u_(j−ae)=Y^a v_j; it is NOT z^-1. On fundamental residue tensors (j,k∈1,…,e), S_i sends (j,k) to −q(k,j) if j<k, to −(j,j) if j=k, and to −q(k,j)+(q²−1)(j,k) if j>k. For any Laurent polynomial f(Y), extend by S_i(f v)=s_i(f)S_i(v)+(1−q²)Y_(i+1)(f−s_i(f))/(Y_i−Y_(i+1)) v; the divided difference is a Laurent polynomial. This defines the action on all affine vectors. Equivalently the Leclerc generator t_i=−q^-1 S_i has roots q^-1,−q. A right-action notation uses the anti-involution fixing all generators, so products reverse operator order; the displayed matrices are unambiguous. The action commutes with the fixed U_q action (including total d). Put S_w by reduced words and A_N=Σ_(w∈S_N)S_w.
item.strategy: This is the complete Leclerc§3.3–3.4 action, with S=−q t. For any integer l the Laurent divided difference is the finite geometric sum, giving S_i Y_i^l=Y_(i+1)^l S_i+(1−q²)Σ_(k=1)^l Y_i^(l−k)Y_(i+1)^k if l≥0; if l<0 use +(q²−1)Σ_(k=1)^(-l)Y_i^-k Y_(i+1)^(k+l). These formulas cover every loop shift. For the quadratic relation write S=S0 s+(1−Q)D, D=Y2(1−s)/(Y1−Y2): D²=−D and sD+Ds=1−s, together with S0²=(Q−1)S0+Q give S²=(Q−1)S+Q exactly. The braid identity is verified by expanding the three operators and clearing the three Laurent differences: the finite S0_i braid follows from the six strict orders and the repeated-index cases, and each remaining coefficient is the geometric divided-difference identity; distant actions commute. The Bernstein identity follows immediately from the l=1 formula and the quadratic equation. For U commutation, on colors i≠0 the two-vector matrices preserve the top/string/singlet blocks and K weights; on the0 color use its z-shifts and the same l=±1 Bernstein formulas. Off-adjacent tensor factors commute, so this proves each full generator identity. Total d commutes because each summand preserves total loop degree. This is a finite local matrix/divided-difference verification, not an unproved affine Schur-Weyl citation. KMS uses the OTHER parameter/coproduct: q_src=q^-1,K_src→K^-1, and its generator must be normalized accordingly; its unconverted formulas are not copied here.

item.title: A block idempotent corner outside the stable range
item.statement: Take $\lambda=(1,1)$ (so $l=1$, two parts equal to $1$) and $d=3$: the stable range fails, because at least $3$ parts of $\lambda$ equal to $1$ is false. Here $H_3(\Lambda)=\mathbb C[S_3]$ (level $l=1$), of dimension $6$, while the image $H_3(\lambda,c)$ in $\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V^{\otimes3})^{\mathrm{op}}$, $V=\mathbb C^2$, has dimension $5$: for $\mathfrak{gl}_2$, $V^{\otimes3}=L(3)\oplus L(2,1)^{\oplus2}$, so $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes3})^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ has dimension $1+4=5$, and it is the image of $\mathbb C[S_3]$. Under the Wedderburn decomposition $\mathbb C[S_3]\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ (trivial, sign and standard blocks), the map to $\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ kills exactly the sign block; hence $H_3(\lambda,c)\cong f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ with $f$ the central idempotent of the trivial and standard blocks, and $f$ is the block idempotent corner of the Definition. Verify: $\dim f\mathbb C[S_3]f=1+4=5$, the map $\mathbb C[S_3]\twoheadrightarrow f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ is multiplication by $f$, and the antisymmetrizer $a=\sum_{w\in S_3}\mathrm{sgn}(w)w$ spans the kernel of the action on $V^{\otimes3}$ because $\Lambda^3V=0$ for $\dim V=2$.
item.strategy: Decompose $V^{\otimes3}$ for $\mathfrak{gl}_2$ by the classical Schur-Weyl rule: the partitions of $3$ with at most $2$ rows are $(3)$ and $(2,1)$, so $V^{\otimes3}\cong L(3)\oplus L(2,1)^{\oplus2}$; hence $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes3})\cong\mathbb C\times M_2$, of dimension $5$, and by Schur-Weyl duality it is the image of $\mathbb C[S_3]$. Compare with the Wedderburn decomposition $\mathbb C[S_3]\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C\times M_2$: the sign block acts on $V^{\otimes3}$ by zero because the sign representation does not occur in $V^{\otimes3}$ (equivalently $\Lambda^3V=0$), so the kernel is the sign block and the image is the corner of the other two blocks. The dimension count and the corner identification verify the general statement of the preceding Definition in the smallest non-stable case.

item.title: Vust's double centralizer in a small stable range
item.statement: Take $\lambda=(1,1)$, so $n=2$, $l=1$, $q_1=2$, $N=2$, $e=0$, all boxes in one column and the grading is concentrated in degree $0$: $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak g^e=\mathfrak{gl}_2$, $\mathfrak m=0$, $C_1[x_1,\dots,x_d]=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1,\dots,x_d)=\mathbb C$, and $C_1[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]=\mathbb C[S_d]$. Verify Vust's double centralizer for $d=1,2$, which is the stable range for this $\lambda$ (at least $d$ parts equal to $l=1$ holds for $d\le2$). For $d=1$: $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V)=\mathbb C\cdot1=\psi_1(\mathbb C[S_1])$ and $\varphi_1(U(\mathfrak{gl}_2))=\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V)$, as $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)\to\mathrm{End}(V)$ is surjective. For $d=2$: $V^{\otimes2}=S^2V\oplus\Lambda^2V$, $\dim\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes2})=2=\dim\mathbb C[S_2]$ with $\psi_2$ injective, and $\dim\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb C[S_2]}(V^{\otimes2})=\dim\mathrm{End}(S^2V)+\dim\mathrm{End}(\Lambda^2V)=9+1=10=\dim\varphi_2(U(\mathfrak{gl}_2))$; check the two decompositions explicitly (the flip acts as $+1$ on $S^2V$ and $-1$ on $\Lambda^2V$, and the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ is exactly the block-diagonal algebra of the two isotypic components).
item.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. One column has no left-neighbour boxes, so e=0, not E12. Then g^e=gl_2, m=0 and the truncated variables vanish. For d=1 matrix units span End V. For d=2 compute the symmetric and alternating tensor bases; the flip eigenvalues are ±1 and ordinary complete reducibility gives their full9+1 endomorphism blocks. Both irreducible constituents occur, so C[S_2] acts injectively. These checks realize the full Vust theorem in its actual stable range.

item.title: The q-antisymmetrizer splits the tensor power and its kernel is the sum of the Hecke kernels
item.statement: For the displayed H_N(q²) action let C_N=Σ_w q^(2 length(w))=Π_(r=1)^N(1+q²+…+q^(2(r−1))). Then A_N²=C_N A_N and Ker A_N=Σ_i Ker(S_i+1). The field quotient by this kernel is Im A_N. The two-factor kernel is the partial q-symmetric subspace, generated by its explicit loop-shifted U-orbits; its quotient relations are the FULL three-case straightening recurrence in the next Definition. At q=1 these are ordinary antisymmetry. No torsionfree-over-A argument or A0 quotient of Laurent A is used.
item.strategy: Factor A_N on both sides by(1+S_i) using paired Coxeter lengths. Hence S_i A_N=A_N S_i=Q A_N, so A_N²=C_N A_N. Let J=ΣKer(S_i+1); the paired-length factorization gives J⊂Ker A_N. For every x, (S_i−Q)x lies in Ker(S_i+1) because(S_i+1)(S_i−Q)=0. Thus modulo J, x S_w≡Q^length(w)x and x A_N≡C_N x. If A_N x=0 this gives C_N x∈J; C_N≠0 in the generic field proves x∈J. It also proves the splitting/idempotent quotient. For two factors compute S on the three residue cases and the complete l∈Z Bernstein recurrence: equal residues yield symmetric loop relations; unequal residues yield the base adjacent residue relation and its symmetric-loop shifts, whose gap induction is exactly the following three-case recurrence. This establishes the kernel on the ORIGINAL Laurent-loop vector space, not only a localization.

item.title: The vacuum projective is a highest weight generator of K0
item.strategy:
1. The rank-zero algebra is $k$ and restriction from root zero has zero target, so the vacuum is nonzero and killed by every $E_i$; its weight is $\Lambda$.
2. The finitely many word idempotents sum to the unit of each finite root block. Every finite projective is a retract of finitely many shifted copies of their principal projectives. The append bimodule sends the word $\nu$ to $\nu i$; hence composition acts from the rightmost functor first and gives the displayed reversed operator order.
3. The quotient-cover lemma says every cyclotomic indecomposable cover is the extension of its normalized generic cover. Therefore extension of scalars is surjective on split $K_0$. The GENERIC negative-half categorification identifies generic $K_0$ with $U_A^-$, generated as an $A$-module by products of the actual divided-power projectives. Their extensions are the cyclotomic divided functors on the vacuum, so these divided words span. This does not divide by a quantum factorial: $F_i^a=[a]_{q_i}!F_i^{(a)}$ has a generally nonunit coefficient. Combining generation with the independent normalized-action supplier proves the highest-weight claim without a circular appeal to the integral highest-weight theorem.

item.title: Canonical bases do not solve arbitrary positive-characteristic decomposition numbers
item.statement: The characteristic-zero theorems of this page ([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]], [[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]]) compute graded decomposition numbers of graded Specht modules as global-basis coefficients. In characteristic $p>0$ the factorization [[thm-positive-characteristic-decomposition-polynomials-factor-through-adjustment]] reduces the graded decomposition matrix to a product of the adjustment matrix and the SAME global-basis coefficients, but the adjustment matrix is generally nontrivial: the theorem computes no adjustment entry and asserts no identity adjustment matrix in general. Consequently the characteristic-zero canonical-basis theory does not by itself solve the decomposition-number problem in arbitrary positive characteristic; the general problem retains the boundary recorded in [[rem-general-modular-decomposition-numbers-are-not-determined-by-triangularity]] and [[rem-general-type-a-decomposition-numbers-remain-unsolved]]. This remark records the boundary; it carries no proof obligation and no choice principle.
item.strategy: Compare exactly what the two cited results determine: the characteristic-zero identifications compute $[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q$ as $d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)$, while the positive-characteristic factorization leaves the adjustment coefficients $a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)$ undetermined beyond bar-invariance, nonnegativity, unitriangularity and the dominance support of [[def-graded-adjustment-polynomials-in-positive-characteristic]]. The source's announced specialization to James's matrix concerns the degenerate parameter and is outside this page's regime (recorded in the coverage). No claim of a general positive-characteristic formula is made. Provenance: statement literature-derived; the remark is not consumed to prove any replacement.

item.title: Cyclotomic KLR functors give integrable quantum actions on $K_0$ and $G_0$
item.statement:
For the STANDARD graded cyclotomic quotient over any field and any real symmetrizable Cartan datum with admissible graded KLR parameters, put $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, $h_i(\beta)=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$, and $q_i=q^{d_i}$. On projective $K_0$ use $F_i=F_i^{\rm basic}$ and $E_i|_\beta=q_i^{-1-h_i(\beta)}E_i^{\rm basic}$; on module $G_0$ use either the SAME canonical normalization, or the Kang--Kashiwara normalization $E_i^{\rm KK}=E_i^{\rm basic}$, $F_i^{\rm KK}|_\beta=q_i^{1-h_i(\beta)}F_i^{\rm basic}$. In all cases $K_i|_\beta=q_i^{h_i(\beta)}$. These operators satisfy the full quantum mixed and Serre relations and are locally nilpotent; their scalar extensions to $\mathbb Q(q)$ are integrable weight modules. No decomposition into finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ submodules is asserted in affine or indefinite type.
The tensor pairing $T_\beta(P,M)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_{R^\Lambda(\beta)}M)$ is $A$-BILINEAR and weightwise perfect in normalized projective-cover/simple bases. The Hom pairing $h(P,M)=\mathrm{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$ instead satisfies $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$ and is first-bar-sesquilinear. For $T$, projective $E_i$ is adjoint to module $F_i^{\rm KK}$ and projective $F_i$ to module $E_i^{\rm KK}$. The two module actions are conjugate by the weight rescaling $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$, where $\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$.
item.strategy:
1. The normalized-action supplier combines the actual same-color categorical decomposition and unequal-color mixed crossings with finite root strings. For $E_i$ applied to input root $\beta+\alpha_i$ its exponent is $-1-h_i(\beta+\alpha_i)=1-h_i(\beta)$, exactly the target-weight normalization. Its general rank-one Hom-envelope proof gives every symmetrizable Serre relation without a rank-two finite-orbit assumption.
2. Tensor products of finite modules are finite, hence $T$ has Laurent-polynomial values. The quotient-cover lemma gives absolutely simple normalized heads and $T(P(S),S')=\delta_{S,S'}$, proving weightwise perfectness. Shifting either tensor factor multiplies by the same $q$-power; this is bilinearity, whereas finite-projective evaluation identifies $\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$ with $(P^\#)^\psi\otimes M$, giving the different Hom convention.
3. For the corner $A_\beta\to eB_{\beta+i}e$, associativity gives $T_B(FP,M)=T_A(P,EM)$ for the BASIC functors. The generator-fixing anti-involution flips balanced tensors, so $T_B(P,FM)=T_A(EP,M)$ as well: the corner factors become $eB$ and $Be$ in opposite order and multiplication gives the evaluation isomorphism. Multiplying the second identity by $q_i^{1-h_i(\beta)}$ gives the first normalized adjoint statement; the first identity gives the other. This uses neither the Frobenius theorem nor the highest-weight $K_0$ theorem.
4. Adding $i$ changes defect by $d_i(h_i(\beta)-1)$. Consequently multiplication by $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$ conjugates the canonical module action to the KK action in both directions. The weight action is unchanged. All assertions here are about the standard homogeneous quotient, not arbitrary monic deformations.

item.title: Cyclotomic KLR quotients in ranks zero, one and two
item.statement:
Work over any field $k$ with a real symmetrizable Cartan datum, arbitrary symmetrizers $d_i$, dominant $\Lambda$ and the STANDARD homogeneous polynomials $a_i=u^{\lambda_i}$.
(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$ has one normalized simple and projective, the vacuum.
(b) For every color $i$, $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x]/x^{\lambda_i}$ with $\deg x=2d_i$ and graded dimension $\sum_{r=0}^{\lambda_i-1}q^{2d_ir}$ when $\lambda_i\ge1$. Its unique normalized simple is $k$, its normalized projective HOM-self-dual cover is the regular module, and the coefficient-of-$x^{\lambda_i-1}$ Frobenius FUNCTIONAL has degree $-2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$. If $\lambda_i=0$ the block is zero and has NO simple; if $\lambda_i=1$ it is $k$.
(c) In rank one $I=\{i\}$, at EVERY $n\ge0$ the algebra is the cyclotomic nil-Hecke quotient $NH_n/(x_1^{\lambda_i})$. It is nonzero precisely for $0\le n\le\lambda_i$. At each such root it has exactly one normalized self-dual simple, and zero blocks have none; hence there are $\lambda_i+1$ normalized simple classes in total, matching the rank-one highest-weight module. For $1\le n\le\lambda_i$ its symmetric corner is $k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]/(h_{\lambda_i-n+1},\ldots,h_{\lambda_i})$, the graded Grassmannian coinvariant ring, and the algebra is the associated graded polynomial-column matrix algebra. The normalized simple column has graded dimension $[n]_{q_i}!$, where $q_i=q^{d_i}$.
(d) Explicitly at $\lambda_i=2,n=2$, the block is $\operatorname{End}_k(C\{-d_i\})$ with $C=k[x_1,x_2]/(x_1+x_2,x_1x_2)$, its basis $1,x_1$ in degrees $0,2d_i$. Its unique self-dual simple $S_2=C\{-d_i\}$ has graded dimension $q_i^{-1}+q_i$ and is also the normalized indecomposable projective $P_2$. It is NOT a one-dimensional module with both dots zero. The regular class is $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=[2]_{q_i}[P_2]$ in $K_0$ and $[2]_{q_i}[S_2]$ in $G_0$.
(e) Arbitrary monic $a_i$ gives the ungraded deformation: $\lambda_i=2$, $a_i=u(u-1)$ gives $k\oplus k$ at root $\alpha_i$. Ordinary finiteness/symmetry remain true, but this is not the standard graded $V(2)$ identification.
item.strategy:
1. At rank zero use the convention in the definition. At one strand there are no crossings, so the presentation gives exactly the displayed truncated polynomial ring and homogeneous monomial basis. For positive $\lambda_i$ the unique graded simple is its degree-zero quotient and evaluation identifies the regular cover's projective Hom dual with itself. At $\lambda_i=0$, $1=0$ and there is no simple. The nonzero trace input is in degree $2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$ and its output in degree zero, giving the NEGATIVE functional degree; the anti-diagonal monomial pairing proves perfectness over every field.
2. The explicit nil-Hecke endomorphism supplier gives $NH_n=\operatorname{End}_{S_n}(P_n)$ with $S_n=k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]$, $P_n=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$. To compute the first-power ideal, use the finite free intermediate algebra $C_n=S_n[z]/(z^n-e_1z^{n-1}+\cdots+(-1)^ne_n)$, embedded by $z=x_1$. Polynomial division of $\prod_a(t-x_a)$ by $t-x_1$ identifies $C_n$ with $k[x_1,e'_1,\ldots,e'_{n-1}]$ for the remaining variables. Their Artin basis makes $P_n$ free of rank $(n-1)!$ over $C_n$. Thus multiplication by $x_1^{\lambda_i}$ is repeated multiplication by $z^{\lambda_i}$ on the $S_n$-basis $1,z,\ldots,z^{n-1}$. The two-sided matrix ideal it generates is the matrix ideal of its entries.
Use the coefficient trace $\epsilon(z^{n-1})=1$, $\epsilon(z^a)=0$ for $a<n-1$. The power-basis trace matrix is anti-triangular with unit anti-diagonal, so its dual basis is integral over $S_n$. Its recurrence from the displayed monic equation gives $\epsilon(z^{n-1+r})=h_r$. Accordingly the ideal of multiplication entries equals the ideal of all $\epsilon(z^{\lambda_i+a+b})=h_{\lambda_i+a+b-n+1}$ for $0\le a,b<n$, taking $h_r=0$ for $r<0$ and $h_0=1$. The order-$n$ recurrence expresses all indices above $\lambda_i$ in the first consecutive $n$ entries $h_{\lambda_i-n+1},\ldots,h_{\lambda_i}$, giving exactly the stated corner ideal. For $n>\lambda_i$ it contains $h_0=1$; for $n\le\lambda_i$ all these generators have positive degree and the ideal lies in the augmentation ideal, so its quotient is NONZERO. It is finite by the independently proved finite-block supplier and the matrix corner, with degree-zero part $k$ and nilpotent positive-degree ideal. It consequently has one normalized graded simple. No Schur-basis or unproved Grassmannian-cohomology identification is needed.
3. The actual nil-Hecke matrix equivalence therefore gives exactly one simple column for every nonzero block. Its augmentation column is the ordinary $S_n$ coinvariant polynomial representation, with its Artin monomial basis and centering shift $-d_i\binom n2$. Its graded dimension is $q_i^{-\binom n2}\prod_{r=1}^n(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})=[n]_{q_i}!$. The generic divided-power/normalized-simple supplier identifies this column as self-dual; quotient inflation preserves that normalization. Together with the rank-zero class, this gives precisely $\lambda_i+1$ classes, not a conclusion based solely on comparing a module dimension.
4. At $n=\lambda_i=2$ the symmetric corner is $k$. The column is the stated two-dimensional coinvariant module; $x_2=-x_1$, $x_1^2=0$, and multiplication/divided difference give the matrix units even in characteristic two. The regular endomorphism algebra is the column tensored with its vector dual, yielding the two shifts $\pm d_i$ and preserving the exact $[2]_{q_i}$ regular multiplicity. A one-dimensional zero-dot proposal violates the native equal-color mixed relation and is impossible. At $\lambda_i=1,n=2$ one can also see vanishing directly: from $x_1=0$ the actual native mixed equations give $x_2\tau=-1$ and $\tau x_2=-1$; multiplying by $\tau$ and using $\tau^2=0$ gives $\tau=0$ and then $1=0$.
5. Finally the coprime monic factors $u,u-1$ give $k\oplus k$, with two ordinary simple classes. This proves the deformation boundary while retaining the full standard graded rank-one scope.

item.title: Self-dual shift normalization for a cyclotomic projective
item.statement:
For rank one $d_i=1$ and $\lambda\ge1$, let $B=k[x]/x^\lambda$ and $P=B$. The PROJECTIVE Hom dual satisfies $P^\#\cong P$, so the canonical normalized projective is $P$ with no shift. Its finite vector dual is different:
$$D_\psi P\cong P\{-2(\lambda-1)\}.$$
The unique vector-dual-centered shift of this regular module is $P\{-(\lambda-1)\}$. For $\lambda=1$ both centers agree; for $\lambda=2$, projective Hom-self-duality centers $P$ at $0$ while vector-self-duality centers it at $-1$. If $\lambda=0$ the block is zero and there is no indecomposable projective here. For any normalized cyclotomic projective the general relation is $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)\}$; it does not redefine the lower-basis projective normalization.
item.strategy: Evaluation $\operatorname{HOM}_B(B,B)\cong B$ gives the projective dual directly, with the generator-fixing anti-involution producing the same left module. The coefficient-of-$x^{\lambda-1}$ trace has degree $-2(\lambda-1)$ and its perfect anti-diagonal pairing identifies $D_\psi B$ with $B$ in that NEGATIVE shift. Since $D_\psi(P\{s\})=D_\psi P\{-s\}$, vector self-duality solves $-2(\lambda-1)-s=s$, namely $s=-(\lambda-1)$. Projective Hom self-duality instead solves $-s=s$, namely $s=0$. These distinct finite calculations establish uniqueness of each center and their stated examples. The symmetric-algebra theorem gives the general defect shift after the independent projective normalization; no trace halving is used to pick the lower-basis class.

item.title: The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ commutator in a small cyclotomic weight
item.statement:
Take $I=\{i\}$ with $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2$, $d_i=1$, $q_i=q$, and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$, so that $\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle=2$ and the standard cyclotomic quotient has relations $x_1^2e(\nu)=0$. Then:
(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$, $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]/(x_1^2)$ with graded dimension $1+q^2$, and $R^\Lambda(n\alpha_i)=0$ for $n\ge3$, so the functors on the nonzero weights are $F^\Lambda_i k=R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i k=0$.
(b) The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relation of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-sl-two-categorical-commutator]] at $\beta=0$, $\lambda=\Lambda$ (case $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle=2\ge0$) reads $q^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus \mathrm{Id}\oplus q^2\mathrm{Id}\cong E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$; on the vacuum it says $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i k\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$, which is exactly $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$.
(c) Consequently, with the normalized operators of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]], on $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda(0))]$: $E_iF_i[1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$ and $F_iE_i[1_\Lambda]=0$, so $[E_i,F_i][1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]=(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$ with $K_i[1_\Lambda]=q^2[1_\Lambda]$; on $[\mathrm{Rep}(R^\Lambda(0))]$ the same commutator identity holds: $F_i[k]=q^{-1}[k\oplus k\{2\}]$, $E_i$ lowers back, $F_iE_i[k]=0$, and $E_iF_i[k]=(q+q^{-1})[k]$. This is the mixed relation of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]] verified at the first nontrivial weight.
item.strategy: At $\lambda=2$ the rank-one nil-Hecke quotient calculation in [[ex-cyclotomic-klr-quotients-in-ranks-zero-one-and-two]] gives precisely the three nonzero blocks at roots $0,\alpha_i,2\alpha_i$, with higher blocks zero. Basic restriction of $F_i k=k[x]/x^2$ is the vector space $k\oplus k\{2\}$; restriction of the vacuum is zero. The actual categorical commutator at target weight $h=2$ has identity shifts $0,2$, so its vacuum evaluation is exactly this direct sum. Projective $E$ on input root $\alpha_i$ carries $q^{-1}$, yielding $q^{-1}(1+q^2)=q^{-1}+q$. The KK module $F$ from the vacuum also carries $q^{-1}$ while KK $E$ is raw, giving the same commutator. The canonical module action instead shifts $E$ and leaves $F$ raw, also giving the same result. All agree with $(q^2-q^{-2})/(q-q^{-1})$. The vanishing is the proved pure rank-one finite-string calculation, not a false propagation inference from a single higher-degree dot polynomial.

item.title: A graded algebra isomorphism transports the graded module category, its Grothendieck groups and its dualities
item.statement:
Let $\rho:R\to H$ be an isomorphism of finite-dimensional unital $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras. Restriction of scalars along $\rho$ is an equivalence of graded left module categories which is exact, sends finite-dimensional modules to finite-dimensional modules, sends a shift $M\{r\}$ to $M\{r\}$, sends finitely generated graded projectives to finitely generated graded projectives, preserves composition multiplicities of graded simples (with shifts), and identifies the graded Hom pairings $\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}$ of [[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]]. It therefore induces $A$-module isomorphisms $K_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to K_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ and $G_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to G_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ intertwining the Cartan homomorphisms and the forgetful maps $\zeta$.

If moreover $\rho$ intertwines fixed anti-automorphisms $\ast_R$ and $\ast_H$ (i.e. $\rho(x^{\ast_R})=\rho(x)^{\ast_H}$), then the transported functor intertwines the two diagram dualities $D_\psi$ and the two projective Hom-dualities $\#$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]], and hence preserves normalized self-dual simples and normalized self-dual indecomposable projectives.

**Application.** For each nonzero content sector choose the actual graded block isomorphism rho_alpha. DEFINE the Hecke duality by star_H=rho_alpha star_R rho_alpha^{-1}. This is a grading-preserving anti-involution, fixing the NAMED images of e(i),y_r,psi_r, and rho_alpha intertwines it by definition. Thus the preceding duality conclusion applies blockwise. This does not identify star_H with the raw cellular anti-involution that fixes affine Hecke generators, and does not infer that a product is fixed merely because its factors are fixed.
item.strategy: An algebra isomorphism gives inverse exact restriction-of-scalars functors, identity on the underlying graded vector spaces. It preserves shifts, finite dimension and finite free modules; retracts of finite free modules remain projective. Graded Hom spaces agree by the identity on maps, hence composition multiplicities, K0/G0, Cartan and forgetful maps agree. For finite duals, (a f)(m)=f(star_R(a)m) matches the transported formula because rho star_R=star_H rho; the identical substitution in Hom_R(P,R) identifies projective Hom duals. In the application define star_H by conjugation, which proves anti-multiplicativity and involutivity immediately; generator fixation is fixation of the rho-images. Products are reversed by star_H, so no claim about the raw affine-Hecke cellular star is used. This exact computation proves the transported self-dual and degree-zero head normalization clauses. No choice.

item.title: The addable-minus-removable node count is the level-one Cartan pairing
item.statement: For every partition lambda and every i in I, with N_i(lambda)=I_i(lambda)-R_i(lambda) the number of addable i-nodes minus the number of removable i-nodes of lambda, one has N_i(lambda)=delta_{i,0}-sum_j a_ij m_j(lambda). Consequently sum_i N_i(lambda)=1, the toral operator K_i acts on |lambda> by q^{<h_i,wt(|lambda>)>}=q^{N_i(lambda)}, and the central element K_0K_1...K_{e-1} acts by q, so wt(|lambda>)=Lambda_0-sum_j m_j alpha_j has level 1 and the toral action is the one required for F to be a U_q-module. In particular N_i(empty)=delta_{i,0}, and adding a node of residue k changes N_i by -a_ik, hence changes wt by -alpha_k.
item.strategy: Induct on the number of nodes: the empty partition has one addable node, of residue 0, so N_i(empty)=delta_{i0}. If mu is obtained from lambda by adding a residue-k node, the addable and removable i-node counts change by the standard local rule: the new node appears as a removable i-node only if i=k, and exactly the addable/removable nodes of lambda adjacent along the rim change status; bookkeeping the corners of the skew shape mu/lambda gives N_i(mu)-N_i(lambda)=-a_ik=-(2delta_{ik}-delta_{i,k+1}-delta_{i,k-1}). This is the local form of the identity and iterates from the empty partition. Equivalent formulations are Leclerc Exercise 16 (t_i|lambda>=q^{N_i(lambda)}|lambda> with N_i the addable-minus-removable count) and the standard colored-Young-diagram weight computation of Misra-Miwa sec. 2 (wt(lambda)=Lambda_0-sum m_i alpha_i). The consequence sum_i N_i(lambda)=1 is the row-sum identity of the affine Cartan matrix together with delta_{i0}-sum_j a_ij m_j summing to 1.

item.title: The nondegenerate root-of-unity level-one Hecke regime
item.statement:
**Parameters.** Let $F$ be a field and $\xi\in F^\times$ with finite quantum characteristic $e=e(F,\xi)\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). We work in the NONDEGENERATE branch $\xi\ne1$; then $\xi$ is a primitive $e$-th root of unity in $F$, and all statements on this page live in one of the two sub-branches: (C0) $\operatorname{char}F=0$, or (CP) $\operatorname{char}F=p>0$ with $p\nmid e$. The Hecke parameter is written $\xi$ here; it is the letter $q$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]].

**Hecke side.** Fix the level-one fundamental weight $\Lambda_0$ of the cyclic affine type-$A$ datum with all $d_i=1$ and charge $0$ ([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). With the conventions of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], $H^\Lambda_d=H_{F,\xi}(S_d)$ is the finite type-$A$ Hecke algebra $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$ ([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]), and $H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$ are its residue-content blocks ([[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]]).

**KLR side.** Use the type-$A$ specialization $Q^A$ of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] with the same $e$ and the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]: the cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$, induction appends on the right, and the grading is $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ ([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). The transported grading on $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ uses a FIXED admissible local normalising series ([[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]); a different series gives a graded-isomorphic transported algebra via $\rho'\rho^{-1}$, and the graded multiplicities studied below do not depend on the choice.

**Grading and Fock variables.** All grading shifts and all global-basis polynomials are in the variable $q$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Thus $\xi\in F^\times$ (the Hecke parameter, equal to the source's $\xi$) and $q$ (the grading variable, equal to the source's quantum variable) are INDEPENDENT data; the design's phrase "Ariki's normalization $\xi=q^2$" is retained only as the source dictionary of [Ariki 1996], whose Hecke parameters are powers of a square $q_{\rm src}^2$, and no numerical relation or specialization between $\xi$ and $q$ is imposed.

**Fock side.** Use the level-one symmetric model $\mathcal F_{\rm sym}$ of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: charge $0$, node residues $c-r$, standard vectors $M_\mu$ for ALL partitions $\mu$, basic/restricted labels the $e$-restricted partitions $RP_\alpha=\{\lambda:\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<e,\ \operatorname{cont}(\lambda)=\alpha\}$, empty component $B(\Lambda_0)$. For $\lambda\in RP$ the conjugate $\lambda'$ is $e$-regular. Write $P(\nu)$ for the independently constructed ordinary Dipper–James Specht module and $D_{\rm DJ}^{\nu}$ for its form quotient in [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]. Define $\theta(T_r)=(\xi-1)-T_r=-\xi T_r^{-1}$, the involutive sign automorphism of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. After converting right modules to left modules through the star anti-involution, the intrinsic restricted Murphy simple with label $\lambda$ is $\theta$-pullback of $D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}$, not the untwisted ordinary module. This is an ungraded convention dictionary. The pullback can move blocks: on the multiplicative Jucys–Murphy elements $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$, so charge-zero residue content is sent from $\alpha$ to $-\alpha$. Thus the ordinary module before pullback has the conjugate content; no claim identifies it untwisted inside the same block. At $\xi=1$ the separate specialization theorem [[cor-dj-bridge-specialization-and-composition-multiplicity-dictionary]] identifies $\theta$ with sign tensoring over every field; $\xi=1$ remains outside the present nondegenerate regime.

No choice principle is used.
item.strategy: Direct convention check. At level one $(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\delta_{i,0}$, so the cyclotomic polynomial of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]] is $\prod_i(X_1-\xi^i)^{(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)}=X_1-1$ and the KLR cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$; the finite-characteristic hypothesis $e\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ makes $\xi\ne1$ a primitive $e$-th root, and in sub-branch (CP) the hypothesis $p\nmid e$ is exactly what makes a primitive $e$-th root exist in $F$. The type-$A$ datum and the grading are batch-24 clauses; the transport statement is the graded block isomorphism of [[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]] with [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]. The Fock-side residues, the restricted labels and the empty component are batch-9/batch-23 clauses. The ordinary dictionary uses the actual universal module-and-form comparison [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]], not a rename of a cellular module. Its Laurent-unit form factor preserves radicals, including zero quotients, and gives $D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}\cong(D_{\rm M}^{\lambda})^{\theta}$; apply the involution again. Right-to-left conversion sends $h\cdot m=m h^*$, and commutation $\theta *=*\theta$ preserves the same pullback dictionary. On the finite level-one tower $X_j=\xi^{1-j}T_{j-1}\cdots T_1^2\cdots T_{j-1}$. Applying $\theta(T_r)=-\xi T_r^{-1}$ to this palindrome gives $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$: the $2j-2$ signs cancel and the scalar is $\xi^{j-1}$. Generalized eigenvalues $\xi^i$ therefore become $\xi^{-i}$, proving the content reflection. No raw Hecke automorphism is claimed to preserve a fixed transported grading. The $\xi=1$ specialization is the separate arbitrary-field polytabloid specialization corollary, not an inference from a prime-field-only statement. The parameter dictionary is the naming clause of [BK 2009 §1 and §4.2] and [Ariki 1996 §1]; it makes no substitution. No choice is used.

item.title: Residue-node reading orders and the conjugation dictionary
item.statement: For distinct addable/removable corners of one residue i (finite e≥2), smaller row implies strictly larger column and strictly larger content. Hence top-to-bottom=DECREASING content=decreasing column; bottom-to-top=increasing content. A same-residue row or column cannot repeat. Conjugation sends a top-to-bottom i-corner list of lambda to the bottom-to-top (increasing content) −i-corner list of lambda-prime, preserving signs. Thus its modular −+ cancellations, FIRST− good deletion and LAST+ cogood addition agree exactly with the QG INCREASING-content −+ rule on lambda-prime. Equivalently reverse the latter list and use decreasing-content +− cancellation, LAST− deletion and FIRST+ addition. Both versions select the same actual nodes. They apply to all partitions as signatures; the basic graph restriction is imposed separately.
item.strategy: Let rows r<s. Boundary inequalities give c_r≥c_s: check removable/removable, addable/addable, addable/removable directly from weak row lengths; for removable/addable, the upper removable drop and lower addability give the same weak inequality. Equality is possible for mixed types, so the native general 'impossible' assertion was false. If a removable upper corner and an addable lower corner share a column, their rows must be adjacent at that column's boundary, hence their contents differ1; the reverse mixed orientation cannot share a column. Equal-row mixed corners also differ1 in content. Same-residue e≥2 excludes these exceptions. Strict columns and r<s imply strictly DECREASING content. Conjugating exchanges rows/columns and negates content, yielding the stated order reversal. Stack reduction of −+ is uniquely determined: scan with a minus stack, cancel each plus with the last unmatched minus; reversing the word yields +− with first/last extrema reversed. Therefore the surviving-node bijection and selected-node identities are exact, not only an abstract isomorphism. This is the full elementary proof supplementing Fayers §4, whose text records the conventions but omits proofs.

item.title: The graded Specht module by homogeneous standard tableaux
item.statement:
Work in the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]. Fix a partition $\mu$, put $d=|\mu|$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let $K(\mu)$ be the $F$-span of the Murphy elements $m_{S,T}$ of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] with $S,T$ standard tableaux of a multipartition strictly dominating $\mu$; by [[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]] $K(\mu)$ is a two-sided ideal of $H^\Lambda_d$ and $z_\mu:=m_{t^\mu t^\mu}+K(\mu)$ is defined. Define the (level-one) **cell/Specht module** $$S(\mu):=H^\Lambda_d\,z_\mu\subseteq H^\Lambda_d/K(\mu),$$ a LEFT $H^\Lambda_d$-module lying in the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$ fix a reduced decomposition $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ of the associated permutation and put $z_T:=T_{w_T}z_\mu$, $v_T:=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ in the Khovanov-Lauda presentation of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]]. For a removable $i$-node $A$ of a partition $\lambda$ define $d_A(\lambda):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}$ (equivalently in the level-one symmetric residue convention of the regime) and define the **degree** of a standard tableau inductively by $\deg(\varnothing):=0$ and, for $d>0$, $\deg(T):=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)$ where $A$ is the node of $T$ containing $d$.

The definition asserts, and proves below in [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]], that $\{v_T:T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)\}$ is a homogeneous $F$-basis of $S(\mu)$ making it a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module whose $q$-character is $\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_T q^{\deg T}i_T$; forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded cell module. **Convention.** This is the LEFT Murphy cell module, obtained from the right cellular datum by $h\cdot m=m h^*$. Forgetting its grading, [[thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual]] identifies it with the star-contragredient dual of the same-shape independently defined ordinary Dipper–James Specht module $P(\mu)$. Separately, [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]] gives $S(\mu)\cong P(\mu')^{\theta}$ after the same left-module conversion. These are two proved module comparisons, not the identification of an untwisted conjugate module. The sign pullback may change ordinary residue content from $-\alpha$ to $\alpha$; these ungraded comparisons do not assert homogeneity of the ordinary form or of a raw Hecke sign automorphism in the fixed transported grading. The labelling of simples by $e$-restricted or $e$-regular partitions is NOT asserted here; it is determined by the head-classification theorem later on this page.

No choice is used in the definition.
item.strategy: This is a definition with its construction; the asserted basis, homogeneity and module structure are discharged by [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]], and the ideal/cellular facts by [[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]]. The degree recursion is the source's (4.33); the vectors $v_T$ depend a priori on the chosen reduced decompositions, and the theorem proves the resulting grading is well defined. The same-shape ordinary duality is established by the perfect star-balanced cross-pairing of [[thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual]], which does not require a nondegenerate self-form. The separate conjugate comparison is the explicit universal signed isomorphism of [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]. Convert both right modules through star; because theta commutes with star, finite duality and sign pullback keep their stated positions. No unsupported historical source20 convention is used. No choice. Use the LEFT-handed Murphy basis: if the supplied cellular datum is right-handed, apply its anti-involution to every basis identity. Then H z_mu is a left cyclic cell module, z_T=T_w z_mu and v_T=psi_w z_mu are left actions, consistent with the left KLR modules and right-append corner functors used throughout. No identification of a right module with a left module without this conversion is made.

item.title: The integral form of the cyclotomic Hecke-KLR block
item.statement: Let $K$ be a characteristic-zero field in branch (C0) of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]] and fix, for each residue content $\alpha$, the Khovanov-Lauda generators $\{e(i)\}$, $\{y_r\}$, $\{\psi_r\}$ of the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], i.e. the $\rho_\alpha$-images of the KLR generators ([[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]], [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]]), in a fixed admissible local normalising series. Define $$H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z):=\bigl\langle e(i),\ y_r,\ \psi_r\ \bigr\rangle_{\mathbb Z}\subseteq H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$$ to be the $\mathbb Z$-subring generated by them. It is the $\mathbb Z$-span of the same finite normal forms (in the Khovanov-Lauda generators) that span $H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$ over $K$, hence a free $\mathbb Z$-module and a lattice; the generator degrees give it a grading, and the base-change maps $$K\otimes_{\mathbb Z}H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_\alpha(K),\qquad F\otimes_{\mathbb Z}H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_\alpha(F)$$ sending $1\otimes e(i)\mapsto e(i)$, $1\otimes y_r\mapsto y_r$, $1\otimes\psi_r\mapsto\psi_r$ are isomorphisms of graded algebras for every field $F$ of sub-branch (CP) with a primitive $e$-th root of unity, the second being the reduction modulo $p$. The direct sums over $\alpha$ give the integral form of the tower. No choice is used.
item.strategy: Use the exact integer type-A KLR presentation with generator images in each characteristic-zero sector. Integer PBW straightening spans its image by ordered dot monomials times crossing words and word idempotents. Dot nilpotence in the finite characteristic-zero standard cyclotomic quotient bounds every position; finitely many words give finitely many nonzero spanning monomials. Their Z-span is closed under integer straightening and is torsion-free inside the characteristic-zero algebra. First descend to Q: the map from the Q KLR presentation to the generator image becomes the actual BK isomorphism after extending to K; faithful field extension makes it an isomorphism already over Q. Thus the integer image is a full finite lattice in this Q-algebra, of rank equal to dim_K H_alpha(K), and K tensor this lattice is H_alpha(K). For EVERY content alpha at fixed rank the reduced named generators satisfy the integer relations and generate F tensor the lattice, giving a SURJECTION H_alpha(F) -> F tensor H_alpha(Z) via the actual field BK presentation. Consequently dim_F H_alpha(F) >= dim_K H_alpha(K) for every alpha, including zero sectors. Sum over all finitely many rank-d contents: both total dimensions equal ell^d d! by the late field basis theorem. All individual nonnegative differences therefore vanish, proving every surjection is an isomorphism. Rankzero gives the singleton unit lattice; the levelzero positive-rank quotient is zero. Homogeneity of generators and relations supplies the integer grading. This is the complete applicable BK2008 Theorems6.1/6.4 proof route, without inferring an individual block dimension directly from total dimension alone. No choice.

item.title: Degree and codegree of standard tableaux
item.strategy: Separate below and above counts. Removing the removable i-node A changes the total addable-minus-removable count by the Cartan column, and A becomes an addable node in mu^A. Splitting all remaining i-nodes into strictly above and strictly below A gives d_A(mu)+d^A(mu^A)=d_i(mu)+1. Induction from the empty diagram and the same local boundary changes gives d_i(mu)=(Lambda0-alpha,alpha_i). Expanding defect(alpha)-defect(alpha-alpha_i) using (alpha_i,alpha_i)=2 gives d_i(mu)+1. Induct on the number of nodes in the degree/codegree recursion to obtain their sum equal to defect. For a horizontal terminal brick, codegree counts strictly ABOVE it: the first row has no such nodes; an e-brick contains every residue once and above boundary addable/removable contributions cancel. This proves both brick clauses. Check e2 shape(2): below degree1, above codegree0, defect1; shape(1,1): degree0, above codegree1, defect1. These checks illustrate, not replace, the boundary count proof. No choice.
